stories.title: 3 Ukrainian soldiers arrested in Lucknow over terror conspiracy:Militants trained in Myanmar, drone attack plans exposed
stories.summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested three former Ukrainian soldiers from Lucknow. The trio had been training terrorists in Myanmar and were allegedly conspiring against India. They are also believed to have links with an international drone-terror network. Additionally, NIA arrested four more suspects connected to this network at Delhi Airport. According to NIA sources, the three Ukrainian nationals—Petro Hurba (36), Taras Slyvyak (37), and Ivan Sukmanovsky (34)—were arrested from Lucknow Airport on March 13. The accused, experts in drone technology, were planning to spread terror in India and had been working from Myanmar to strengthen their terrorist network. Traveled from UAE to India, then Myanmar Investigations revealed that the trio arrived in India from the United Arab Emirates on December 18, 2025. From here, they travelled via Mizoram to Chin State in Myanmar, where they established contacts with terrorist organisations. The network was reportedly involved in transporting large consignments of drones from Europe to Myanmar. These drones were intended to be used by “Ethnic Armed Groups” (EAGs), which would then supply weapons, technology, and training to banned organisations operating in India. The agency said this activity posed a serious threat to India’s national security. Accused were planning to flee to Kuala Lumpur After reaching Lucknow, the three Ukrainians had booked a room at a hotel near the airport. Hotel staff asked them for identification and a C-form, raising suspicion about their presence. Their details were shared with investigative agencies and embassies. Following preliminary checks, authorities issued an alert regarding their activities, which eventually reached the immigration department. Their movements were closely monitored, and once confirmed, preparations were made to apprehend them at the airport. Plan was to stay in Lucknow for one day Investigations indicate that the trio had travelled from Guwahati to Lucknow with plans to stay for only a single day. They had pre-booked tickets to Kuala Lumpur. However, based on the intelligence received, immigration authorities detained them upon arrival. Their travel patterns and activities appeared suspicious during questioning, leading to their arrest. The NIA has registered a case against the three under Section 18 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). They are accused of conspiring against India’s security and promoting terrorist activities. The agency is currently interrogating them to trace the wider network. American citizen also arrested from Kolkata In a related operation, NIA also arrested an American citizen, Matthew Aaron Van Dyke, from Kolkata Airport. According to the agency, Van Dyke was actively involved in supplying weapons and providing training to insurgents in Myanmar. Four other Ukrainian nationals, arrested at Delhi Airport, also played key roles in the network.

stories.title: Rajbhar says Panchayat elections will happen by July 12:OBC Commission forms in next cabinet, no seat disputes
stories.summary: 'Panchayat elections in UP will be completed by July 12. The OBC Commission will be formed by the next cabinet meeting. There will be no problems anywhere.' In an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Rajbhar added that the NDA will also win the 2027 assembly elections. “Discontent among voters will not be a factor. Avimukteshwaranand is not recognised as a Shankaracharya by Yogi Ji,” he noted. On the 2027 assembly polls, Rajbhar said, “The Chief Minister will be from the BJP. Allies like us will get MLA and ministerial positions. Therefore, there will be no dispute over seat allocation.” Regarding the controversy over the ‘Pandit’ option in the UP Sub-Inspector recruitment exam, Rajbhar openly said it was incorrect to link the term to caste. “Pandit means scholar. The controversy is misplaced,” he added. Meanwhile, Amit Kumar Singh, Director of the Panchayati Raj Department, stated that the directorate has sent a proposal to the government for the formation of the OBC Commission. The reservation of seats in panchayats will be based on the commission’s report, which is essential for conducting elections. Read the exact conversation with OP Rajbhar... Question- Has the High Court asked UP government to conduct panchayat elections on time? Rajbhar- Yes, the order will be followed. The terms of office for Pradhan, Zila Panchayat members, Block Pramukh, and Zila Panchayat chairpersons are all different. Question- Everyone's term is not beyond July 12? Will elections be held by then? Rajbhar- Yes, elections will definitely be held by July 12 Question- Was the Panchayat election announced in March 2025? Rajbhar- The State Election Commission and government were ready. Now, the court has given its directive. Question- You haven't even formed the OBC Commission yet, it will take at least 3 months? Rajbhar- Wait until the next cabinet meeting, it will be formed. Look, the election has to be held based on 2011. Therefore, it should not take 3 months. The election has to be held on the old system only. It has to be according to the reservation cycle. What calculations will the Backward Classes Commission make? Therefore, we will get the elections done, there is no problem. Question- Less than 1 year is left for assembly elections. What are the preparations? Rajbhar- If we talk about just Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, recently 26 thousand people gathered in Varanasi. 15 thousand people gathered in Chandauli. Lakhs of people gathered in Azamgarh. Today there was a program in Kasganj, but after falling ill, I sent Arvind. You understand, our preparation is complete. NDA alliance is going to win with a huge majority in the 2027 elections. Question- BJP has 5 allied parties. There are 403 assembly seats, what will be the distribution? Rajbhar- There is no problem. In the NDA alliance, BJP will have the Chief Minister. We people just need to become ministers and MLAs. Then there's no dispute left. Other allied parties also have no issues. Question- Will the incident of pulling Shankaracharya's Batuk's hair and UGC have any effect on elections? Rajbhar- Come with us to the village, ask if those people even know Shankaracharya? They will say who is Shankaracharya? He is a SP leader. He should promote Hinduism. Isn't this what Shankaracharya means? Or is it about abusing the Prime Minister-Chief Minister? Talking about confronting the Prime Minister. The Shankaracharya who has SP people as courtiers, our Chief Minister says he is not even a Shankaracharya. Question- In a Daroga recruitment exam question, the option 'Pandit' was given, what would you say? Rajbhar- The world died reading books, but no one became a scholar. The word Pandit is meant to signify a learned person. It's a different matter if it's linked to caste. Because, the caste is Brahmin. Moreover, those who make the exam papers should also think that we should not write any such word that could cause controversy. Question- Is there a gas shortage in UP? Rajbhar- I am asking you - don't you have a cylinder at your home? Similarly, everyone who talks about shortage has one cylinder each at their homes. What happens is, when rumors spread, people think they should stock up or there will be problems later. The rule is that gas will be delivered to your home on the third day after online booking. If not, you can go to the agency and get it. Question- Then why are such crowds visible outside gas agencies? Rajbhar- Look, UP has a population of 25 crores. Opposition people are spreading rumors wherever they can reach. There are also people who haven't even done online booking. Still, they are reaching agencies with cylinders. The agencies are ready to give cylinders, but you need to make a booking first. There is no shortage anywhere. Question- Today Yogi government has completed 9 years. What would you like to say? Rajbhar- You see, no curfew no riots, entire Uttar Pradesh is healthy. Secondly - whether it's roads, rail or air connectivity, everything has improved significantly compared to before. Today 7 expressways are operational. Single roads have been developed into four lanes. Earlier the ration of the poor was being looted. Today subsidies are reaching directly from government accounts to common people's accounts. 9 years ago, the SP government used to give disabled people an allowance of 300 rupees. BJP is giving everyone 1000 rupees. There is no discrimination. CM Yogi has said that girls going for higher education will be given scooters. We will give bicycles in 10th-12th. This is being done to promote education. Now there is rule of law. If anyone commits a crime, they are sent to jail within 24 hours. The public itself feels that this law and order is better than SP's rule. Go and see in the slums of the poor, they are now getting houses. You see, when the Prime Minister talked about toilets from the Red Fort, the opposition said that the Prime Minister should not have talked about toilets. But now see, 90% people are using toilets. The atmosphere has changed in UP's Yogi government. The opposition sees nothing through their lens. They should remove those glasses and look. They also travel from Ballia to Ghazipur but say things haven't improved. The opposition just talks like this. Railway stations have been built, but they say something is lacking. Look at how it was 10 years ago too. Now there's no dirt at stations, no rats jumping around. The opposition doesn't see any of this. The government's intention is that just as Mahatma Gandhi's dream of independence was fulfilled, now the dream of cleanliness should also be fulfilled. Understand that we are moving towards a better direction.

stories.title: UP encounter kills ₹1 lakh bounty cattle smuggler Shehzad:2 policemen injured, DIG praises their bravery
stories.summary: In Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh, a police encounter with criminals led to the death of 40-year-old history-sheeter Shehzad, who carried a reward of ₹1 lakh. According to police, he was injured during the encounter and was immediately taken into custody, but later died during treatment at the hospital. Shehzad was known for professionally killing cattle. Two policemen were also injured in the shootout. The encounter took place on Tuesday around 3 pm in Sherpur village under Mirzapur police station limits. Police teams from Mirzapur and Fatehpur stations were conducting a checking drive to locate wanted criminals. During the operation, the police received information that the professional cattle killer Shehzad was present in the area. The team moved to surround him, instructing him to surrender. However, seeing himself trapped, Shehzad opened fire on the police. Two police personnel also injured Two policemen, Sumendra and Kuldeep, were injured by gunfire during the exchange. Police returned fire, hitting Shehzad. He fell to the ground and was immediately taken to the district hospital for treatment, where he later succumbed to his injuries. The two injured policemen are undergoing treatment at the hospital. DIG Abhishek Singh visited them and praised their bravery, placing a hand on one officer’s shoulder. See 3 photos... 44 cases were registered against the criminal Shehzad had 44 cases registered against him, including charges of cattle slaughter and gangster activities. He was a resident of Gandevda village in Fatehpur and had been on the run for a long time. A reward of ₹1 lakh had been announced for his capture. According to police, Shehzad was a cunning and professional criminal involved in several offences. Continuous efforts had been made to apprehend him. After the encounter, security in the area was increased, and an investigation into the case is ongoing. His criminal record included serious offences such as cattle slaughter and gangster activities across multiple police stations in Saharanpur.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Akhilesh slams youths' arrests over Ganga iftar party; ‘Shaadi Modi se.....’ Kharge mocks ex-PM Gowda more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Kharge takes dig at former PM Deve Gowda says, ‘Mohabbat humare saath, shaadi Modi se’ Kharge takes dig at former PM Deve Gowda Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday addressed the Rajya Sabha during a farewell for 59 retiring members, acknowledging their contributions to parliamentary functioning. He highlighted senior leaders like HD Deve Gowda, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Sharad Pawar, noting that they have spent more than half their lives in Parliament. 2. ‘Don’t let my son suffer anymore’: Mother of euthanasia patient breaks down; prays beside him in hospital Harish Rana, 31, from Ghaziabad, has been in a coma for 13 years following a fall from a hostel in 2013. The Supreme Court granted his parents permission for euthanasia. At AIIMS Delhi, his oxygen and feeding tube support have been withdrawn, and his organs are being tested for donation. Family members, supported by Brahma Kumaris, remain at his side, praying and coping with the prolonged suffering of seeing him bedridden and unresponsive. 3. Akhilesh says, 'Why can't Iftar be held on Ganga?': Says, youths in Varanasi faced action as they may not have bribed officials Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav criticised the arrest of 14 youths for holding an iftar on a Varanasi Ganga boat, calling it divisive. He also highlighted selective enforcement, LPG shortages, road mismanagement, and law-and-order concerns, while questioning why officials faced no action and BJP may lose polls. 4. BJP to contest 89 of 126 seats in Assam; AAP's second list in Kerala includes 21 names The BJP is expected to release its first list of candidates for the Assam Assembly elections today. The party will contest 89 seats. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) will contest 26 seats, the Bodoland People's Front (BPF) 11, and the BJP the remaining. "We have a parliamentary board meeting on Wednesday. The list will be announced late tonight or the next morning," he said. 5. No permanent DGP in UP for 4 years: SC scrutiny, policy flaws and timing shape Rajeev Krishna’s chances After the Supreme Court’s strict stance, movement has picked up on appointing a permanent DGP in Uttar Pradesh, vacant for nearly four years. The state’s own rules remain unimplemented due to legal concerns and UPSC role, while acting DGP Rajeev Krishna may become eligible after June. 6. SP’s PDA narrative to be countered by BJP’s ‘Triple-S’ formula: RSS to provide feedback; CM Yogi held six meetings BJP is working to counter SP’s PDA pitch with a ‘Triple-S’ strategy—organisation, government and RSS—after coordination gaps hurt its 2024 poll performance. Meetings flagged Brahmin discontent, factionalism and worker grievances. Focus now on unity, outreach and stronger coordination ahead of the 2027 UP elections. 7. Trump says, 'Iran world’s top state sponsor of terror': Israeli attack kills Iran’s intelligence minister Today marks the 19th day of the US-Israel war on Iran. Indian oil tanker Jag Laadki, carrying 80,000 metric tonnes of crude oil, arrived at Mundra Port in Gujarat on Wednesday. 8. Lucknow passport office gets bomb threat: Police and VTS teams deployed in Gomtinagar; alert heightened A bomb threat at the Regional Passport Office in Gomtinagar triggered panic, prompting police and explosive detection teams to launch intensive searches. Entry was restricted, with checks on all people and vehicles. Security tightened across the area as officials began a probe to trace the source. 9. Constable shoots sister’s lover inside hospital in Aligarh: Murder linked to six-year love affair and family opposition A PAC constable allegedly shot dead his sister’s former lover inside a hospital on March 16. The victim, linked to a long-term relationship opposed by family, was killed amid ongoing tensions. Family claims prior threats were ignored; police have detained the accused’s father. 10. India sees a fall in LPG consumption amid Iran war; Petrol diesel sales increase LPG consumption across the country decreased by 17% in the first week of March. This occurred due to the war conditions in West Asia. According to data from 3 government companies IOCL, BPCL and HPCL (that boast of 90% market share), LPG consumption has decreased compared to the same period last year.

stories.title: Police claim explosives were being made at ex-SP MLA’s house:Blast blows off basement, 6 booked including both sons
stories.summary: Explosives were being manufactured at the house of former SP MLA Vijay Singh in Farrukhabad. Police have made this claim in their FIR. 6 people including 2 sons of the former MLA were injured in the blast. Cases have been registered against all of them. The explosion occurred on Tuesday evening in the former MLA's three-story house. The basement ceiling was blown off, and windows up to the third floor were shattered. Initially there were suspicions of a cylinder blast, but the former MLA's wife had denied this. When police arrived to investigate, no evidence of cylinder explosion was found. There was a smell of sulfur (gunpowder) inside the house. Police stated in their FIR that explosives were collected in the house. They were also being manufactured. The entire building has been sealed. Today, Wednesday, DIG Harish Chandra reached the spot. He said the family members are not cooperating in the police investigation. Vijay Singh is a strongman leader. He is known as 'Ustad' in the area. He is currently in Varanasi jail. He was sentenced to life imprisonment in 1997 for the murder of BJP leader Brahmadutt Dwivedi. Now read in detail... First read what the inspector reported... City Kotwali sub-inspector Imran Farid lodged the report. He said that he was checking vehicles at Sahabganj crossing when he saw an e-rickshaw carrying two injured and burnt persons heading towards Bharat Nursing Home. When he stopped the e-rickshaw and inquired, he found that the injured were the former MLA’s sons—Avinash alias Vicky and Abhishek alias Sikki. Police immediately reached the former MLA’s residence in Machharata locality. The injured told them that a massive explosion had occurred in the house, injuring five to six people, while some were still lying inside. A heavy crowd had gathered outside, and there was panic and chaos in the entire locality, with people shouting. The basement ceiling was torn off On entering through the main gate, police saw the floor broken, the basement roof blown off and all items inside scattered. In the debris, a man identified as Bhaiya Lal from Noorpur was found in a severely injured condition. Sub-inspector Imran, with the help of others, rescued him and sent him to hospital. During inquiry, it was found that apart from Vicky and Sikki, Eshu Chaurasia, Ramveer Yadav and Rashu Mishra were also injured and had been taken to hospital. When the officer looked into the damaged basement, a smell of explosive substances was coming from inside. Windows broken up to third floor Blood stains were seen on the walls of the house. Windows, doors, grills, roof and lintel up to the third floor were completely damaged. Locals said that around 7:30 pm, a loud explosion damaged the building. The situation at the spot clearly indicated that illegal explosive materials were being collected and something was being made, which led to the blast and put lives at risk. The incident created panic and stampede-like conditions. Denied cylinder explosion Former municipal chairperson Damayanti Singh, wife of the former MLA, said she was at home at the time of the incident. She had lit a lamp at the tulsi plant upstairs and came down, sitting near the kitchen in the courtyard while the children were downstairs. Suddenly, it felt like a storm had hit. Glass and curtains started falling from all sides. She could not understand what had happened. When she went downstairs, she saw her elder son Avinash bleeding heavily, while the younger son was also injured. She clearly stated that there was no cylinder blast in the house and the cause of the explosion is still unknown. Six people have been named The report names former MLA Vijay Singh's elder son Avinash alias Vicky, younger son Abhishek alias Sikky, Ishu Chaurasia from the same locality, Ramvir Yadav who lives near Farrukhabad railway station, Rashu Mishra resident of city's Mittukucha area, and Bhaiya Lal resident of Mau Darwaza. Which sections were applied, what could be the punishment? Bomb disposal team and ATS arrived A bomb disposal squad reached the former MLA’s house late Tuesday night for investigation and revisited again on Wednesday morning. An Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) team from Kanpur has also reached the spot for investigation. DIG Harish Chander spent about 20 minutes inside the house examining the situation. He said it would be premature to comment at this stage. He added that family members are not cooperating. The house has been sealed by police. DIG said - Explosion occurred inside the house DIG Harish Chandra said, The forensic team has been called again. The ATS team has come from Kanpur. They are also conducting the investigation. Samples have been taken for forensic examination. The entire house has been secured. He said all angles are being probed to determine how and under what circumstances the explosion occurred. It is confirmed that the blast happened inside the house. CCTV footage has also been obtained and an FIR has been registered. He added that those injured neither informed the police nor called the emergency helpline 112 and are still not cooperating. It has been learnt that both sons of the former MLA have referred themselves to Lucknow for treatment. Further action will be taken after the investigation report is received.

stories.title: Drugs peddled on Ahmedabad streets traced to UP hinterlands:Raid by Gujarat ATS unearths laboratory in Ambedkar Nagar district
stories.summary: What began as a tactical street-level drug bust in Ahmedabad’s Danilimda area, culminated in the exposure of a sophisticated, industrial-scale narcotics operation from Uttar Pradesh’s hinterlands by Gujarat ATS. On 1 March, ATS officials intercepted Shafaat Ahmed Farooqi with a mere 4.6 grams of Mephedrone (MD). However, in the world of high-stakes counter-narcotics, there are no ‘small’ seizures. The subsequent interrogation of Farooqi and his local suppliers, Sohil Mirza and Farhan Pathan, provided the thread that ATS officials needed to pull. The trail led directly from the urban pockets of Gujarat to the Ambedkar Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh, revealing a supply chain anchored by two primary manufacturers, Kapildev Sharma and Ramshankar, alias Pankaj. High-stakes raid in remote UP village Operating with a level of calculated secrecy reminiscent of a crime drama, the duo had established a functional MD laboratory within a nondescript tin shed on a remote poultry farm. The location was chosen for its isolation, but it could not hide from the 12-day continuous undercover surveillance maintained by an advance ATS team. In a coordinated strike with the Uttar Pradesh Police, ATS officials stormed the Ramnagar Karai facility, discovering a ‘running’ factory. The scale of the recovery was massive, including 6 kg of finished Mephedrone, 50 kg of liquid Mephedrone in process, and 88 kg of 2-bromo-4-methyl propiophenone (a newly controlled substance). Alongside, 200 kg of raw precursor chemicals and specialized laboratory equipment were also seized. Accused under police’s legal net In this case, ATS initially busted Shafaat, Sohil, and Farhan, all residents of Ahmedabad. Alongside the initial perpetrators in the drug syndicate, police have now nabbed Kapildev Sharma (31), and Ramshankar alias Pankaj (30), both residents of UP’s Beni Gadowpur district. All five accused now face stringent charges under Sections 8(c), 22(b), and 29 of the NDPS Act.

stories.title: Lucknow passport office gets bomb threat:Police and VTS teams deployed in Gomtinagar; alert heightened
stories.summary: The Regional Passport Office located in Gomtinagar, Lucknow, has received a bomb threat. As soon as the information was received, local police and the VTS (explosive detection team) reached the spot and began a thorough search of the entire campus. Security in the area has been stepped up. Vigilance has been increased in nearby areas as well. For now, entry and exit at the office have been restricted. Every person present and all belongings are being checked. See 3 pictures- Police and investigation team reached the spot After receiving the threat, Gomtinagar police and the VTS team immediately swung into action. The teams launched an intensive checking drive inside the passport office and in nearby areas. Following the incident, security arrangements across the area have been tightened. People entering and leaving the passport office are being thoroughly checked, and suspicious activities are being closely monitored. Investigation of threat source continues According to police officials, an investigation is underway to find out how the threat was issued and who is behind it. A technical team is also engaged in the probe. Officials said the situation is currently under control, but keeping in mind any possible threat, security agencies remain fully alert and are examining every aspect closely. News is being updated...

stories.title: SP’s PDA narrative to be countered by BJP’s ‘Triple-S’ formula:RSS to provide feedback; CM Yogi held six meetings
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is preparing to counter the Samajwadi Party’s PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) narrative with its own ‘Triple-S’ formula, Organisation, Government and Sangh. To strengthen this strategy and ensure better coordination, a series of meetings involving BJP leaders, government officials and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) were held across six cities between 28 February and 7 March 2026. Why were the coordination meetings held ? The meetings were prompted by concerns that weak coordination between the party organisation, government and RSS contributed to setbacks in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. To avoid a repeat in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, efforts are now underway to realign all three pillars. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat attended four of these meetings, underlining their importance. Key issues discussed Three major concerns dominated discussions- 5 outcomes from the meetings Five broad action points emerged- Discontent over UGC rules There is growing unease among upper-caste communities, particularly Brahmins, regarding reservation-related provisions under UGC regulations introduced in January 2026. In meetings held in Kanpur and Ghaziabad, this was identified as a significant political concern. The RSS advised caution, and leaders were instructed not to comment publicly on the issue. Shankaracharya controversy raises concerns The controversy surrounding the alleged insult of Swami Avimukteshwaranand during the Magh Mela was also discussed. Participants expressed concern that the incident could weaken the broader ‘Sanatan Unity’ narrative and impact the BJP’s Hindutva image. Worker discontent and organisational gaps Grassroots workers raised concerns about being ignored after elections, despite playing a key role during campaigns. They highlighted the lack of representation in boards, corporations and urban local bodies. In response, the government nominated 2,802 councillors in urban local bodies on 16 March, seen as an attempt to address these grievances. Factionalism within the party Rising tensions between MPs, MLAs and party workers were flagged as a serious issue. Several district-level disputes were discussed- The RSS expressed concern over such disputes, stressing the need for internal discipline. Gap between government and ground reality Sources indicated that bureaucratic filters often prevent accurate feedback from reaching the government. Officials may downplay public dissatisfaction, while coordination meetings allow direct interaction between RSS workers, BJP leaders and the Chief Minister. This platform enables the government to better understand ground-level issues, public sentiment and emerging political challenges. Lessons from the 2024 Elections Political observers note that these meetings are part of a broader strategic recalibration after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, where the BJP fell short of a majority by 32 seats, suffering setbacks in key states such as Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra. A statement by then BJP president JP Nadda, suggesting that the party no longer needed the RSS as before, is believed to have demotivated sections of the Sangh cadre. Subsequently, the BJP renewed its engagement with the RSS, contributing to electoral victories in states such as Haryana, Delhi, Maharashtra and Bihar. Strengthening booth-level and social outreach Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath sought detailed feedback from the RSS on booth-level organisation, social outreach and the messaging around Hindutva. With caste dynamics and social justice issues gaining traction again, the BJP is focusing on consolidating its core support base while countering the opposition alliance. Plans were also discussed to intensify engagement with students, teachers and social groups, particularly in the wake of controversies such as the UGC issue. Experts: Early Blueprint for 2027 Elections Senior journalist Anil Singh described these meetings as more than routine exercises, calling them an early blueprint for the 2027 elections. He noted that similar coordination efforts before the 2019 Lok Sabha and 2022 Assembly elections had yielded positive results. BHU professor TP Singh added that while the direct electoral impact of such meetings may not be immediately measurable, they play a crucial role in maintaining cadre morale and organisational efficiency. BJP moves early to address challenges The 2024 election results highlighted that electoral dynamics in Uttar Pradesh are becoming increasingly complex, influenced by local issues and shifting social equations. In response, the BJP is moving early to identify weaknesses, strengthen coordination with the RSS, and activate its organisational machinery — signalling a more structured and proactive approach ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

stories.title: Gorakhpur murder case cracked in 13 hours:2 held for killing BJP leader during morning walk over revenge motive
stories.summary: Police have solved the murder of BJP leader Rajkumar Chauhan, who was killed during his morning walk in Gorakhpur. According to SSP Dr Kaustubh, two dump truck drivers have been arrested for the crime. During interrogation, the accused revealed that two months ago, the leader’s nephew had assaulted them, and Chauhan had supported him. They alleged the nephew often misused his influence, prompting them to plan the murder in revenge. Murder planned in advance, accused lay in wait The accused said they were aware of Chauhan’s daily routine. On the day of the incident, they hid behind a tree and attacked him when he was alone. They first opened fire, but he managed to escape. As he tried to flee, they chased him and stabbed him to death. Police examined footage from eight CCTV cameras, which helped identify the suspects. They later confessed during questioning. The incident took place at around 5:30 AM on Tuesday in the Chiluatal area. Within 13 hours, the police cracked the case. During a press conference, DM Deepak Meena and the SSP said that the accused, Raj Chauhan alias Nirhua and Vipin Yadav, are residents of Bargadwa. They had an ongoing dispute with the victim’s nephew, Nitesh, for the past four months. A case has been registered against eight named individuals, seven of whom have been detained. Their role is under investigation. Chased, stabbed repeatedly; family demands justice Family members said Rajkumar Chauhan (38) had left home at around 5 AM for his usual morning walk. About 30 minutes later, they were informed of the attack. Eyewitnesses claimed that four assailants surrounded him about 500 metres from his home and attacked him with knives. Despite being stabbed, he tried to escape, but the attackers chased him, caught him about 100 metres away, and repeatedly stabbed him. He sustained 20–25 stab wounds to his head, chest and face. The attackers reportedly remained at the scene for some time to ensure he had died before fleeing. He was taken to BRD Medical College, where doctors declared him dead. On hearing the news, his wife Sushila fainted. His sister Mohini demanded strict action, saying, “We want justice. Who will now support the family?” She also demanded a government job for his niece. See 2 images related to the incident- Crowd's uproar, police removed them using batons After the incident, more than 500 people gathered and blocked the Gorakhpur-Sonauli road in protest. Forces from 10 police stations arrived and dispersed the crowd using batons. After the post-mortem, the body reached home around 5 PM, after which the family members stood firm on their demands. MP says, ‘Will expose those who try to save the killers in Rajya Sabha’ The family agreed after persuasion from Rajya Sabha member Dr. Radha Mohan Agrawal and Cabinet Minister Dara Singh Chauhan. Late at night, the cremation was performed at the ghat near Moharipur. Around 2000 people were present during this time. Dr. Agrawal said, “I have left Parliament to come here, whoever tries to save the accused of this murder, I will expose them in the Rajya Sabha.” BJP leader was seeking assembly ticket from BJP Rajkumar Chauhan was the only son of Jangi Chauhan from the Bargadwa area. He got married 18 years ago. He has 2 daughters - Sonam (17) and Priyanka (13), while his son Yuvraj is 12 years old. He has 4 sisters who are all married. It is being reported that Rajkumar, who belongs to the OBC community, was preparing to contest the 2027 assembly elections from Basti. He was seeking a ticket from BJP. Rajkumar served as councillor representative from 2018 to 2023. He had made his driver Virendra Chauhan's wife Rinki Devi a councillor. Later, Rinki Devi gave support to BJP. A year ago, Rajkumar had also gone to jail in an assault case. Rajkumar had posted on Facebook 18 hours ago Rajkumar Chauhan has 40K followers on Facebook, while he followed 25 people. He made his last post on March 16 at 11:05 AM. In it he wrote, “I have the skill to walk alone, I keep both heart and liver strong.” In another post, he had written for his father, “Father is a banyan tree, who keeps the entire family safe in his shade.” Posted a reel with Rajya Sabha MP 5 days ago Rajkumar had posted a reel with Rajya Sabha MP Radhamohan Agarwal 5 days ago. In the post, he wrote, “Our dear Guruji, Rajya Sabha MP”. Before this, on March 9, he had also posted a reel with Cabinet Minister Dara Singh Chauhan.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'Why can't Iftar be held on Ganga?':Says, youths in Varanasi faced action as they may not have bribed officials
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has criticised the arrest of 14 Muslim youths who allegedly organised an iftar gathering on a boat in the Ganga in Varanasi. Questioning the police action, he asked, ‘Can one not break their fast on the Ganga? All this is being done to create division among people’. Speaking at an iftar event in Lucknow, Yadav also took a swipe at the administration. He remarked that officials such as the District Magistrate (DM), Superintendent of Police (SP), and Station House Officer (SHO) should have been offered iftar as well. In a controversial comment, he added that police behaviour often depends on informal inducements, suggesting that action may have been taken because “their palms were not warmed”. Questions over action against luxury river cruise Yadav further criticised the administration for what he described as selective enforcement. He pointed to the operation of a luxury “five-star” vessel on the Ganga, alleging that it served expensive liquor and discharged toilet waste into the river. He questioned what action had been taken against the operator of that vessel, adding that untreated waste from pits dug earlier had also reached the Ganga without accountability. Remarks on LPG crisis and infrastructure issues The Samajwadi Party leader also raised concerns about a growing LPG shortage, warning that businesses could face significant losses if the situation persists. He insisted that his party was not spreading rumours but sharing factual information, adding that the public is aware of who spreads misinformation. Referring to potholes on a Green Corridor project, Yadav alleged mismanagement, remarking sarcastically that despite heavy expenditure, roads had deteriorated, suggesting negligence or poor execution. Political comments on elections and law and order Yadav commented on administrative practices during elections, stating that in Uttar Pradesh, senior officials such as the Director General of Police (DGP), Home Secretary, Chief Secretary, District Magistrates, and Commissioners are typically not removed during polls. Despite this, he expressed confidence that the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) would face electoral defeat. Drawing comparisons with West Bengal, he said that although officials had been changed there, the public was likely to support Mamata Banerjee again. He also alleged discrimination in West Bengal under the pretext of SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls), claiming that voters were harassed and that electoral rolls remained incomplete. Law and order concerns raised Yadav highlighted law and order issues in Gorakhpur, alleging frequent incidents of violence. He claimed that whenever the Chief Minister visits the city, law enforcement appears to weaken, allowing criminal incidents to occur. What happened in the Varanasi Iftar case? The controversy stems from an iftar gathering held on a boat in the middle of the Ganga in Varanasi earlier this week. During the event, participants were served fruits, dry fruits, and, reportedly, chicken biryani. A video of the gathering was recorded and shared on social media, where it quickly went viral. The mention of non-vegetarian food triggered objections from BJP leaders and some Hindu organisations. Complaint and police action Rajat Jaiswal, city president of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), lodged a complaint at Kotwali police station. Acting swiftly, the police registered a First Information Report (FIR) and arrested 14 individuals within eight hours. Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh confirmed that two teams were formed to conduct raids and apprehend those involved. Further investigation is ongoing. stories.title: ‘Don’t let my son suffer anymore’:Mother of euthanasia patient breaks down; prays beside him in hospital
stories.summary: “Oh God, please do not let my son suffer any longer. Do not put him through so much pain that we cannot even bear to see him. For 13 years, we have prayed with folded hands. We made countless wishes, but Harish could never speak. Even if his body leaves us, he will always live within us. Our family will carry this pain for the rest of our lives.” These are the words of Nirmala Devi, mother of Harish Rana from Ghaziabad, who has received permission for euthanasia from the Supreme Court. A woman from the neighbourhood, who met her at the hospital, shared these details with a Dainik Bhaskar reporter on condition of anonymity. She said that Harish’s mother is praying constantly for her son, along with his father, Ashok Rana. According to sources, AIIMS Delhi has allowed the parents to stay in a room adjacent to the palliative care ward where Harish is being kept. His oxygen support has been withdrawn. On Tuesday, doctors also stopped administering water through a feeding tube. Medical experts say that after withdrawal of food and water, a person may survive for one to two weeks. Harish Rana, now 31, has been in a coma (brain-dead condition) for the past 13 years. On 11 March, the Supreme Court granted permission for euthanasia following a petition filed by his parents. On 14 March, he was shifted from his home in Raj Empire Society, Rajnagar, Ghaziabad, to AIIMS Delhi. Harish's kidneys and liver being tested for organ donation On Tuesday, parents expressed their wish for Harish's organ donation. After this, AIIMS medical team is examining Harish's organs. The team is checking which organs of Harish's body are suitable for transplantation. If Harish Rana's organs like liver, lungs, kidneys, heart, pancreas and intestines are found functional, they can be donated. Cornea and heart valves are also being examined. According to doctors, the test report will be completed in one or two days. Video emerged from before taking him to AIIMS from home When Harish was being taken from home to AIIMS on March 14, Sister Lovely from Brahma Kumari Ashram had visited his house that day. She had applied a sandalwood tilak on Harish's forehead. While stroking his head, she had said - 'Now go, forgiving everyone and asking forgiveness from everyone... okay...' During this time, the eyes of all members of Harish's family were filled with tears. Father Ashok had apologized to all family members. He said that he had to take this step even though he didn't want to. Harish's family has been associated with Brahma Kumaris for about 18 years. About 6 years ago, the entire family shifted to Ghaziabad. Before this, Harish Rana's father Ashok Rana lived in Delhi for 13 years. Brahma Kumari Lovely had said that 2-3 years ago, the family told about Harish's pain. Harish's brother, sister, mother and father kept crying all the time. When they could no longer bear to see Harish's pain, they came to the Brahma Kumaris center and expressed the idea of euthanasia. They said that enough is enough. Now they cannot see their son in so much pain. Please just give him liberation. 'Supreme Court did a great favor to Harish by giving permission' The Rana family said that the High Court had rejected our petition. However, the Supreme Court did a great favor to Harish by giving permission. We couldn't bear to see his suffering. The helplessness is that he cannot even tell where he is in pain. We don't even want to call this passive euthanasia. We are leaving him in God's lap. When Harish passes away, we will bring him home with great respect and give him a final farewell. Silence prevails in family and society There has been silence in the family since Harish was shifted to Delhi AIIMS. Father is also not meeting anyone. Society people say that he is emotional. Sister and mother cried even after returning from Delhi AIIMS. Mother Nirmala had said that the one she gave birth to, raised and nurtured. Then cared for him again like an innocent child. The only sorrow was that he did not even share his pain. When I would massage him morning and evening, I would tell him stories about what happened at home that day. Many times I would wait for hours just to see him blink once. So that I could feel that he had heard everything. Sometimes when he would yawn, sometimes sneeze, or when the skin around his eyes would twitch, we would feel relieved that he was alive. Learn how Harish ended up in this condition... Born in Delhi, Harish Rana was pursuing BTech from Punjab University in Chandigarh. In 2013, during his final semester studies, he fell from the fourth floor of the hostel. After the accident, his entire body became paralyzed and he went into a coma. Since then, he has been unable to speak or feel anything. Doctors have diagnosed Harish with a serious condition called quadriplegia. In this condition, the patient survives with the help of a feeding tube and ventilator. According to doctors, the chances of recovery in this condition are almost nil. Due to being bedridden continuously for the past 13 years, Harish has also developed bedsores (deep wounds) on his body. His condition has been deteriorating further with time. For the family, seeing him in this state has become mentally very difficult.

stories.title: Constable shoots sister’s lover inside hospital in Aligarh:Murder linked to six-year love affair and family opposition
stories.summary: A shocking case of murder has come to light from Aligarh, where a constable allegedly shot dead his sister’s lover inside a hospital. The incident, which took place on March 16, has revealed a complex backstory of a long-running love affair, family opposition and escalating tensions. Love story that began in Mathura The deceased, Vedpal (32), was a resident of Ahraula and had completed his BA-LLB from AMU. Around six years ago, he was working in a private company in Mathura, where he met a woman employed at the same firm. Their friendship gradually turned into a relationship, and for nearly five years, the two remained in love, promising to marry each other. Vedpal came from a farming family, while the woman’s family was financially strong and had links with the police department. Dainik Bhaskar's special report reveals how a story that began with love ended in death... Family opposition blocks marriage When the woman’s family learned about the relationship, they opposed it due to differences in social and financial status. Despite this, Vedpal approached the family with a marriage proposal, assuring them he would keep their daughter happy. Initially, the woman supported him, but later backed out after pressure from her father and brothers. She eventually stopped communicating with him. Engagement disrupted, tensions escalate Following this, the woman’s family arranged her marriage elsewhere. On February 2, 2026, Vedpal reached her engagement ceremony and created a scene, leading to the marriage being called off. He was allegedly beaten up by the woman’s family and handed over to the police, after which he spent 14 days in jail. The family then quickly got the woman married to someone else on February 3. Harassment complaints after release After his release from jail, Vedpal allegedly continued to harass the woman and her husband through phone calls. He is also accused of sending objectionable photos of the woman to her husband. On March 10, the woman filed a complaint against him on the women’s helpline (1090). Shot dead on hospital bed On March 16, Vedpal was admitted to Renuka Hospital in the Quarsi area of Aligarh for hand surgery. According to his family, the woman’s relatives had been searching for him and were tipped off about his presence at the hospital. Around 9:40 PM, the woman’s cousin Bhupendra Chaudhary, a PAC constable, along with his brother Jitendra, allegedly entered the hospital ward. After locating Vedpal, they shot him in the head while he was lying on the bed. He was rushed to JN Medical College, where he died during treatment on March 17. Family alleges prior warning ignored Vedpal’s father, Dharmveer Singh, claimed that he had already alerted authorities on March 10, submitting a written complaint to officials in Mathura and Aligarh. He alleged that he had shared audio recordings of threats received between January 23 and March 10, warning of possible harm to his son. However, no preventive action was taken. Allegations and unanswered questions At the time of the attack, Vedpal’s brother Sonpal was on a hunger strike at a university, demanding student union elections. He alleged that Vedpal was first abducted, then assaulted, and ultimately killed. The incident has raised serious questions about law and order, as well as the failure to act on prior warnings.

stories.title: No permanent DGP in UP for 4 years:SC scrutiny, policy flaws and timing shape Rajeev Krishna’s chances
stories.summary: After the Supreme Court’s strict stance on appointing a permanent Director General of Police (DGP), activity has intensified in Uttar Pradesh. The state has been without a permanent DGP for nearly four years. Although the UP government framed rules for the appointment, they have not been implemented so far, raising questions over delays and legal hurdles. Read in this Dainik Bhaskar report... Why is UP government unable to implement its own rules? The Uttar Pradesh government approved the Director General of Police, Uttar Pradesh Selection and Appointment Rules, 2024 in September 2024. However, according to senior journalist Rajendra Kumar, the rules contained several complications and could have been challenged in court. To avoid legal trouble, the government has effectively shelved its own framework. Another key issue is the role of the UPSC, an autonomous body. The state government cannot direct it. Since the DGP is an IPS (All India Service) officer, any deviation is also seen as potential interference in the Centre’s domain. Key provisions of the UP DGP appointment rules Selection Committee: A 6-member panel headed by a retired High Court judge, including the Chief Secretary, UPSC representative, UPPSC Chairman (or nominee), Additional Chief Secretary (Home), and a former DGP Tenure: Minimum fixed tenure of 2 years Eligibility: Officer must have at least 6 months of service left before retirement Procedure: No need to send a panel to UPSC; the state can appoint the DGP based on the committee’s recommendation Removal: DGP can be removed under state rules for dereliction of duty or other reasons The state government argued that this process aligns with the Supreme Court’s 2006 Prakash Singh judgment. Seniority list: Who is ahead of Rajeev Krishna? In the IPS seniority list, Renuka Mishra is at the top. Two other officers senior to acting DGP Rajeev Krishna are: Alok Sharma (1991 batch) Piyush Anand (1991 batch) Alok Sharma is set to retire in June, which will significantly impact the seniority dynamics. When can Rajeev Krishna become permanent DGP? Rajeev Krishna was appointed acting DGP in June 2025, superseding around seven senior officers. Under UPSC norms, a panel of the three senior-most officers is sent to the state, and the DGP is selected from that list. At present, Rajeev Krishna is fourth in seniority. After Alok Sharma’s retirement in June, he will move up to third position, making him eligible for consideration under UPSC rules. Sources indicate that the two officers senior to him—Renuka Mishra and Piyush Anand—are not seen as the state leadership’s preferred choices. Mishra has not been assigned a posting since February 2024 and has applied for voluntary retirement, which is yet to be approved. No permanent DGP in UP for 4 years Mukul Goyal was the last permanent DGP of Uttar Pradesh. He was removed on May 11, 2022. Since then, the state has seen a series of acting DGPs: Devendra Singh Chauhan (till March 2023) Rajkumar Vishwakarma Vijay Kumar Prashant Kumar Rajeev Krishna (since June 2025) Supreme Court case and April 1 hearing On March 12, 2026, the Supreme Court issued contempt notices to six states—Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur, and Mizoram—for not following DGP appointment norms. The next hearing is scheduled for April 1, and attention is now on the Uttar Pradesh government’s stand in court. Experts believe the state may try to delay the process until June. By then, Rajeev Krishna would become eligible under UPSC norms, clearing the path for his appointment as permanent DGP.

stories.title: Harish Rana dies after SC permits mercy killing:Spent 13 years in coma; approval came just 13 days ago
stories.summary: Harish Rana took his last breath at Delhi AIIMS on Tuesday. PTI confirmed this citing sources. 31-year-old Harish had been in a coma for 13 years. The Supreme Court had granted permission for euthanasia on March 11. This is the first case in the country where someone has been given euthanasia. Harish was shifted to Delhi AIIMS on March 14. AIIMS administration removed Harish Rana's feeding tube on March 16. Harish was given passive euthanasia at AIIMS. This means that the external life support or treatment being given to keep a seriously ill patient alive is stopped or removed, so that the patient can die naturally. Supreme Court delivered the verdict on March 11 The Supreme Court had delivered its verdict on the euthanasia case on March 11. The court had granted permission for passive euthanasia to 31-year-old Harish Rana, who had been in a coma for 13 years. After the decision, mother Nirmala Devi had said that 'We made every possible effort for the son's treatment. Showed him to major hospitals and got treatment from many doctors, but hopes are almost gone. Now I just pray to God that he gets relief from this pain soon.' Had fallen from 4th floor of hostel, bedridden since then Born in Delhi, Harish Rana was pursuing BTech from Punjab University, Chandigarh. In 2013, he fell from the fourth floor of the hostel. Due to this, his entire body became paralyzed and he went into a coma. He can neither speak nor feel anything. Doctors diagnosed Harish with quadriplegia disease. In this condition, the patient is completely dependent on feeding tube and ventilator support. There is no possibility of recovery. Due to being bedridden for 13 years, Harish has developed bedsores, which are deep wounds on his body. His condition continues to deteriorate. This situation is very painful for Harish. For the family, seeing him like this has become mentally very difficult. The family has been financially broken due to years of expenses on ventilator, medicines, nursing and care. There are 2 types of euthanasia Passive Euthanasia: In this, the patient's treatment or life support such as ventilator, feeding tube, or medications are stopped so that death can occur naturally. Doctors don't perform any new procedures, they simply stop the treatment. The cause of death remains the illness. Active Euthanasia: In this, doctors use medicines or injections to cause death to the patient. This is illegal in India. If someone deliberately kills a patient by giving medicine, it is considered murder under BNS section or assistance to suicide. What is the law of euthanasia in the Constitution of India In 2005, an NGO called Common Cause filed a petition in the Supreme Court demanding the right to passive euthanasia. On March 9, 2018, a 5-judge bench led by CJI Deepak Mishra gave legal recognition to euthanasia. The Supreme Court had then said, If a patient has an incurable disease or is in a vegetative state, meaning alive only on life support system, their treatment can be stopped for natural death. This will not be considered euthanasia, but rather the right to die with dignity. This right is part of Article 21 of the Constitution, which includes the right to die with dignity along with the right to live with dignity. What are the rules regarding euthanasia In 2018, while validating passive euthanasia, the Supreme Court made 2 types of rules... 1. When the patient has already written a 'Living Will': When the patient has written a living will of their own accord while being mentally fit. This living will clearly states that if the patient's illness becomes incurable, meaning if they are beyond recovery, they should be removed from life support systems. The Supreme Court has also made some rules for this... Only a healthy person above 18 years of age can write a living will. The patient must have signed the living will in front of 2 witnesses. The documents must be verified by a Judicial Magistrate. Approval must be obtained from the treating doctor, hospital medical board, and an external medical board at the district level. After approval from both boards, life support systems like ventilator can be turned off. The family is informed about this entire process. In case of any dispute, an appeal can be made to the High Court. 2. When there is no living will: When a patient does not make a living will while conscious, their family or close ones can make this decision. However, this is not easy. For this, these rules made by the Supreme Court in 2018 must be followed... A board of hospital doctors checks the patient's condition and makes a report. The Collector forms a second medical board of 3-5 experts, which checks this report. When both boards agree, this decision is sent to the Judicial Magistrate. The Magistrate meets the patient and makes the final decision. If there is any kind of dispute in this, an appeal can be made to the High Court. Has this happened in any case before Harish Rana's case is the first such case of passive euthanasia in India where the Supreme Court's rules are being followed. Actually, in the 2018 Common Cause judgment, the Supreme Court had made rules which have not been applied to any case until now. Harish's case is the first case in which these are being implemented. On December 11, the Supreme Court ordered Delhi AIIMS to form another medical board to examine Harish Rana's condition. In this case, the process of primary and secondary medical boards is proceeding under court supervision. However, the 2011 Aruna Shanbaug case first legalized passive euthanasia, which became the basis for the 2018 Common Cause case. Aruna Shanbaug Case: In 1973, at Mumbai's KEM Hospital, a 42-year-old nurse Aruna Shanbaug was attacked and then raped by a ward attendant. Due to severe brain injuries sustained in the attack, Aruna went into a coma. Given her serious condition, in 2009, a journalist Pinki Virani filed a petition in the Supreme Court on Aruna's behalf. The petition requested removal of Aruna's life support machines so that she could die naturally. In this case, the Supreme Court had declared euthanasia a legal right, but did not grant permission for Aruna's euthanasia. Because at that time she was breathing to some extent without machines. After this, Aruna Shanbaug died naturally in 2015.

stories.title: UP gas crisis triggers long queues, panic:Man suffers heart attack in Hapur; protests erupt in Unnao
stories.summary: Gas cylinder shortage continues in Uttar Pradesh. Long queues are being seen outside gas agencies. Around 11 am on Tuesday in Hapur, a 35-year-old man suffered a heart attack while standing in line for a cylinder. He collapsed on the ground. People tried to give him CPR and then admitted him to a nearby hospital. The man, Pappu, is a resident of Kavi Nagar and works as a driver. This is the third such case in the country where someone has suffered a heart attack while standing in a gas cylinder queue. Earlier, Mukhtar Ansari (75) in Farrukhabad and Bhushan Kumar Mittal (66) in Barnala district of Punjab had suffered heart attacks; both died. See 2 pictures... In Unnao, people became angry after Bhaiyaji Gas Agency was closed without prior notice. Around 1 pm, residents blocked the Kanpur–Lucknow highway by placing cylinders on the road. Police later persuaded them and cleared the blockade. In Kanpur, people who reached gas agencies said they were not getting cylinders even after receiving OTPs. At the agency, they were told their booking did not exist A 55-year-old woman, Mumtaz, said, “My house has five daughters. Even after getting the slip, I am not receiving a cylinder. The agency staff keep sending me back every day. I have BP issues. I am spending ₹200 daily on travel. If something happens to me, who will look after my children?” For the past 15 days, people across the state have been facing problems regarding gas cylinders. Officials claim there is no shortage, saying panic among people is causing the situation.

stories.title: RSS chief flags conversion, infiltration threat during Mathura event:Mohan Bhagwat says, 'wrong mentality prevailing in society'
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat arrived in Vrindavan on Tuesday. He participated in the inauguration ceremony of Jeevan Deep Ashram. He took blessings by touching the feet of saints. Addressing the program on conversion and infiltration, the RSS chief said that efforts are ongoing to bring back those people who were previously Hindu and have now gone to other communities. He also spoke about focusing on employment and civil rights issues. Bhagwat said that all citizens in India should be treated equally, but special opportunities and employment can be ensured for indigenous Hindu people. Society and administration should work together to make efforts to prevent conversion and infiltration. The security of the community should be maintained. The RSS chief said, "The wrong mentality that has been prevailing in society for a long time needs to change now. Many people do not adopt the right path due to their ego, selfishness, and old caste feelings. Fighting and quarrels among ourselves only cause harm. Old ways, which seemed right in the past, are no longer appropriate and need to be changed. See 3 photos.. UP Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, MP Chief Minister Mohan Yadav and Juna Akhada's Avdheshanand Giri also attended the program. Former Bihar Governor Arif Mohammad Khan and former Maharashtra Governor Bhagat Singh Koshyari participated in the program. Mahamandleshwar Yatindranand Giri of Roorkee has set up Jeevan Deep Ashram in Rukmani Vihar, marking his fifth ashram. The 24-room facility is aimed at providing spiritual guidance along with Vedic education. The foundation stone of the ashram was laid by RSS Sarkaryawah Bhaiyaji Joshi. Notably, before embracing spiritual life, Yatindranand Giri served as an important member of the RSS.

stories.title: Ghaziabad cops arrest Mathura woman in espionage case:Rickshaw driver allegedly filmed crucial sites, sent them to Pakistan for money
stories.summary: Ghaziabad police have arrested 30-year-old Meera Prajapati from Mathura on suspicion of espionage. An e-rickshaw driver and mother of two living separately from her husband, she reportedly used her rickshaw to spy without raising suspicion. On March 22, police also apprehended two others, Naushad from Bihar and a minor. During interrogation, all three admitted receiving Rs 4,000–6,000 for photographing sensitive locations and sending the information to Pakistan. So far, 22 people have been arrested in the case. Investigations reveal that the accused installed solar-powered CCTVs at sensitive sites, with live feeds sent directly to Pakistan. Meera’s involvement is considered the most surprising. To know more about her, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached the Aurangabad area of Mathura, where she used to live. The team spoke to her family. Read what they said Detained a year ago in arms trafficking Meera Thakur lived in Mahadev Nagar Colony. People in the area know her as Hariya. According to the police, Meera was caught by Delhi's special team in 2025 in a case of illegal arms trafficking. She also went to jail in this case, although she later got bail. Meera’s family and background Meera taken by police in March Narottam said that on the night of March 13, some people suddenly took Meera away; he didn’t know if they were police or criminals. On March 14, her husband Mukesh filed a complaint, followed by her mother Prakashi’s online complaint on March 15. It is now revealed that Ghaziabad police had taken her. Prakashi, sitting wrapped in a blanket at Narottam’s house, said that the police pushed open the gate at night. Everyone was in plain clothes and asked them to show Meera’s house, which they did. 550 sq ft house, lock hanging Brother Narottam said that Meera has built a house in Mahadev Nagar, 500 meters away. After getting information about Meera's house, we reached Mahadev Nagar. Here, Meera's house is built on 550 sq ft. The door was locked. Upon inquiring in the vicinity, it was learned that Meera had been living here with her two daughters for about a year. Her husband Mukesh had left after a dispute. Meera's house initially had a tin shed, which was later gradually converted into a single-story house. ‘Meera was friendly and had a good mobile phone’ E-Rickshaw route under scrutiny Police investigation revealed that Meera had registered her e-rickshaw with the municipal corporation and was assigned route number 9, which runs from the National Highway through Cantt Chauraha to Cantt Station. The route passes through the Army Area, Cantt Station, offices and residences of top district officials, and the Veterinary University, an area critical for security. Initial investigation suggests Meera sent photos of these locations. How was the footage being sent from India to Pakistan? Recently, a case of espionage came to light in the Sahibabad area of Ghaziabad, UP, after information from a beat constable. The investigation found that small solar-powered cameras were installed around sensitive areas. These cameras were connected to foreign servers via the internet. Their live feed was being sent directly to Pakistan, posing a threat to the country's internal security. The investigation revealed that CCTVs have been installed by different agencies across the country, but there is no integrated database or clear control system. This is why flaws persist in the surveillance system in many places, which have now become security risks. All networks across the country to be checked According to sources, the Ministry of Home Affairs, in collaboration with IB and other agencies, is preparing to start an audit of CCTV networks across the country. Meanwhile, from April 1, only hacking-proof cameras that pass government security checks (STQC certification) will be sold. 80% of cameras in India are from China, which poses a risk of data theft. Currently, only 53 models from 7 companies are considered certified and secure.

stories.title: 23 constables suspended for fake sick leave:Cite illness and appear for departmental exam to get promotion
stories.summary: In a disciplinary crackdown, 23 police constables in Jhansi have been suspended after it was found that they falsely claimed illness to take leave and appear for the Sub-Inspector (SI) recruitment examination. The action was taken by Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) B.B.G.T.S. Murthy on March 19, although the matter came to light on Monday. Leave misused to appear in exam According to officials, all 23 constables applied for leave citing medical reasons. However, instead of being unwell, they traveled to take the SI recruitment exam. After the examination, they returned and resumed duty as if nothing had happened. An internal departmental inquiry later revealed the truth, leading to immediate suspension. The SSP termed the act as indiscipline, stating that the constables took leave on false grounds without proper permission. SI recruitment exam held in March The written examination for 4,543 Sub-Inspector posts in Uttar Pradesh Police was conducted on March 14 and 15. Authorities stressed that while filling out application forms does not require prior approval, appearing for the examination does require official permission. Rules on permission and leave Former Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police, Sulkhan Singh, explained that police personnel must seek formal approval before appearing in any examination. Leave taken for such purposes is deducted from the annual leave quota. However, if leave is obtained under false pretenses, it is treated as a serious disciplinary violation and warrants a departmental inquiry. Possible consequences for the accused If found guilty in the inquiry, the constables may face strict penalties, including: Department orders further probe The SSP has ordered a detailed departmental investigation to determine individual accountability and ensure strict action against those found guilty. The incident highlights concerns over discipline within the force and reinforces the importance of adhering to official procedures. Who all faced action, and where were they posted?

stories.title: Cylinder blast during cooking kills brother and sister:Explosion flattens house; mother and sibling rescued from debris
stories.summary: A gas cylinder exploded while food was being prepared in a Varanasi house on Tuesday morning, around 9. The powerful blast caused the entire house to collapse, killing a brother and sister, while their mother and another brother were trapped under the debris. Police and rescue teams reached the spot promptly, pulled them out, and rushed them to the BHU Trauma Center. Doctors declared two of them dead on arrival. Victims identified The deceased has been identified as, Aman Chaudhary (31) and Preeti alias Lakshmi (24). Four family members were present in the house at the time of the incident. See 3 pictures Location and Impact The incident took place in the Lahartara area, about 7 kilometers from the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. The explosion was so intense that it caused cracks in several nearby houses. Residents rushed out of their homes in panic and gathered to help with rescue efforts. Family background The house belonged to 60-year-old Girija Devi, who lived there with her two sons and a daughter: Their father, Atma Prasad, had passed away three years ago. How the incident happened The house was about 50 years old. While the rear portion had been recently constructed and was still under finishing work, the front portion (around 400 square feet) was in a dilapidated condition. The family was present in this section at the time of the incident. According to initial reports, Girija Devi was cooking when gas began leaking from the cylinder. The pipe caught fire, and before she could react, a massive explosion occurred, causing the house to collapse. Rescue operation After hearing the explosion, neighbors rushed to the scene and informed the police and fire department. With the help of locals, rescue teams pulled all four people from the rubble and sent them to the hospital. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) also reached the site. A senior police official confirmed that the explosion was caused by a gas cylinder blast. Eyewitness account Chanda Sahni, a relative living nearby, said: We were asleep when we heard a loud explosion. We rushed outside and saw the house had collapsed. We immediately called others for help and informed the police. The electricity supply was cut off for safety. Investigation underway Authorities are investigating the exact cause of the gas leak and assessing the structural safety of nearby buildings. The incident raises serious concerns about gas safety and the condition of old residential structures.

stories.title: Jaya Prada’s meetings trigger comeback speculation:After talks with BJP state chief and Aparna, questions rise on 2027 elections role
stories.summary: After a long political lull, Jaya Prada has once again sparked speculation about her active return to Uttar Pradesh politics. On March 22, she was in Lucknow, where within a span of just six hours, she met two prominent BJP faces—state president Pankaj Chaudhary and party leader Aparna Yadav. Photos of these meetings quickly surfaced, fueling discussions about whether Jaya Prada is preparing for a larger political role—either within the party organization or as a candidate in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Return after long political silence Jaya Prada was last seen in March 2024 in Rampur, when she appeared in an MP-MLA court. Since then, she had largely stayed away from active politics. Her sudden presence among senior BJP leaders has raised eyebrows and triggered speculation about her next move. While she reportedly visited Lucknow to attend a private event, her political engagements during the visit have become the center of attention. Meeting with BJP state chief sparks speculation Jaya Prada began her political career in Andhra Pradesh but gained significant recognition in Uttar Pradesh, particularly from Rampur, where she won the Lok Sabha elections in 2004 and 2009 on a Samajwadi Party (SP) ticket. However, she was expelled from Samajwadi in 2010, after which her political journey saw several shifts—from forming her own outfit to joining the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), and eventually the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). After contesting the 2019 Lok Sabha elections from Rampur as a BJP candidate and losing, she remained largely on the sidelines. Her recent meeting with Pankaj Chaudhary has reignited political discussions. According to party insiders, the two leaders have known each other since her tenure as an MP and have met frequently in the past. Following the event, Jaya Prada accompanied Chaudhary to the BJP office, where they reportedly held a long discussion. Although the details of the conversation remain undisclosed, party sources have termed it a routine interaction. However, senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana believes otherwise. He suggests that this meeting signals Jaya Prada’s intent to become politically active again. With Chaudhary recently taking charge as state president and working on organizational restructuring, there is speculation that Jaya Prada could be given a significant role within the party. Will she contest from Rampur or elsewhere? Political observers remain divided on whether Jaya Prada will contest the 2027 Assembly elections. After her expulsion from SP, she contested from Bijnor on an RLD ticket, indicating that she does not have an independent vote base in Rampur. Senior journalist Faiz-e-Aam Akbar, who closely tracks Rampur politics, notes that while Jaya Prada is a popular celebrity capable of drawing crowds, her absence from Rampur since her 2019 defeat weakens her prospects in the constituency. Rampur district has five assembly seats—two are currently held by BJP and its ally Apna Dal (S), while three are with Samajwadi. The political landscape has undergone significant changes, especially after Azam Khan was jailed. There is a growing sympathy factor for Azam Khan among sections of the electorate. Reports suggest that his daughter-in-law may contest from the Rampur Sadar seat, making it a tough battleground. The Swar seat is already held by BJP ally Apna Dal (S), while the remaining seats are Muslim-majority constituencies, where Jaya Prada’s candidacy remains uncertain. Given these dynamics, experts believe she may avoid contesting from Rampur to prevent another electoral setback. BJP’s potential counter to Samajwadi’s ‘women card’ Jaya Prada could play a crucial role in BJP’s strategy against the Samajwadi Party’s outreach to women voters. Recently, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav announced an initiative to honor women from different communities and promised an annual financial assistance of ₹40,000 to women if his party comes to power in 2027. The BJP has strongly criticized this move, with Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya raising concerns about women’s safety during SP’s previous tenure. In this context, Jaya Prada could emerge as a strong counter-narrative. During her time in SP, she had a bitter public fallout with Azam Khan, who made controversial remarks about her. BJP may leverage this past conflict to challenge SP’s claims on women empowerment. Meeting With Aparna Yadav Signals Strategic Alignment After her meeting at the BJP office, Jaya Prada visited the residence of Aparna Yadav, who is also the daughter-in-law of Mulayam Singh Yadav. Aparna welcomed her warmly with a traditional tilak, and the two shared a hug—indicating a strong personal rapport. According to sources, they held a closed-door meeting for about an hour. The political significance of this meeting is noteworthy. Both leaders have roots in the Samajwadi Party but are now part of BJP. Their joint presence could be part of a broader strategy to target SP, especially its leadership under Akhilesh Yadav. There is growing speculation that BJP may project both leaders together as influential women faces with SP backgrounds to politically corner Akhilesh. Controversies surrounding Jaya Prada Jaya Prada’s career has also been marked by several controversies: Comeback or Cautious positioning? Jaya Prada’s recent political engagements suggest that she is keen on re-entering active politics. Whether she will contest the 2027 Assembly elections or take up a key organizational role in BJP remains uncertain. However, her meetings with top BJP leaders and her renewed visibility indicate that she could soon play a significant role in the party’s Uttar Pradesh strategy—especially as it prepares for a high-stakes electoral battle in 2027.

stories.title: Rinku Singh to become Regional Sports Officer:UP CM Yogi Adityanath will hand over appointment letters to several athletes today
stories.summary: Ahead of the IPL 2026, Rinku Singh is set to receive key responsibility as the Regional Sports Officer (RSO) as per the Sports Directorate of Uttar Pradesh. The appointment letters are expected to be handed over to athletes at the UP Sports award ceremony today. Notably, Rinku is part of the Kolkata Knight Riders. Known for his prowess as a match-finisher, Rinku is currently entirely focused on the Indian Premier League, which is set to start from March 28. At Lok Bhawan, CM Yogi Adityanath will present appointment certificates for officer-level posts to a total of six athletes. He will also distribute the Rani Lakshmi Bai and Laxman Awards. Rajkumar Pal (from Ghazipur), a member of the Indian hockey team that won the bronze medal at the Olympics, will be awarded the rank of DSP. Rinku Singh set to receive key responsibility The Uttar Pradesh government is in the process of offering government jobs to several athletes, including Rinku, who was part of the T20 World Cup 2026 winning team. Apart from the 28-year-old, the list of beneficiaries includes the names of several other athletes. Praveen Kumar, who delivered a stellar performance in para-athletics, and Raj Kumar Pal, a hockey medallist at the Paris Olympics, are set to be appointed to the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police. : Abhishek, Ishan, Head lead fiery batting, but bowling lacks sting: SRH SWOT Analysis CM Yogi Adityanath to hand over appointment letters Additionally, para-athletes Ajit Singh and Simran will be appointed as District Panchayat Raj Officers, while Preeti Pal will be appointed as the Block Development Officer. All these appointments are being made under the "Uttar Pradesh International Medal Winners Direct Recruitment Rules-2022," a framework designed to honour athletes who have won medals at major international platforms such as the Olympics, Paralympics, Commonwealth Games, and Asian Games. On Tuesday, March 24, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will personally hand over the appointment letters to these athletes at the Lok Bhawan in Lucknow. KKR's first match on March 29 Notably, in the 2026 IPL season, Rinku Singh's team, the Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), will start their campaign on March 29. KKR's opening fixture will be against the Mumbai Indians. This match is scheduled to take place at the Wankhede Stadium. Rinku Singh will be aiming to make a significant impact in the IPL right from the very first match. Rinku has been an integral part of the KKR squad since 2018. He has scored 1,099 runs for Kolkata in 59 IPL matches, including four half-centuries. During this period, his average has been 30.52 and his strike rate 145.17. Additionally, para-athletes Ajit Singh and Simran will serve as District Panchayat Raj Officers, while Preeti Pal has been appointed as a Block Development Officer. These appointments follow a 2022 government rule in Uttar Pradesh that allows international medal winners from events like the Olympics, Paralympics and Asian Games to be hired directly for government roles.
