stories.title: Azam in jail, Samajwadi reshuffles Rampur leadership:Party faces backlash prior to 2027 polls as supporters allege betrayal
stories.summary: The political landscape of Rampur is witnessing a significant shift as the Samajwadi Party (SP) attempts to recalibrate its leadership strategy ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. At the center of this transition lies a growing and increasingly visible rift between senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan and party chief Akhilesh Yadav. The tension became evident on November 7, 2025, when Akhilesh Yadav visited Rampur to meet Azam Khan shortly after his release from jail. The meeting, which was expected to signal unity, instead revealed underlying discomfort. Azam Khan appeared visibly upset and made remarks that hinted at emotional and political distance. Responding to questions about his relationship with the party leadership, Azam said, “The heart is no longer there; we are working without it. This relationship will take centuries to break. If it gathers rust, I will clean it myself—no one else is needed.” This cryptic yet sharp statement suggested that Azam was wary of external interference in Rampur’s political affairs—particularly any leadership imposed without his consent. Samajwadi Party’s surprise move: Appointment of Surendra Sagar Less than four months later, on March 2, 2026, SP made a decisive move by appointing former BSP leader Surendra Sagar as State Secretary. The decision was taken in Azam Khan’s absence, as he is currently serving a seven-year sentence in a fake PAN card case. The move has sparked resentment among Azam Khan’s loyalists in Rampur. Even weeks after the announcement, discontent continues to simmer on the ground. Supporters argue that the decision reflects a gradual sidelining of Azam, who once single-handedly dominated Rampur’s political landscape. Many believe the timing of the decision is crucial. With Azam Khan barred from contesting elections until at least 2028, the party appears to be preparing for a post-Azam political scenario in Rampur. The big questions The leadership change has raised several important political questions: Strategic reasons behind the shift 1. Strengthening the PDA social coalition The Samajwadi Party has been aggressively promoting its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak—Backward, Dalit, Minority) formula as a cornerstone of its electoral strategy. By appointing Surendra Sagar, who has strong roots among Dalit communities, SP aims to consolidate its outreach among marginalized sections. Rampur and the broader Moradabad division have a significant Dalit population. Sagar’s induction into a key organizational role sends a message that the party is serious about expanding its social coalition beyond its traditional Muslim-Yadav base. 2. Filling the leadership vacuum Azam Khan’s legal troubles have created a leadership vacuum in Rampur. Having spent nearly 50 months in jail over the past five years, his active participation in politics has been severely limited. After his release in September 2025, Azam Khan remained politically active for just 54 days before being sentenced again in November. This uncertainty has made it difficult for the party to rely solely on him for future electoral battles. By elevating Surendra Sagar, SP is attempting to create an alternative leadership structure that can function independently of Azam’s availability. 3. Targeting BSP’s core vote bank Surendra Sagar’s political background is deeply rooted in the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). He has served as a district president five times and has a strong network among Dalit and Jatav voters. SP’s strategy appears to be aimed at making inroads into BSP’s traditional vote bank. By bringing in a leader with grassroots connections, the party hopes to attract voters who have historically supported BSP. Sagar’s political journey also reflects shifting alliances in Uttar Pradesh politics. He was expelled from BSP by Mayawati in December 2024, reportedly due to internal disagreements. 4. Managing internal factionalism Rampur’s SP unit has long been plagued by factionalism. Differences between local leaders, including MP Mohibullah Nadvi and Azam Khan’s camp, have created internal friction. By appointing an outsider like Sagar, the party leadership is attempting to neutralize existing power struggles. The move is seen as an effort to balance competing factions and establish a more centralized control over the district unit. From unchallenged authority to political isolation Azam Khan’s political journey in Rampur is nothing short of remarkable. A nine-time MLA and two-time MP, he has been the face of SP in the region for over four decades. His influence peaked during the tenure of Mulayam Singh Yadav. As a cabinet minister, Azam wielded immense power, and his word often carried more weight than official directives. Between 2012 and 2017, it was widely believed that key administrative decisions in Rampur—from the appointment of district officials to local governance matters—were influenced by Azam Khan. One of his most significant achievements was the establishment of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, which became a symbol of his political clout. However, the political landscape changed dramatically after the rise of Yogi Adityanath in 2017. Since then, Azam has faced multiple legal challenges and prolonged periods of incarceration, significantly reducing his political influence. “SP now wants a silent Azam Khan” Political analyst Tamkeen Fayaz Khan offers a sharp assessment of the current situation. According to him, Azam Khan’s stature within SP remains intact, but his outspoken nature has become a liability for the party. “The party now prefers a silent Azam Khan,” he says. “When he is in jail, he works like a fixed deposit for SP. But when he is out, his statements often create discomfort.” Azam Khan has, on several occasions, publicly questioned the party’s implementation of the PDA formula, particularly its treatment of minority leaders. Such statements have reportedly caused unease within the party leadership. Signs of deliberate distancing There are growing indications that SP may be consciously distancing itself from the Azam Khan family. A notable example was a major minority conference organised in Rampur, where Azam’s son Abdullah Azam Khan was not invited, despite being out on bail at the time. This exclusion was widely interpreted as a signal that the party is no longer prioritizing the Azam family in its political calculations. Both Azam Khan and Abdullah Azam have been disqualified from contesting elections for several years due to legal convictions—further complicating their political future. Ground reactions: Divided opinions Anger among loyalists Many of Azam Khan’s supporters view the leadership change as a betrayal. Local residents argue that his contributions to Rampur’s development—particularly in infrastructure, education, and healthcare—are unmatched. One resident remarked that even top leaders would struggle to match Azam’s influence in Rampur. Support for change At the same time, there is a section of voters that welcomes the shift. They believe that Rampur’s politics has been dominated by a single family for too long. Supporters of Surendra Sagar argue that his grassroots approach and focus on village-level outreach could bring a new dimension to local politics. Experts: Azam Khan still a dominant force Despite the current developments, many political observers believe that Azam Khan’s influence in Rampur remains formidable. His legacy, built over decades, continues to command respect among large sections of the population. Senior journalists and analysts argue that replacing a leader of his stature is not an easy task. While Surendra Sagar may strengthen the party organizationally, matching Azam’s mass appeal will be a significant challenge. Conclusion: A high-stakes political gamble The Samajwadi Party’s decision to promote Surendra Sagar marks a clear shift in its political strategy. By attempting to diversify its leadership and expand its social base, the party is preparing for a future where it cannot rely solely on Azam Khan. However, this transition comes with risks. Alienating Azam’s loyal support base could weaken the party’s position in Rampur—a constituency that has long been considered its stronghold. As the 2027 elections approach, Rampur is set to become a key battleground, reflecting not just electoral dynamics but also the evolving power equations within the Samajwadi Party.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Pending SIR list pushes by-polls on 3 Assembly seats beyond April 10; Israel says Iran’s security chief Larijani 'killed' more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Israel says Iran’s Larijani killed, Tehran rejects claim Israeli military claimed that it has targeted ⁠Iran's ​security chief ​Ali Larijani, adding that ​it ​was not immediately ‌clear ⁠whether he was killed ​or ​injured, Reuters reported quoting Israeli media. 2. By-elections on 3 UP Assembly seats after April 10: Pending SIR list causes the delay; SP says, 'BJP is scared' By-elections for three assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh could be held after April 10. According to Election Commission officials, polls cannot be conducted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls, so elections can only take place after the final voter list is released. 3. Former councillor murdered on morning walk in Gorakhpur: Ran 100 metres after attack, 4 men chased stabbed him A former councillor was murdered while out on a morning walk in Gorakhpur. According to eyewitnesses, 4 attackers surrounded him and launched a knife attack. After being assaulted, former councillor Rajkumar Chauhan tried to escape and ran nearly 100 metres. However, the attackers chased him and stabbed him again. 4. TMC announces candidates for 291 seats in Bengal The Trinamool Congress (TMC) on Tuesday released its list of candidates for 291 out of the total 294 seats. CM Mamata Banerjee will contest the elections from the Bhabanipur constituency, where she is set to face BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari. 5. Varun Gandhi meets PM Modi: First meeting after Lok Sabha ticket snub: Neither he nor Maneka in Parliament Former Pilibhit MP and BJP leader Varun Gandhi met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday. This was their first meeting after he was denied a ticket in the recent Lok Sabha elections. Varun visited the Prime Minister along with his family. 6. Kuldeep Yadav’s wedding reception in Lucknow today: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Ravindra Jadeja, Shikhar Dhawan arrive; over 900 VVIP guests expected Indian cricket team spinner Kuldeep Yadav has married his childhood friend, Vanshika Chadha. The couple tied the knot on 14 March in Mussoorie, Uttarakhand, in an intimate ceremony attended only by close family members and relatives. A grand reception is being held today in Lucknow, where more than 900 guests are expected to attend. 7. SC scraps 3-month maternity leave cap for adoptive mothers The Supreme Court on Tuesday declared unconstitutional a provision in the Code on Social Security, 2020, that limited maternity leave to adoptive mothers of children below three months of age. 8. FIR, arrests in Varanasi over iftar on Ganga boat: 14 men held after BJYM complaint over non-veg consumption in sacred river An iftar party held on a boat in the middle of the Ganges in Kashi has triggered a controversy after a video of the event went viral on social media. Organizers served fruits, dry fruits and chicken biryani to those observing the fast. The mention of chicken biryani in the viral video drew strong objections from BJP leaders and Hindu organizations. 9. 11-year old murdered in Kanpur, nude body buried in field: Suspicion of rape on neighbour; crowd attempts to burn suspect's house An 11-year-old girl was found murdered in Kanpur, with her body recovered from a field on Tuesday morning. The body was found buried and without clothing, with multiple deep injury marks. Police suspect she may have been sexually assaulted before being killed. 10. AB de Villiers questions Dhoni's spot in CSK With a major revamp in the Chennai Super Kings ahead of the Indian Premier League 2026, all eyes will be on MS Dhoni and how he establishes himself as a valuable addition to the playing XI. With Sanju Samson joining the Yellow army as wicketkeeper, South Africa legend AB de Villiers has questioned if Thala will really add any value as an individual.

stories.title: Euthanasia for Harish Rana starts from Tuesday:Doctors stop water intake for bed-ridden patient, parents cannot meet
stories.summary: Harish Rana of Ghaziabad, who has been in a coma for the past 13 years, will stop receiving water from today, Tuesday, as part of the process to end life support. He is not on any oxygen support, and earlier, food given through a tube had already been stopped. Now, doctors will place a cap on the feeding tube after stopping water, though the tube will remain in his body. A team of doctors at AIIMS Delhi is closely monitoring his condition and gradually following all procedures to withdraw life support. However, the hospital has not made any official statement on the matter. The development comes after the Supreme Court granted permission for euthanasia on March 11. Harish was shifted to AIIMS from his home in Raj Nagar, Ghaziabad, on March 14. Following the court’s directions, the process began on March 16. Strict restrictions have now been imposed at AIIMS, with a complete ban on photos and videos. No family members or outsiders are being allowed to meet him. Oxygen removed, doctors' team is monitoring 31-year-old Harish Rana is currently in the Palliative Care ward of IRCH at AIIMS. Here, a complete protocol has been established to implement the Supreme Court's decision allowing 'passive euthanasia'. A large meeting of doctors was held on Monday. Senior doctors from various departments participated in it. After this, late in the evening, he was not given food through a tube. His oxygen support has also been removed. Doctors stated that after food and water are stopped, a person can only survive for one to two weeks. A video from before he was taken from home to AIIMS had surfaced Just before Harish was being taken to AIIMS, Brahmakumari Lovely had arrived at his home. She had applied a sandalwood tilak on Harish's forehead. Stroking his head, she had said- Forgiving everyone and asking for forgiveness from everyone, now go...okay... During this time, the eyes of all members of Harish's family became moist. Father Ashok had apologised to all family members. He had said- This step had to be taken even unwillingly. Harish's family has been associated with Brahmakumaris for about 18 years. About 6 years ago, the entire family had shifted to Ghaziabad. Before that, Harish Rana's father Ashok Rana lived in Delhi for 13 years. BK Lovely said that 2-3 years ago, the family had informed about Harish's suffering. Harish's brother, sister, mother, and father used to cry all the time. When they could no longer bear Harish's pain, they came to the BK center and put forward the idea of euthanasia. They said that enough was enough, they could no longer see their son in such pain. Just grant him liberation. Supreme Court did a great favor to Harish by giving approval The Rana family had said, 'The High Court had rejected our petition, but the Supreme Court did a great favor to Harish by giving approval. We cannot bear to see his pain, and the helplessness is that he cannot even tell us where or what is bothering him. We don't even want to call this passive euthanasia. We are leaving him in God's lap. When Harish breathes his last, we will bring him home with great respect and give him a final farewell. Silence descended on the family and society After Harish was shifted to Delhi AIIMS, there is silence in the family. The father is also not meeting anyone; society members only say that he is emotional. The sister and mother cried even after returning from Delhi. The one they gave birth to, nurtured and raised. What kind of pain would a mother feel having to care for him like an infant again? The only sorrow was that he didn't even tell his pain. When I massaged him morning and evening, I would tell him stories from home, what happened today? Many times I would just wait for hours for him to just blink once, so that I would feel he had heard everything. Sometimes he would yawn, sometimes sneeze, or the skin around his eyes would twitch, and that would give us the comfort that he was alive. Know the reason how Harish reached this state Harish Rana, born in Delhi, was pursuing B.Tech from Punjab University, Chandigarh. In 2013, during his final semester studies, he fell from the fourth floor of the hostel. After the accident, his entire body was paralyzed and he went into a coma. Since then, he has been unable to speak or feel anything. Doctors have diagnosed Harish with a severe condition called quadriplegia. In this condition, the patient survives entirely with the help of a feeding tube and a ventilator. According to doctors, the chances of recovery are almost nil. Due to being continuously bedridden for the past 13 years, Harish has also developed bedsores, or deep wounds, on his body. Over time, his condition has deteriorated further. It has become extremely difficult for the family to see him like this, mentally.

stories.title: UP govt mandates expiry and laying date on eggs:Rule to take effect from 1 April, key meeting of distributors on 18 March
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh government has taken a big step to protect people’s health. From April 1, 2026, it will be compulsory to print the expiry date on eggs sold in the state. With this rule in place, shopkeepers will not be able to sell old or spoiled eggs by claiming they are fresh. Customers will be able to check the date themselves and decide whether the egg is safe to eat or not. Why was this rule introduced? Investigations by the Animal Husbandry Department and the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) revealed that old or spoiled eggs were being sold as 'fresh' in many places, which could pose a risk to people's health. Rules were not being followed. Harishankar Singh, Joint Commissioner of FSDA, said that efforts for this had been going on for two years. Initially, it was decided to write the batch number, but this was not practically possible. Because eggs come from different places, it was not possible to write the batch number. Therefore, it has been decided that the date should be written on the eggs. For this, the laying and expiry dates will be stamped on the eggs. Additional Chief Secretary of Animal Husbandry and Dairy Department, Mukesh Meshram, said, The government has taken this step to protect the health of consumers. This step is very important for increasing food transparency. Meeting of Egg Distributors on March 18 Harishankar Singh informed that a meeting of the state's major egg distributors has been called on March 18. In this, discussions will be held with them to understand and implement the government order. It is to be implemented from April 1, and we want to understand how it will be implemented and how it will be monitored. What will be printed on the egg? Laying Date: When the hen laid the egg, i.e., the production date. Expiry Date: How long the egg will remain safe, i.e., the spoilage date. What was the rule until now: The production date is written on the egg tray, but not individual stamping on each egg. What is the punishment for breaking the rules? If any producer, farmer, poultry farm, or shopkeeper does not comply with this rule, strict action will be taken. Their eggs will be confiscated and destroyed, or they will be stamped 'unfit for human consumption'. Such eggs will not be allowed to be sold in the market. Everyone will be forced to comply with the rules. How many days do eggs remain safe? According to Harishankar Singh Why is separate storage necessary? According to food safety regulations, eggs cannot be stored in the same cold storage with vegetables or other food items. Both require different temperatures and conditions. Proper storage helps eggs stay fresh for a longer time. Condition of Cold Storages in UP Currently, there are only two special cold storages for eggs in the state. One in Agra and the other in Jhansi. This number is very low for the entire state. Lack of storage remains a big challenge. The government will need to build more cold storages in the future so that new rules can be implemented easily. 2.5 crore eggs consumed daily in UP The state consumes 2.50 crore eggs daily. Currently, egg production in the state is around 1.60 crore. More than 90 lakh eggs are imported from states like Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, etc. Egg consumption increases by 20 to 25 percent in India. The annual per capita egg consumption in the country is 106. However, in UP, the annual per capita consumption is 30 eggs. If consumption in UP also increases like the national average of 106 eggs per year, then 7 crore eggs would be needed daily here. What kind of harm can eating bad eggs cause? According to FSDA, the biggest risk of eating bad eggs is food poisoning. This is especially caused by infection from Salmonella bacteria that thrive in eggs. Other bacteria like E-coli can also grow in bad eggs, which can cause serious illness. This can lead to severe abdominal pain, cramps, vomiting, nausea, fever, headache, fatigue, abdominal bloating, and dehydration. Sometimes, bloody diarrhea can also occur. For children, the elderly, pregnant women, and patients with diabetes or cancer, this can even be fatal.

stories.title: FIR, arrests in Varanasi over iftar on Ganga boat:14 men held after BJYM complaint over non-veg consumption in sacred river
stories.summary: An iftar party held on a boat in the middle of the Ganges in Kashi has triggered a controversy after a video of the event went viral on social media. Organisers served fruits, dry fruits and chicken biryani to those observing the fast. The mention of chicken biryani in the viral video drew strong objections from BJP leaders and Hindu organisations. Following the backlash, Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha’s city president Rajat Jaiswal lodged a complaint at Kotwali police station against unidentified persons. Acting swiftly, the police registered a case and arrested 14 people within eight hours of the complaint. See 3 images... Now read the full story… On Monday evening, a youth organised a Roza iftar programme on the Ganga river in Kashi. People observing the fast were invited to the ghats, where a large boat had been pre-booked. The group travelled by boat from Assi Ghat to Namo Ghat. During the journey, those fasting first offered namaz and then broke their fast with dates and fruits. In another video from the event, several people on the boat were seen eating food from a large vessel. Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) city president Rajat Jaiswal alleged that chicken biryani was served and that its bones were thrown into the Ganga. He filed a written complaint at Kotwali police station over the incident. Jaiswal said the Ganga is a major centre of faith for followers of Sanatan Dharma, with lakhs of devotees visiting daily to take achaman (a ritual sip of holy water). He termed the alleged act of consuming chicken biryani on the river and disposing of its remains in the Ganga as “condemnable”. A video of the incident was also submitted as evidence along with the complaint. He further claimed that the incident had hurt the religious sentiments of Sanatan followers and demanded strict action against those involved, including the boatman. He also called for cancellation of the boatman’s licence. Meanwhile, the Varanasi Police acted swiftly in the case. ACP Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh said a complaint was received from Rajat Jaiswal, following which an FIR was registered. Two police teams were formed and raids were carried out to identify and arrest the accused. So far, 14 people have been arrested, and further investigation is underway.

stories.title: Varun Gandhi meets PM Modi with family:First meeting after Lok Sabha ticket snub; may return in active politics
stories.summary: Former Pilibhit MP and BJP leader Varun Gandhi met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday. This was their first meeting after he was denied a ticket in the recent Lok Sabha elections. Varun visited the Prime Minister along with his family. After the meeting, Varun Gandhi shared a post on X, saying, “Your presence carries a unique paternal warmth and a sense of protection. Meeting you strengthens the belief that you are the true guardian of the nation and its people.” His mother, Maneka Gandhi, also lost the Lok Sabha election from Sultanpur. For the first time in three decades, neither mother nor son holds a seat in Parliament. Following the meeting, political circles are abuzz with speculation over Varun Gandhi’s possible return to active politics. Sidelined in party organization for a decade Varun Gandhi was appointed BJP National General Secretary in 2013 and was also given charge of West Bengal. At the time, he was seen as a prominent face in Uttar Pradesh politics, with even speculation around his potential as a chief ministerial candidate. However, when the new party executive was formed in 2014, he was not included. Since then, for nearly a decade, he has not been assigned any significant organizational role. Party insiders believe his critical statements on the government and system contributed to his distancing from the organization. Entered politics in 2009, constituency changed in 2014 Varun Gandhi began his political journey by campaigning for his mother, Maneka Gandhi, in 2004. He formally entered electoral politics in 2009, contesting from Pilibhit, where he won by a margin of 2.81 lakh votes. In 2013, he was elevated as BJP National General Secretary. In 2014, the party swapped constituencies between mother and son—Varun Gandhi was fielded from Sultanpur, while Maneka Gandhi contested from Pilibhit. Varun secured a decisive victory in Sultanpur as well. The Pilibhit seat is considered a stronghold of the Gandhi family. In 2019, Varun Gandhi returned to Pilibhit and was elected MP once again. Varun Gandhi has been a writer by profession Varun Gandhi was born on March 13, 1980. He is a politician, columnist and writer by profession. His wife's name is Yamini Roy Chowdhury. His father is Sanjay Gandhi (deceased) and mother is Maneka Gandhi. He completed his B.Sc. Honours from the University of London.

stories.title: 11-year old murdered in Kanpur, nude body buried in field:Suspicion of rape on neighbour; crowd attempts to burn suspect's house
stories.summary: An 11-year-old girl was found murdered in Kanpur, with her body recovered from a field on Tuesday morning. The body was found buried and without clothing, with multiple deep injury marks. Police suspect she may have been sexually assaulted before being killed. Following the discovery, angry family members created a ruckus, accusing a neighbour of involvement in the crime. The situation escalated as some people attempted to set the suspect’s house on fire. Police reached the spot on receiving information, brought the situation under control and dispersed the crowd. Police have cordoned off the accused’s house and begun a detailed investigation. During the search, mud-stained clothes were found hanging at the neighbour’s residence. The forensic team has seized the clothes for examination. The accused has been detained and is being questioned. The incident took place in a village under the jurisdiction of Bidhnoo Police Station See images Girl missing since Monday evening, family searched all night A resident of a village under Bidhnoo Police Station said his 11-year-old daughter, a Class 5 student, had gone to graze goats in a nearby field on Monday evening but did not return. The family informed the police and began searching for her. Despite efforts throughout the night, no trace of the girl was found. Suspicion after freshly dug soil spotted Alleging police negligence, the family claimed that no immediate assistance was provided in the search. They continued looking on their own and resumed the search early Tuesday morning. During this, they noticed freshly disturbed soil in a wheat field about 300 metres from their home, which raised suspicion. Body found buried in field The family said the soil appeared recently dug, as it was still moist. Suspecting something amiss, they began digging at the spot. Shortly after, they discovered the girl’s body buried in the field, leaving the family in shock. Body found nude, signs of brutality According to the family, the girl’s body was found buried in a pit without clothing. There were visible injury marks, including bleeding from her private parts, and multiple signs of severe assault. The family and villagers immediately informed the police, following which a team from Bidhnoo Police Station along with forensic experts reached the spot. Considering the sensitive condition of the body, police cleared the area and restricted public access by cordoning it off. The body was then carefully recovered, wrapped in cloth and sent for post-mortem examination. The victim’s family has accused a neighbouring युवक (youth) of rape, murder and burying the body. Acting on suspicion, police have detained the accused and are questioning him. Police say key evidence recovered Vipin Tada, Additional Police Commissioner (Law and Order), also reached the scene. He said the case is being investigated seriously and several crucial pieces of evidence have been recovered. He added that the body has been sent for post-mortem, and any confirmation regarding sexual assault will be made only after the medical report is received.

stories.title: Gas crisis hits Lucknow food business:Tunday Kababi doubles prices, 80% shops affected; many on verge of closure
stories.summary: "Our business has completed 100 years, but we have never seen such a big crisis. Gas cylinders are not available and workers are facing a lot of difficulties working with coal and furnaces." This pain was expressed by Lucknow's famous Tunday Kababi's grandson Abu Bakr. The commercial gas cylinder supply disruption in Lucknow has severely impacted the city's food business. Its effect is clearly visible from the traditional market of Chowk to the food courts of large malls. The situation has become so dire that about 80 percent of businesses have been affected and many shops are on the verge of shutting down. How many days have the shops been closed? What are traders saying about this crisis? And how much is it affecting customers? Read the full report... See photos Current situation Famous Tunday Kebab doubles its prices Due to the shortage of gas cylinders, famous Tunday Kebab has nearly doubled the prices of their kebabs. Around 20 shops at the veg point on Chowk intersection have been closed for the past week, causing problems for both shopkeepers and customers. Three options before shopkeepers During a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, shopkeepers expressed their troubles. They said that the gas cylinder problem has increased significantly. They never thought there would be such a big crisis regarding gas. According to traders, they now have three options. Either they close their shops or increase the prices of food items after buying cylinders at higher rates. The third option is to cook on traditional stoves and sell limited items. Now read about traders' problems Had to increase kebab prices Tunday Kebabi's grandson Abu Bakr says that our business is completing 100 years, but we have never faced such a big crisis. Commercial gas cylinders are not available, after which we are cooking food on coal and ovens. The kebabs that we used to sell for 5 rupees per piece, we have now started selling them for 10 rupees per piece. Meanwhile, paratha costs 10 rupees. When that runs out, we make a 20 rupee paratha, which is called double paratha. Workers are also facing a lot of difficulties working with coal and ovens. Coal price increased up to ?15 per kg Abubakr says that a few days ago the government was saying that everything is sufficient, then what is the reason that hotel owners are not getting gas cylinders. Why commercial cylinders are not available, where black marketing is happening, the government should pay attention to this. The way we are doing business, we are not making any profit. Just understand that the shop is running because we cannot close the shop and cannot remove our employees. It's festival time and these people will become unemployed. Coal prices have also increased at this time. Stone coal has increased from 15 rupees to 25 rupees. While wooden coal has increased from 30 rupees to 40-45 rupees. Shop near KGMU closed for 4 days Aman Bhojanalaya is located near KGMU. A large number of attendants and medical students have breakfast here. Owner Ashish Mishra says, “We have been in the food business for the past 25 years, but have never seen such a crisis before. After the gas cylinder shortage began, we managed for a day or two.” “Now the cylinder is finished and we had to close the shop. The shop has been closed for the last 4-5 days. Our shop is near the medical college, so a large number of attendants and doctors used to eat here. They are also facing a lot of problems due to the shop being closed,” he added. Saffron milk and lassi sales stopped Ashish, the owner of the famous Chowk shop Raja Thandai, said that our shop has been running since 1936. It was inaugurated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. For so many years, we have been selling saffron milk and lassi along with thandai. But after the price increase of gas cylinders, we have stopped selling saffron milk and lassi because both items require boiling milk to prepare. Currently, we are only preparing thandai from raw milk. All other food and beverage shops in the market have been closed for a week. The employees working with the shopkeepers are also troubled. Cylinder costing 2000 is now available at 5500 Food vendor Rajiv says - Our work has been completely affected by the ban on commercial gas cylinder supply. Small cylinders are also not being allowed to be used, so we have no option but to close the shop. The closure of shops has affected the workers working with us the most. 22 boys work at our place. We are somehow feeding them, but their families are facing difficulties. We are having to bear double losses Rajiv said - We are having to bear double losses. On one hand, we have to pay salaries to employees and on the other hand, business is completely stalled due to shop closure. We only appeal to the government to stop black marketing of gas cylinders. For now, we are preparing to use wood and coal as alternatives to keep the work going.

stories.title: Kuldeep, Vanshika host grand reception in Lucknow:Yogi Adityanath, Gautam Gambhir, Rishabh Pant, Jadeja attend ceremony
stories.summary: Indian cricket team spinner Kuldeep Yadav and his wife Vanshika held a grand reception ceremony in Lucknow on 17 March. The couple tied the knot on 14 March in Mussoorie, Uttarakhand, in an intimate ceremony attended only by close family members and relatives. A grand reception was held today at The Centrum, a five-star hotel in Lucknow, which was attended by guests from cricket and politics. Team India head coach Gautam Gambhir, Rishabh Pan, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Ravindra Jadeja were among the cricket figures who attended the ceremony. UP CM, Akhilesh Yadav also blessed couple The event was designed to reflect a royal theme, with extensive arrangements made for VVIP guests. Apart from personalities from the cricket fraternity, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also arrived and blessed the couple. See pics from Kuldeep-Vanshika's reception ceremony Kuldeep and Vanshika married in Mussoorie on 14 March Kuldeep married Vanshika, his childhood friend, in a dreamy ceremony in Mussoorie on 14 March. The event was also attended several cricket stars, which include Yuzvendra Chahal, Rinku Singh, Tilak Varma and Team India fielding coach T Dilip. Kuldeep was part of India's T20 World Cup-winning campaign. The chinaman bowler played just one match, against Pakistan where he took one wicket in three overs while conceding 14 runs. stories.summary: A former councillor was murdered while out on a morning walk in Gorakhpur. According to eyewitnesses, 4 attackers surrounded him and launched a knife attack. After being assaulted, former councillor Rajkumar Chauhan tried to escape and ran nearly 100 metres. However, the attackers chased him and stabbed him again. They repeatedly attacked him in the chest, head and hands. Eyewitnesses said the assailants waited at the spot for some time to ensure he had died before fleeing the scene. Family members rushed Rajkumar Chauhan to BRD Medical College, where doctors declared him dead. Initial reports suggest the attackers had parked their vehicle some distance away and reached the crime scene on foot. After receiving information about the incident, police reached the spot and began scanning CCTV footage from the surrounding areas. The incident took place in the Bargadwa area under the limits of Chiluatal Police Station. See images related to the incident- Rajkumar was only brother of 4 sisters Rajkumar Chauhan's father is Jangi Chauhan. Rajkumar was their only son. He had four sisters, all of whom are married. Rajkumar got married 18 years ago. He has two daughters and a son. He was preparing to contest the assembly elections in 2027. A youth said - Brother Rajkumar Chauhan has been shot. He was going to contest the assembly elections in 2027. When we used to meet him daily, we would discuss which places to go for campaigning.

stories.title: UP police officials clarify ‘Pandit’ option not a crime:Sub-Inspector exam paper not to be re-conducted; results to be released on time
stories.summary: Politics has intensified over the inclusion of the ‘Pandit’ option for opportunists in the UP Sub-Inspector recruitment exam, raising questions about action against those responsible. However, the recruitment board and its former officials believe no major action is likely, neither will the company be blacklisted nor treated as a criminal case, and results are expected on time. CM Yogi had directed the Police Recruitment Board to investigate the entire process, but no action has been taken so far. An investigation by Dainik Bhaskar examined the agency conducting the exam and identified the three key individuals responsible for adding the ‘Pandit’ option. First - Chairman of the Recruitment Board Second - Exam Controller of the Recruitment Board Third - Exam Conducting Agency Rules made in 2008, process kept confidential to prevent leaks After speaking with board officials, it came to light that the Chairman and the Examination Controller are not being held responsible for such irregularities. How is this possible? We spoke to Satyarth Aniruddha Pankaj, DIG of the Recruitment Board, about this. He says- Orders have been given to investigate the controversy that has arisen regarding the question. I want to state that the Police Recruitment Board does not set its own papers. It gets this work done by confidential agencies. To prevent paper leaks, no officer or employee of the board can see the paper. The sealed packets of the paper are opened for the first time at the center in the presence of 2 candidates. Action will be taken only after the investigation into the question and its options, which are causing controversy, is completed. Will the agency be blacklisted? Candidates are asking whether the agency conducting the UP Sub-Inspector exam will be blacklisted. Officials say the issue is not serious enough for that. Former DGP Sulkhan Singh adds that technically, there is no error in the question; it is being exaggerated, no crime has been committed, and results will be released on time. The recruitment board’s ongoing investigation report is still awaited. The exam will not be re-conducted, but a new SOP will be created to avoid questions on religion, caste, or community that may hurt sentiments. How is the agency that sets the paper decided? The recruitment board conducts a confidential tender process, inviting agencies from across the country and selecting one internally. Former DGP Sulkhan Singh says the paper-setting process is highly confidential, and even the board does not know the questions in advance. How do agencies prepare questions? Agencies hire subject matter experts. For 100 questions, around 200 are collected from different experts and used to prepare four sets of papers. Questions cover General Hindi, General Knowledge, Numerical and Mental Ability, and Law and Constitution, following the syllabus. Each question and its options are carefully checked for accuracy and clarity. How to ensure security during printing The question about 'Pandit Vikalp' is at the center of the controversy The question in the exam asked candidates to choose a word for someone who changes according to the occasion. The options were Virtuous, Pandit, Opportunist, and Sincere. An official linked to the recruitment board said it was a multiple-choice question, not a synonym question. In such questions, three options are usually incorrect, so linking the word ‘Pandit’ with ‘opportunist’ is not justified. However, the Brahmin community, BJP MLAs, and leaders strongly objected to including ‘Pandit’ as an option. They said the term is associated with knowledge, scholarship and religious respect, and linking it to opportunism insults the dignity of the community. Why did politics heat up? The controversy has also turned political. BJP leaders, including Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, and MLAs Shalabhmani Tripathi, P.N. Pathak, and Ramesh Mishra, objected to the question. Some issued statements, while others wrote letters to the Chief Minister demanding action. Senior journalist Siddharth Kalahans said the issue gained political traction because it surfaced at a time when many Brahmins already feel their identity is being hurt. He cited recent controversies involving BJP MLA meetings, UGC matters, the “corrupt Pandit” remark, Shankaracharya, and incidents like pulling the topknot of young Brahmins. As a result, BJP leaders raised the issue and wrote to the Chief Minister to control the damage, after which the CM termed the question wrong and ordered an investigation. stories.title: By-elections on 3 UP Assembly seats after April 10:Pending SIR list causes the delay; SP says, 'BJP is scared'
stories.summary: By-elections for three assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh could be held after April 10. According to Election Commission officials, polls cannot be conducted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls, so elections can only take place after the final voter list is released. The Election Commission had announced assembly elections for Assam, Kerala, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal on March 15, but did not declare dates for the UP by-elections. This triggered speculation that the polls for the three seats had been postponed. Experts say the commission currently has two options: By-elections are due for the Ghosi, Faridpur and Dudhi assembly seats. For Faridpur, the BJP has indicated it may field the son of its current MLA, Dr. Shyam Bihari. Meanwhile, the Samajwadi Party is preparing to nominate family members of the MLAs in Ghosi and Dudhi, aiming to use the sympathy factor. The SP is considered strong on both these seats. This raises key questions: Can the Election Commission postpone the by-elections? Which faces from the BJP and SP are likely to contest the three seats? And what preparations are both parties making for the upcoming contests? Read in this report Rules for by-elections Under the rules of the Election Commission of India, by-elections should be held within 6 months of a seat becoming vacant. There are 2 conditions for this- 1. If the term of the assembly seat remaining is more than 6 months, then by-elections are held. 2. According to Section 151 of the Representation of the People Act, the commission should conduct by-elections within 6 months if a seat becomes vacant. BJP, SP's preparations BJP leaders busy with Bengal elections After the announcement of West Bengal election dates, the BJP organisation is preparing to send several leaders there for campaigning, including CM Yogi, Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak. Meanwhile, the party’s local cadre is doing public outreach in the constituencies. Potential candidates have also been asked to connect with people and strengthen their political presence. SP leaders active, want by-elections soon SP leaders, on the other hand, want by-elections for all three seats to be held soon. The party sees these polls as a semi-final before the 2027 UP assembly elections. While the results may not significantly impact the assembly polls, they could influence the political atmosphere. SP leaders believe there is resentment among upper-caste voters against the BJP and want to test this factor in these elections. BSP not active; its entry may hurt SP more It is believed that the by-elections will mainly see a direct contest between SP and BJP. However, if the BSP fields candidates, it could hurt SP more than BJP. At present, BSP’s cadre does not appear active on any of the three seats. Words of BJP, SP leaders Victory on all three seats is certain BJP State Spokesperson Hero Bajpai says, The Election Commission of India decides the date for the by-election. BJP will contest the election with full might. It is certain that only BJP candidates will win on all three seats, including Duddhi and Ghosi. On the ground, our workers are active among the people. They are continuously reaching out to people and informing them about the work done during BJP's rule. SP leaders are feeling insecure. BJP is afraid of defeat SP's national spokesperson Ameeq Jamei says, BJP has already started fearing defeat. That's why they don't want to hold by-elections. In fact, BJP is troubled by the increasing strength of PDA. They know that if elections are held now, they will not be able to win even by using all means, fair or foul. This is why by-elections are being held in 8 states, but not in UP. Whereas three seats are vacant here. Why did 3 assembly seats become vacant? Who are the contenders? stories.title: Cricketer Rinku Singh offers prayers in Mathura:Visits Baglamukhi Devi temple, says ‘won the World Cup with the mother’s blessings’
stories.summary: Star cricketer Rinku Singh arrived in Mathura on Monday following India’s victory in the T20 World Cup 2026. He visited the Maa Baglamukhi Devi Temple, where he offered prayers and sought blessings. Speaking after the visit, Rinku said, “I had prayed for the team to win the World Cup. With the blessings of Maa Baglamukhi, we achieved victory.” He remained at the temple for around 45 minutes. BJP leader Yogesh Dwivedi accompanied him during the visit. India defeated New Zealand by 96 runs in the final held in Ahmedabad on 8 March. During the tournament, Rinku suffered a personal loss, as his father, Khanchand Singh, passed away. He had briefly returned to Aligarh to perform the last rites. See 2 pictures- Felicitation and temple rituals Before heading to the temple, Rinku visited the farmhouse of former municipal president Pushpa Sharma in Chhatikara. There, he was honoured with a shawl by Pushpa Sharma and Yogesh Dwivedi. Both congratulated him and the Indian team on their World Cup victory. At around noon, Rinku reached the temple near the old bus stand, where priest Neeraj Chaturvedi guided him through the rituals. He offered flowers, presented bhog (food offering), and lit a ceremonial lamp. Priests conducted a special puja with Vedic chants. During the ceremony, Rinku prayed for his family’s well-being and the prosperity of the nation. A large crowd gathered outside the temple to catch a glimpse of the cricketer. After completing the rituals, Rinku interacted with fans and posed for photographs. He expressed gratitude, saying that he had received immense love from people across the country and especially from the Braj region, adding that he would always cherish this support. Uttar Pradesh Ranji team player Ansh Dwivedi was also present. Later, Rinku visited a fuel station, where Indian Oil’s regional officer Lucky Gautam welcomed him with a bouquet. World Cup journey and performance Rinku Singh had not been part of the main squad during the 2024 World Cup and was included as a travelling reserve. However, he earned a place in the 2026 T20 World Cup squad, marking his debut in the tournament. He played five matches during the competition, scoring a total of 24 runs. Personal loss during the tournament Rinku’s father, Khanchand Singh, passed away on 27 February at 4:36 am in Aligarh. He had been battling stage-four liver cancer and was 60 years old. Rinku returned home for the funeral but rejoined Team India immediately afterwards. Following the World Cup victory, he shared an emotional message on Instagram- ‘Dad, today the trophy is in my hands, but you are not with me. Your dream has come true.’ He added that he would miss his father in every moment of joy and that his father’s teachings about duty had guided him on the field. Wedding plans with Priya Saroj Rinku Singh is engaged to Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj. Their wedding is scheduled for 2026, with earlier dates having been postponed twice, first due to a cricket series and then because of the World Cup. Sources indicate the wedding may now take place in May, depending on Rinku’s availability after the IPL season, expected between 26 March and 31 May. The ceremony is planned in Kashi, with a reception in Aligarh.

stories.title: Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak stands in line as patient:Spends an hour at Lucknow CHC, fumes over poor hygiene
stories.summary: Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak carried out a surprise inspection at Chinhat Community Health Centre (CHC) in Lucknow on Monday. To assess the situation firsthand, he wore a mask and joined the queue as an ordinary patient. He obtained an OPD slip and stood in line at both the pathology and medicine distribution counters. For nearly close to an hour, no one recognised him. During this time, he closely observed the functioning of the hospital and was visibly displeased with the level of cleanliness. Action over poor hygiene Disturbed by the unhygienic conditions, Pathak ordered a week’s payment of the cleaning agency to be withheld. He instructed officials that no staff member would be allowed to leave until the premises were properly cleaned. He also reprimanded the concerned officers for failing to maintain basic cleanliness standards in the hospital. Now see 3 pictures- Anger over ward conditions During the inspection, the Deputy CM expressed strong displeasure over the condition of the wards. Several beds in the general ward were found without bedsheets, and overall cleanliness was lacking. He warned officials that negligence in patient care would not be tolerated. Notices were ordered to be issued to those responsible, and strict action was promised if conditions did not improve promptly. Review of pathology and facilities Pathak then visited the pathology department, where he noticed a long queue of patients. He asked the technician about the time required to collect a blood sample and directed that the process be expedited to reduce waiting time. Dust and dirt were also observed near the X-ray room, prompting immediate instructions for cleaning. He further inspected supplies by opening a cupboard and checking the stock available. Inspection of OPD and general ward In OPD Room No. 5, the Deputy CM spoke with doctors about patient load and hospital arrangements. Upon reaching General Ward No. 28, he was angered by the conditions, beds without sheets and poor hygiene. He also inspected the toilets and directed officials to ensure immediate improvement in sanitation facilities. Issues in drinking water facilities The inspection revealed shortcomings in drinking water arrangements as well. Dirt was found around the RO system, and pipes were improperly tied with a net. Expressing dissatisfaction, Pathak emphasised that there would be no compromise on cleanliness and essential facilities in the hospital. Concerns raised by ASHA workers During the visit, ASHA workers undergoing training in the auditorium informed him that their mobile phones were not functioning, affecting their work. In response, the Deputy CM immediately contacted Chief Medical Officer Dr. NB Singh and instructed that the devices be repaired or replaced without delay. He also directed that any pending payments to ASHA workers be cleared promptly. Strict instructions to officials Pathak instructed the CMO to reach the CHC immediately and resolve all issues. He warned officials not to leave the hospital until all arrangements were fully corrected. Observing a long queue at the medicine counter, he directed the CHC Superintendent to streamline the process, stating that patients should receive medicines within five minutes.

stories.title: BJP groups clash in Aligarh:12 bullets fired, three shot in market area
stories.summary: A violent clash broke out between two groups linked to the Bharatiya Janata Party in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh. The groups opened fire at each other in a busy market, and 3 people were injured. 12 rounds fired in 23 seconds The incident took place on March 12 in Sarai Hakim market. According to police, around 12 rounds were fired within just 23 seconds, causing panic and chaos in the area. A video of the incident surfaced on Thursday. So far, 13 accused have been arrested and sent to jail. Police are using the video to identify other suspects. See 2 pictures Fight started over Instagram reel Police said the clash began over an argument on Instagram. Harshad Hindu and Mahesh Sharma, both associated with the BJP youth wing, had a dispute after a comment was made on a reel. The argument escalated into abuse over a phone call and later turned violent. One group allegedly assaulted a person named Mohit Sharma earlier, which further increased tensions. Gunfight in market area On the evening of March 12, both groups gathered again in the market and opened fire at each other. In the video, one injured person can be seen falling on the road while others try to help him. Attackers were also seen firing from narrow lanes. Three injured, some arrested Three people were injured in the firing: Police later arrested injured accused Shoaib Ahmad and Shanu Valmiki after their treatment and sent them to jail. Search for main accused continues Police said the accused had gathered on Harshad’s call. They are now searching for main suspects, including Mohit Sharma, Aman Pandit, Prakhar Rathi, and Mannu Pandit. SP City Mrigank Shekhar Pathak said that strict action will be taken, and illegal activities linked to both groups will also be investigated.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:‘No tolerance for disruption during festivals’ warns CM Yogi; BJP releases second list for WB assembly elections more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. BJP List 2 for WB polls out, former MoS Nisith Pramanik get tickets The Bharatiya Janata Party has announced candidates for 111 Assembly seats in West Bengal in its latest list. Rekha Patra, who did not contest from Sandeshkhali this time, has been fielded from Hingalganj. Former Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Nisith Pramanik has been nominated from Mathabhanga. 2. President Droupadi Murmu visits Ayodhya, offer prayers at Ram Temple President Droupadi Murmu visited the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on the first day of Navratri, where she offered prayers to Ram Lalla. She also installed the Shri Ram Yantra in the Ram Darbar located on the second floor and took a round of the temple premises. 3. Three departments responsible for Green Corridor road collapse The Green Corridor road sank 5 feet due to sewer leakage just 2 days after inauguration in Lucknow. The road caved in near Khatu Shyam Temple on Birbal Sahani Marg. LDA officials kept insisting this was part of the ramp adjacent to the Green Corridor. 4. Iran plans collecting tolls from shipping through Strait of Hormuz The US-Israel-Iran conflict has entered its 20th day, with both military and economic tensions escalating rapidly. A Washington Post report claims the Pentagon is seeking nearly $200 billion to sustain operations, signalling the growing cost of the war. 5. Will Varun Gandhi get a new role after meeting Modi?, absent from UP politics for two years Varun Gandhi entered politics and won the Pilibhit Lok Sabha seat in 2019. In 2014, he contested from Sultanpur and secured victory again by a margin of nearly 1.75 lakh votes. Just before the 2009 election, during a speech in Pilibhit, Varun made a controversial remark, stating that if anyone targeted Hindus or considered them leaderless, he would retaliate strongly, invoking the Gita. 6. ‘No tolerance for disruption during festivals’, says CM Yogi Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that no disturbance of any kind will be tolerated during festivals. Strict action will be taken against those who disrupt the atmosphere. Criminals should fear the police uniform. Festivals should be celebrated only within the bounds of tradition; no new traditions will be permitted. 7. Indian Railways crack down on unauthorised vendors Indian Railways has rolled out QR code-enabled identity cards and digitally traceable food packaging to eliminate unauthorised vending and ensure verified catering services onboard trains. Unauthorised hawking in passenger areas is prohibited and punishable under Section 144 of the Railways Act, 1989. 8. Supreme Court slams Barabanki toll clash; calls lawyer ‘brave’ who represented toll workers 'The behaviour of Barabanki Bar Association members is extremely sad and shameful. This is not the legal profession, but open hooliganism. This incident shows the declining state of the legal profession. Such violence can never be acceptable in the name of lawyers' fraternity (brotherhood).' This stern comment was made by the Supreme Court regarding a case related to a dispute at a toll plaza in Barabanki. 9. Army Major marries Captain bride by taking ₹1 as token-gift An Indian Army Major married a Captain (female) by taking just ₹1 as a token gift in Saharanpur. As per tradition, he only took one coconut. The groom said he had decided during his student life not to take a dowry. However, due to security reasons, information about where both are posted is not available. 10. Ajit Agarkar urges BCCI to extend tenure till 2027 WC Men's senior selection committee's chairman Ajit Agarkar is looking for another extension from BCCI after Team India successfully defended the T20 World Cup trophy at home this year on 8 March. Notably, after Men in Blue won the 2024 T20 World Cup and 2025 Champions Trophy, the Board of Control for Cricket in India rewarded the ex-cricketer with a one-year extension. For India's white-ball dominance, Agarkar's contract got extended from August 2025 to June 2026.

stories.title: 42-year-old man dies after jumping from 13th floor:Mother’s 3-day-old body found inside flat in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: A 42-year-old man died by suicide after jumping from the 13th floor of a residential building in Ghaziabad. When police later entered his flat, they found the body of his 70-year-old mother, which was believed to be 2–3 days old. The incident took place in the Mahagunpuram Society in the Kavinagar police station area. The man, identified as Rajveer Singh, lived in a ground-floor flat (No. 028). According to police, Rajveer first went to the 13th floor and then jumped through the duct area. He hit an iron shed on the way down and fell to the ground, seriously injured. A security guard nearby heard a loud noise and rushed to the spot. He found Rajveer lying in a pool of blood and raised an alarm, after which residents gathered and informed the police. First 2 pictures Mother’s body found inside flat When police entered Rajveer’s flat, they noticed a strong foul smell. Inside, they found the body of his mother, Satnam Kaur. Police said the body appeared to be around 2–3 days old, and no visible injury marks were found. Investigation ongoing Both bodies have been sent for postmortem to determine the exact cause of death. Police are investigating whether the mother died of natural causes and what led Rajveer to take this step. Family background Rajveer got married about 12 years ago. He was reportedly unemployed. His wife lives separately in Crossing Republic with their 10-year-old son. Local residents said they usually saw Rajveer coming and going, but his mother was rarely seen. Police are continuing the investigation to understand the full circumstances behind the incident.

stories.title: UP to hike salary of outsourced workers:Peons, translators and other staff see major payment boost
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government, led by Yogi Adityanath, has increased the salaries of around 200,000 outsourcing employees. The salary hike ranges from ₹8,000 to ₹11,000. Major salary changes The revised salaries will be effective from April. Additional benefits introduced Apart from the salary increase, employees will now also receive: Budget allocation increased The Chief Minister had announced this decision in the Assembly. The government has increased the department’s budget by ₹426 crore, taking the total allocation to ₹2,223.84 crore. New corporation for transparent recruitment The government has also set up the Uttar Pradesh Outsource Service Corporation (UPCOS). From now on, all outsourcing recruitments in the state will be done through this body to ensure transparency. Earlier, different agencies handled hiring on a contract basis, which often led to exploitation of workers, delayed payments, and unfair wages. Reservation Policy to be implemented The government has also introduced reservation in outsourcing jobs: This move aims to ensure fair opportunities and address concerns raised by the opposition regarding lack of reservation in outsourcing jobs.

stories.title: Temple videos shared with Pakistan:2 youths caught in Hapur for espionage, SP confirms network active since 2025
stories.summary: Two young men have been arrested from Hapur district in Uttar Pradesh for allegedly spying for Pakistan. The arrests were made by a team of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) from Delhi. According to police, both suspects had been active since 2025. Police said the accused were in contact with a Pakistan-based gangster named Shahzad Bhatti through social media. They shared photos, videos, and locations of sensitive places, including temples and nearby areas. Hapur SP K.G. Singh stated that the accused—Azeem Rana and Azad Rajput—had sent videos of Sanatan Dharma Temple in Delhi, Ravana Temple in Greater Noida, and other nearby locations to their handler in Pakistan. Contact started via social media Investigations revealed that the contact began in 2025 through Instagram. Later, they also used Telegram and WhatsApp to stay connected. The accused were reportedly lured with money to share sensitive information. The police also found that they conducted reconnaissance (surveying) of places like Ramesh Nagar Metro Station, temples, and other public locations. On February 19, 2026, they shared multiple videos and photos. Family connection between accused Azeem Rana is from Dhaulana in Hapur, while Azad Rajput is from a village in Meerut. Azad is Azeem’s nephew. Their mobile phones contained several videos and images sent to the Pakistani handler. Case registered, investigation ongoing Police have registered a case against both accused and are questioning them further to uncover more details about the network. Who is Shahzad Bhatti? Shahzad Bhatti is believed to be a major gangster with links to international crime networks. He is reportedly involved in illegal arms trade and has connections across several countries, including Europe, the UK, the US, Canada, and Dubai. Reports suggest that he was once banned by the Pakistani government but later returned to Pakistan in May 2025. His exact current location is unknown.

stories.title: Elderly woman kept under digital arrest for 6 days:₹21 lakh duped; fraudsters say, 'You are involved with terrorists, your house will be sealed'
stories.summary: "This is Gujarat Police Commissioner speaking... 26 people lost their lives in a terrorist attack in Gujarat. Investigation has revealed that you are involved with militants and terrorists... You will be sent to jail, your house will be sealed... Until the investigation is complete, you must keep your mobile camera on; you have been digitally arrested... " Using such statements, cyber fraudsters digitally arrested an elderly woman from Kidwai Nagar for 6 days and swindled ₹21 lakh from her. Elderly woman lives alone after her husband's death Snehlata, a resident of Kidwai Nagar, said that she lives alone in a rented house. Her husband had passed away, and her son and daughter live elsewhere. She mentioned that some time ago, she had sold her LIG house in Vikas Sadan, Delhi and land in Krishnanagar, Kanpur, and the money received from these sales was deposited in her accounts. On the morning of March 10th, she received a call for the first time, where the caller threatened by mentioning involvement in a terrorist incident. After a while, they pressured her to accept a video call, saying they would send police to the house. When she answered the phone, a police officer appeared sitting in his office. He identified himself as the Gujarat Police Commissioner and spoke to them very rudely. ₹20 lakhs transferred from account on March 13th It is alleged that the fraudsters transferred ₹20 lakh from their State Bank of India account on March 13th. After this, on March 16th, they withdrew ₹50 thousand, ₹49 thousand, and ₹1 thousand through RTGS. Then the accused stopped calling. Snehlata said that they have a house in the city. There were talks about selling it. They had to go out regarding this matter. While the accused would stop them from going outside or having visitors, when they mentioned making a house deal for ₹80 lakhs, the accused let them go. Those people asked when the ₹80 lakhs would come, but she avoided answering. DCP Dipendra Nath Chaudhary said that a report has been filed. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Census from May 22; house counting in first phase:First-ever digital, caste census; self-enumeration option available
stories.summary: The first phase of the census will begin in Kanpur from May 22. House counting will be done from May 22 to June 20. During this time, it will be determined how many houses are in the district. Additionally, the second phase will begin in February 2027, in which citizens will be counted. For the first time, castes will also be observed in the census. Data will also be prepared showing how many citizens belong to each caste. Personnel engaged in the census will have to upload all data on the CMMS portal. For the first time in the country, the census is being conducted in digital format. Self-enumeration option for citizens for the first time DM Jitendra Pratap Singh said that in the first phase of the census, house listing and house counting will be done, and in the second phase, population counting will be conducted. He informed that this time's census will be completely digital and for the first time, citizens have been given the option of self-enumeration. He mentioned that 15 days prior to the census, citizens will be able to conduct their own enumeration through the Census Self-Enumeration Portal and app. Any ordinary resident can perform self-enumeration by filling out the online questionnaire. 33 details will be recorded During the house-listing phase, surveyors will record 33 types of details related to building usage, construction materials, number of rooms, ownership status, availability of water, electricity, and toilets, types of cooking fuel, and assets like phones, vehicles, and televisions.

stories.title: Army Major marries Captain bride by taking ₹1 as token-gift:Saharanpur groom says, 'I had decided in student life itself to have dowry-free marriage'
stories.summary: An Indian Army Major married a Captain (female) by taking just ₹1 as a token gift in Saharanpur. As per tradition, he only took one coconut. The groom said he had decided during his student life not to take a dowry. However, due to security reasons, information about where both are posted is not available. Meanwhile, the groom's father said that my son has not brought a daughter-in-law but a daughter. The brightness of our house has increased with the arrival of a daughter. We didn't want dowry anyway. What could be a bigger dowry than getting a daughter in the form of a daughter-in-law? This entire matter is from Meerpur village in the Sarsawa area. See 2 pictures of the wedding… The groom's family took ₹1 as token of blessing Chaudhary Ompal Singh, a resident of Meerpur village, has retired from the Indian Army. He is also the Joint Secretary of Sarsawa Arya Jat Samaj Development Committee. He conducted his son Madhur Chaudhary's marriage without dowry on March 16, 2026. Madhur got married to Jyoti Saurot from Brajmandal, where only ₹1 was taken as a token gift. Madhur's family members said that information related to his posting remains confidential, as permission is required from the army for this. Madhur was commissioned into the Indian Army after passing out from the Indian Military Academy, Dehradun, in 2018. Meanwhile, his wife Jyoti Saurot is a 2019 pass-out. Families met during a religious journey The groom's relatives say Madhur's parents had gone to Mathura on a religious journey. Jyoti's family members were also part of that journey. During the conversation, Jyoti's family mentioned that they were looking for a good match for their daughter. That's when Madhur's mother mentioned that her son is in government service. He is working as a Major in the army. After this, conversations between both families began, and gradually this relationship progressed to marriage. Mother-in-law says we consider her daughter, not daughter-in-law Major Madhur Chaudhary's mother, Rekha Chaudhary, says, ‘The daughter-in-law has come to my house like Goddess Lakshmi’. From day one, we have treated her not as a daughter-in-law, but like a daughter. We are very happy. The kind of life partner Madhur wanted for his son, he has found exactly such a daughter. We pray that their married life is always filled with happiness. Father-in-law says, ‘Daughter-in-law is more valuable than dowry’ Chaudhary Ompal Singh said that for us, the daughter-in-law is the biggest dowry. Many prestigious families approached for marriage, but they had already made a resolution to marry without dowry. Wealth comes and goes, but a cultured daughter connects two families. Major Madhur Chaudhary said that I had decided during my student life that I wouldn't take dowry. I made this decision after reading news about broken relationships and scattered families due to dowry. I also appeal to the youth to respect their parents' values. Come forward to bring positive change in society.

stories.title: Will Varun Gandhi get a new role after meeting Modi?:Absent from UP politics for two years, has not visited Pilibhit since 2024
stories.summary: Varun Gandhi entered politics and won the Pilibhit Lok Sabha seat in 2019. In 2014, he contested from Sultanpur and secured victory again by a margin of nearly 1.75 lakh votes. Just before the 2009 election, during a speech in Pilibhit, Varun made a controversial remark, stating that if anyone targeted Hindus or considered them leaderless, he would retaliate strongly, invoking the Gita. Statements like these significantly boosted his visibility in Uttar Pradesh, establishing him as a prominent Hindutva face. With the BJP forming the government at the Centre and Narendra Modi becoming Prime Minister, speculation intensified in Uttar Pradesh that Varun could emerge as Chief Minister if the party won the 2017 Assembly elections. Posters projecting him as a ‘future Chief Minister’ appeared in cities like Prayagraj. Sidelined after BJP’s rise in Uttar Pradesh Despite the BJP’s victory in 2017, Yogi Adityanath was appointed Chief Minister. Thereafter, Varun Gandhi’s political prominence gradually declined. By 2019, he was excluded from the list of star campaigners and removed from the party’s national executive. In 2024, he was denied a party ticket altogether, effectively halting his electoral political activity. On 17 March 2026, Varun met Prime Minister Modi, reigniting discussions about his political future. Questions are now being raised about whether he will be assigned a new role or fielded strategically against opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi. Differences with party leadership Varun Gandhi has long been considered close to Rajnath Singh and reportedly favoured him as a prime ministerial candidate. During a rally in Kolkata addressed by Modi, Varun publicly criticised the crowd’s “Modi-Modi” chants, questioning their appropriateness. Although the rally was deemed successful, Varun described it as a failure the following day. After Modi became Prime Minister and Amit Shah replaced Rajnath Singh as BJP president, Varun’s position weakened. He was subsequently removed from the post of general secretary. Increasingly rebellious image Despite winning Pilibhit again in 2019, Varun adopted a more independent stance, often deviating from the party line. Four major incidents reinforced his image as a dissenter- Meeting with PM Modi On 17 March 2026, Varun shared a photograph with Prime Minister Modi, his wife Yamini Roy, and daughter Anasuya. He described the meeting as a privilege, praising Modi’s “paternal affection” and calling him a true guardian of the nation. Experts see an attempt at political rehabilitation Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi views the meeting as an attempt by Varun Gandhi to regain political relevance. He argues that Varun had earlier opposed Modi through speeches and writings, especially during the farmers’ protests, even aligning with opposition narratives. Tripathi suggests Varun may have anticipated a decline in Modi’s political dominance by 2024. However, when that did not materialise, he was left with limited options. He also notes that Modi’s strategy often includes maintaining a Gandhi family member outside Congress, which serves as a symbolic counterpoint. However, experts believe Varun is unlikely to be given a major role in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 elections, though a position within the party structure remains possible. Internal factors behind marginalisation Journalist Keshav Agarwal highlights two key reasons for Varun’s sidelining- Congress option rejected At one stage, Varun explored joining Congress. However, Rahul Gandhi reportedly declined the proposal. Analysts suggest Rahul may have viewed Varun as a politically mature rival whose inclusion could complicate internal dynamics. Political legacy shaped by early loss Born on 13 March 1980 in Delhi, Varun Gandhi faced early personal tragedies. His father, Sanjay Gandhi, died in a plane crash when he was three months old. At age four, he lost his grandmother, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. Raised by Maneka Gandhi, Varun was introduced to politics in Pilibhit in 1999. He joined the BJP in 2004 and quickly rose through the ranks. Aggressive image and decline Between 2012 and 2017, during the Samajwadi Party government in Uttar Pradesh, Varun gained popularity through aggressive speeches, particularly in western UP and Rohilkhand. He even publicly rejected Mahatma Gandhi’s principle of non-violence in one speech. Although he built a strong support base, this assertive style, combined with internal dissent against party leadership, gradually distanced him from mainstream BJP politics. His recent meeting with Modi signals an attempt to reclaim lost ground in a rapidly evolving political landscape.

stories.title: President Droupadi Murmu visits Ayodhya:Offer prayers at Ram Temple and attend Shri Ram Yantra consecration ceremony
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu visited the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on the first day of Navratri, where she offered prayers to Ram Lalla. She also installed the Shri Ram Yantra in the Ram Darbar located on the second floor and took a round of the temple premises. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath briefed the President about the ongoing temple construction work. The President arrived at Ayodhya airport around 10:30 AM from Delhi, where she was received by Governor Anandiben Patel and the Chief Minister. This is the President’s second visit to Ayodhya after the consecration of Ram Lalla. Earlier, she had visited on May 1, 2024, when she offered prayers at Hanumangarhi and the Ram Temple. The President is scheduled to stay in Ayodhya for around five hours before leaving for Mathura at 3 PM. In Mathura, she will visit ISKCON and Prem Mandir. On Friday, March 20, she will meet Premanand Maharaj. During her visit, she performed aarti at the Ram Temple. Her granddaughters, Adyashree and Nityashree, also accompanied her to the temple and were seen offering prayers. The President also inspected the temple premises, while the Chief Minister shared details about the construction work. To welcome the President, cultural programmes were organised at 20 locations between the airport and the temple, with around 250 artists giving performances. About the Ram Yantra The Ram Yantra was prepared at a monastery in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu. It was then brought to Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh and later reached Ayodhya through a chariot procession about 10 days ago. The Yantra weighs around 150 kg and is plated with gold. According to Ayodhya astrologer Raghunath Das Shastri, the Ram Yantra is a special Vedic geometric structure. It symbolises divine energy, with the presence of Lord Ram and other deities established through sacred chants and patterns, and is considered highly auspicious.
