stories.title: No tolerance for disruption during festivals, says CM Yogi:Police told to stay alert, increase patrolling, extra vigilance at crowded and religious places
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said no disruption will be tolerated during festivals, warning of strict action against those attempting to disturb communal harmony. He stressed that criminals must fear the police uniform. The CM also directed that festivals be celebrated strictly within traditional norms, adding that no new practices will be allowed. These remarks came during a review meeting on preparations for Navratri and Eid, attended virtually by commissioners, district magistrates, and police chiefs on Wednesday evening. The DGP informed the Chief Minister that the police are fully alert to ensure the peaceful completion of the festivals. Patrolling has also been increased. Referring to recent criminal incidents, the CM said; Peace and security must be ensured at all costs. Negligence at any level will not be accepted. Even a single criminal incident spoils the atmosphere of the entire society. Therefore, every complaint and every incident should be taken seriously. Read CM's important statements On gas shortage says, ‘Keep strict watch on black marketing’ Regarding LPG supply, the CM said that despite international conditions, common people should not face any problems. Strict watch should be kept on hoarding and black marketing. Strict action should be taken against the culprits, and people's problems should be resolved immediately. 'Sound of loudspeakers at religious places should remain within set standards' Citing Supreme Court directions, Yogi said that the volume of loudspeakers at religious places should be kept within prescribed limits. Strict action should be taken to remove them if the rules are violated. Expressing displeasure over bike stunts, he directed them to stop it immediately. 'Exercise additional vigilance at major temples during Navratri' The Chief Minister said that during Chaitra Navratri, complete arrangements should be made for security, cleanliness, crowd management, drinking water, lighting, and health services, keeping in mind the crowd of devotees in Devi temples. Additional vigilance should be maintained at major temples and crowded areas. 'Cow shelter facilities will be improved' The Chief Minister directed to further improve the arrangements of destitute cow shelters. He asked to ensure the deployment of nodal officers, the timely payment of funds, the protection of cattle, fodder, and other necessary facilities.

stories.title: Storms hit Mathura-Sambhal; hoardings and trees fall:Drizzle in Ghaziabad, rain alert in 23 districts of UP
stories.summary: The weather has changed once again in UP. Late-night rain with storms occurred in Ghaziabad, Hathras, Sambhal, and Noida. In Mathura, strong winds knocked down hoardings on the road. Trees and electricity poles were also uprooted in many places. Standing crops have also been damaged. A house roof collapsed. Strong winds also blew in Sambhal. In Ghaziabad, it rained intermittently at night. There was also light drizzle on Thursday morning. The meteorological department estimates 3 millimeters of rainfall. The temperature here dropped by 4 degrees Celsius in 24 hours. Clouds have also been covering Noida since morning. The meteorological department has issued a rain alert with thunderstorms in 23 districts of the state today, Thursday. Hail is expected in 6 districts. During this time, winds can also blow at speeds of 40 to 60 km/h. According to the meteorological department, the weather will remain like this for the next 3 days till March 21. If we talk about Wednesday, Banda was the hottest, where the maximum temperature was recorded at 39.6 degrees. Dust storms occurred in Bulandshahr and Agra. Watch the visuals of storm and rain... Why did the weather change, know here Lucknow meteorologist Atul Singh said - A western disturbance has become active near Afghanistan from today. Its effect is visible up to UP. The weather has changed due to this. Its greater effect will be seen from March 20. Due to rain, the maximum temperature may drop by 5 to 7 degrees. How will the weather be for 3 days? March 20 - The effect of a western disturbance will be seen across the state. Many districts may experience rain with strong winds. There is also a possibility of hail. March 21 - There may be rain in some districts of Western-Eastern UP. Winds will blow at a speed of 40 km per hour. The temperature may drop by 2-3 degrees. March 22 - Most districts of Western-Eastern UP will remain cloudy. There may be rain in some places. Strong winds will also blow. Wheat and pigeon pea crops will be damaged. How can they be protected? Agricultural experts say that rain and strong winds can affect rabi, zaid, and horticultural crops. Currently, pods are forming in pigeon pea, mustard, chickpea, peas, green gram, and groundnut. Grains are filling. Strong winds can cause pods to split. Grains can fall off. Wheat crop can also fall due to strong winds, which poses a risk of reduced yield. In vegetables, flowers, and small fruits of okra, tomato, bottle gourd, cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon, eggplant, and chili can fall. Farmers have been advised to immediately harvest crops that are ripe and store them in a safe place. Do not let water accumulate in the fields; arrange proper drainage for this.

stories.title: 3 departments responsible for Green Corridor road collapse:Water line relocated; sewer line left untouched to cut costs
stories.summary: The Green Corridor road sank 5 feet due to sewer leakage just 2 days after inauguration in Lucknow. The road caved in near Khatu Shyam Temple on Birbal Sahani Marg. LDA officials kept insisting this was part of the ramp adjacent to the Green Corridor. However, Jal Kal department officials say that LDA was advised about sewer line shifting before the Green Corridor construction began. This was ignored due to rushed work and budget constraints. During construction, local residents had informed the construction workers about the leakage. Despite this, the sewer line was not fixed properly, while 2 drinking water lines were shifted. The Jal Kal department had not given any information about line shifting to Jal Nigam who was handling maintenance. There was a lack of coordination between all departments and officials. This negligence occurred as a result. Note that Defense Minister Rajnath Singh and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the Green Corridor on March 13. The road caved in on March 15. These 3 are responsible for road cave-in... First - Lucknow Development Authority Phase-2 of the Green Corridor has been constructed by the Lucknow Development Authority. After the road collapsed, people told the Jal Nigam and Jalkal Department's working agency, Suez India, who arrived at the spot, that there was a leakage here when the road was being constructed. At that time, LDA did not pay attention to this and widened the road. Leakage occurred due to the compressor machine pressure After the road collapsed, the engineers working and local people said that when the compressor machine was running during road construction. The leakage occurred due to its pressure. Initially, the leakage was minor, but later it became larger. Due to which the road sank about 5 feet. The line had to be fixed by digging a hole about 20 feet deep. However, after the road collapsed, LDA said that it had nothing to do with corridor construction. A team led by Upper Secretary Gyanendra Verma also inspected and said that the green corridor is safe. Second - Jal Nigam Jal Nigam is responsible for the maintenance of sewer lines. Local residents told the officials who reached the spot that during road construction, they were informed about the leakage, but they did not pay attention. Due to this, a small problem became big. On the Jalkal department's advice regarding line shifting, Chief Engineer of Jal Nigam Shamim Akhtar said that Jal Nigam was not given any information in this matter. Two drinking water lines were shifted. Its proposal had also come. No information or proposal was provided by the Water Works Department regarding this. Only the Water Works GM had gone to the meeting held before making the corridor. Upon inquiring about the leakage, he said that the line runs under pressure in the rising line. Information is only known when water comes out. Regarding the cost of line shifting, officials say that if the line is crossing along with the road, the work gets done in a lower budget. If the line runs alongside, it costs more. Now, Jal Nigam will ask Sewage India to bring such equipment that can detect leakage in the rising main line. Third - Water works department Lucknow Jal Kal Department had advised LDA to shift the sewer line, but LDA ignored it in the rush of work. Meanwhile, Jal Nigam, which is looking after the maintenance work, said they have no information about any such proposal. In this situation, the question arises whether the Jal Kal department merely went through the motions in the name of giving advice for line shifting? Jal Kal department's GM Kuldeep Singh said that a large sewer line is going from the Kukrail pumping station. There was also a discussion about shifting this sewer line. However, due to it being a large line, the cost would be higher. Because of this, this proposal was postponed. Read now how the road will be built... LDA itself has to do the back-filling There was a gap in the pipeline joint in the Green Corridor, which caused water leakage. The Jal Nigam and Suez India teams have resolved the problem. Now, the Lucknow Development Authority will carry out the backfilling of this pit. Road construction will also be completed by the same department. Local residents have informed Suez India and Jal Nigam that when the road was being constructed, they had informed the working officers and employees about the water leakage. They were asked to inform the concerned department so that this problem could be resolved, but despite all this, the road construction work was carried out.

stories.title: First look of Asia's largest Noida Airport:Ganga Ghat-style entry and automatic baggage drop boxes
stories.summary: The Noida International Airport being built in Jewar, UP is ready for your journey. In the first phase, work on one terminal and runway built on 3300 acres has been completed. Only finishing remains. With one runway, this terminal will have an annual capacity to handle 30 million passengers. The cost of the airport's first phase is about 11 thousand crores. PM Modi will inaugurate it on 28 March. After completion of all 4 phases, it will be Asia's largest and world's sixth largest airport. However, the deadline for complete construction is 2040. Bhaskar is the first to reach inside this airport. Read all the important information... 1. Terminal Building 2. Entry Gate 3. Departure Area 4. Self Baggage Drop Facility 5. Security Check 6. Boarding Area 7. Lounge Area 8. Temple of Bells 9. Aerobridge 10. Security Special Features of Noida Airport 1. Asia's Largest Airport in Terms of Runways Noida International Airport will have 5 runways. A sixth runway may also be constructed here. After this, it will become Asia's largest and world's sixth largest airport. In terms of runways, China's Shanghai Pudong International Airport is currently the largest in Asia. 2. Also Asia's Largest in Terms of Area Noida International Airport is proposed to be built on a total area of 52 square kilometers. If this happens, it will become Asia's largest airport in terms of area as well. Currently, China's Beijing Daxing International Airport is Asia's largest airport with an area of 47 square kilometers. 3. Will be the country's largest airport after completion Yamuna Development Authority has allotted 3300 acres of land for the first stage of Noida Airport. This area is approximately 13.35 square kilometers. In the second stage, the total area of the airport will increase to about 7200 acres or 29 square kilometers. Currently, the country's largest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad, which is built on approximately 5500 acres or 22.25 square kilometers. Inauguration on March 28, First Flight in April PM Modi will inaugurate the Noida International Airport on March 28. However, flights will begin in April. Officials associated with the Noida Airport Authority said that fares have not been decided yet, but they could be lower compared to Delhi airport as the development charges for airlines have been kept lower here.

stories.title: Mother wanted euthanasia for Harish, father initially resisted:Brahmakumari's sister says his karmic journey is complete
stories.summary: 'You are like a bird trapped in a cage of sorrow and pain. The time has come for you to fly free.' These were the words of Brahmakumari Sister Lovely as she bid an emotional farewell to Harish Rana in Ghaziabad. Harish, who has been in a coma for 13 years, is currently at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences after the Supreme Court of India permitted passive euthanasia on his parents’ petition. Medical condition and current status Harish has been taken off oxygen support, and food and water have also been withheld for the past two days. Previously, he was being fed through a tube. A team of doctors at AIIMS is monitoring his condition continuously. Meanwhile, his parents remain in a hospital ward, praying for a peaceful and painless passing for their son. SC approval and transfer to AIIMS On 11 March, the Supreme Court granted permission for euthanasia. Subsequently, on 14 March, Harish was shifted from his residence in Raj Empire Society, Raj Nagar, Ghaziabad, to AIIMS Delhi. At the time of his departure, Sister Lovely, associated with the Brahmakumari organisation, offered spiritual support and performed a farewell ritual with the family. Family’s internal conflict over Euthanasia According to Sister Lovely, Harish’s father, Ashok Rana, was initially opposed to euthanasia, believing in a natural death. However, his mother, Nirmala, had a different perspective. She had expressed her wish for euthanasia nearly four years ago, stating that she could no longer bear to see her son’s suffering. She sought Sister Lovely’s help in convincing her husband. Over time, with counselling and emotional support, the father and other family members came to accept the decision. The family then pursued legal recourse, taking the matter from the High Court to the Supreme Court. Long association with Brahmakumaris Sister Lovely stated that the Rana family had been associated with the Prajapita Brahmakumari Ishwariya Vishwavidyalaya for 18 years. About five years ago, they began attending daily one-hour classes at her centre in Rajnagar Extension, which strengthened their connection. It was during this association that she became personally involved in the family’s struggle and their eventual decision regarding euthanasia. Harish’s condition over the years Sister Lovely described Harish as a “pure soul” whose karmic journey had been fulfilled. Despite being in a coma, his eyes often remained open, and he occasionally coughed or showed minor responses. However, there was no movement in the rest of his body. Over the years, his physical condition deteriorated severely. His body became extremely frail, with bones visibly protruding. His parents and younger brother Ashish cared for him tirelessly, even helping him sit upright at times. Emotional moments before transfer A video from 14 March shows Sister Lovely applying a sandalwood tilak on Harish’s forehead and gently telling him to forgive everyone and seek forgiveness before departing. Family members were visibly emotional. Harish’s father apologised to relatives, saying he was taking this step despite personal reluctance. Family’s struggle and silence The Rana family moved to Ghaziabad about six years ago, after previously living in Delhi for over a decade. Since Harish’s transfer to AIIMS, a deep silence has enveloped the household. Neighbours say the father has withdrawn from social interactions. Harish’s mother and sister continue to grieve, recalling years of caregiving. His mother shared how she would speak to him daily, hoping for even the slightest response, a blink, a yawn, or a twitch, just to feel he was still present. Accident and diagnosis Harish, originally from Delhi, was pursuing a B.Tech at Punjab University in Chandigarh. In 2013, during his final semester, he fell from the fourth floor of his hostel. The accident left him paralysed and in a coma. Doctors diagnosed him with Quadriplegia, a condition in which survival often depends on ventilatory and assisted feeding support. Recovery chances in such cases are extremely limited. Over time, prolonged immobility also led to severe bedsores, further worsening his condition, making the family’s emotional and physical burden increasingly difficult to bear.

Not advocacy, but open hooliganism:Supreme Court slams Barabanki toll clash; calls lawyer ‘brave’ who represented toll workers
stories.summary: 'The behavior of Barabanki Bar Association members is extremely sad and shameful. This is not the legal profession, but open hooliganism. This incident shows the declining state of the legal profession. Such violence can never be acceptable in the name of lawyers' fraternity (brotherhood).' This stern comment was made by the Supreme Court regarding a case related to a dispute at a toll plaza in Barabanki. The bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta ordered the transfer of the entire case from Barabanki to Delhi's Tis Hazari Court. The Supreme Court also praised lawyer Manoj Shukla, who fought the case despite pressure. Now know complete matter On January 14, 2026, a dispute over toll occurred between lawyer Ratnesh Shukla and toll workers at Haidargarh toll plaza in Barabanki. The toll workers had assaulted lawyer Ratnesh Shukla. A video of this incident had also surfaced. After the incident, lawyers began protesting against the toll workers. The District Bar Association had passed a resolution that no lawyer would represent the toll workers. Meanwhile, lawyer Manoj Shukla had filed a bail petition for toll workers opposing this proposal. Angered by this, some lawyers entered his chamber and vandalized and set it on fire. They also burned his effigy. When legal assistance was not available at the local level, the toll workers went to the Supreme Court. Supreme Court made strong remarks During the hearing of this case, the Supreme Court bench, which included Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta, expressed strong displeasure over the attitude of the Barabanki Bar Association. The court said that such incidents reflect the declining reputation of the judicial system and legal profession. Additionally, the court praised Manoj Shukla, calling him a 'brave lawyer' who fought the case despite pressure. The Supreme Court granted bail to the toll plaza employees. Also, directed the UP DGP to ensure their security. They should be escorted to a safe location. Case transferred from UP to Delhi Due to violence and local protests by lawyers, the court transferred the entire case from UP to Delhi. The Supreme Court said that the legal rights of toll workers were affected because no lawyer was willing to stand in their favor. UP Bar Council also reprimanded The Supreme Court also reprimanded the Uttar Pradesh Bar Council. Said that the Council's demand to impose NSA from the state government was inappropriate, as it was a case of minor scuffle. The court expressed hope that the Bar Council of India will take necessary action in this entire matter.

stories.title: Lucknow BJP's new district working committee announced:New and old faces included, focus on strengthening booth-level organisation
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party has announced the new executive committee of the Lucknow district unit. After the recommendation of state president Pankaj Chaudhary, district president Vijay Maurya announced the entire team. It includes 8 vice presidents, 3 general secretaries, 8 ministers, 1 treasurer, and 3 joint treasurers. A total of 35 officials were given responsibilities, including media and IT in-charges. The announced executive committee has taken into account organisational balance and regional representation. Under the Awadh region, this team of Lucknow district includes both experienced faces and new workers. This team has been prepared keeping in view the upcoming elections and organisational expansion, so that strength can be brought up to the booth level. Responsibilities fixed from Vice President to General Secretary In the new team, Rajkumar Verma, Arvind Yadav, Krishna Kant Awasthi, Hansraj Lodhi, Anil Singh Chauhan, Shiv Darshan Yadav, Pratima Verma and Hansraj Rawat have been given responsibility as district vice presidents. While Dhirendra Pandey "Dhiru", Ankit Gupta and Gaurav Singh Chauhan have been appointed as district general secretaries. These positions are considered to have an important role in the organisation's operations. District Minister and Treasurer positions also appointed Raju Kashyap, Dhirendra Maurya "Dhiru", Vivek Singh, Sanjeev Mishra, Mukesh Sharma, Shyampyari Lodhi, Pratima Singh and Kamta Prasad Rawat have been included in the District Minister position. Chandra Prakash Awasthi (Advocate) has been made District Treasurer, and Abhishek Rajput, Gyanendra Singh Pappan and Amit Tiwari have been made Co-Treasurers. Media, Social Media and IT Team also announced BJP has set separate responsibilities, keeping in mind the media and digital platforms. Chitranmani Pandey has been made District Media In-charge, while Santosh Sharma and Ashish Kanaujia have been given the responsibility of Co-Media In-charge. In social media, Ravi Dwivedi has been made coordinator and Ajit Yadav and Nirmal Singh have been made co-coordinators. In the IT cell, Rajkumar Rohit has been given the responsibility of coordinator, and Vipin Saxena and Amit Kashyap have been made co-coordinators. Goal to strengthen the organization at grassroots level District President Vijay Maurya said that the objective of the new executive committee is to make the organisation active and strong up to the booth level. Clear instructions have been given to all office bearers to remain active in their respective areas and ensure government schemes reach every person. He expressed confidence that with the new team, BJP will become organizationally stronger in Lucknow and will firmly face the upcoming political challenges.

stories.title: Govt employee leaks fighter jet locations to Pakistan:In touch with ISI since 2023; shared Air Force, military base details
stories.summary: Rajasthan’s Intelligence team has arrested a government employee from Chabua Air Force Station in Assam on charges of espionage. The accused was allegedly passing sensitive information related to the Indian Air Force to Pakistani handlers. He had shared confidential details, including locations of fighter aircraft, missile systems, and information related to officers and personnel. ADG (Intelligence) Prafull Kumar said the case began in January 2026 with the arrest of Jhabraram, a resident of Jaisalmer. During interrogation, the name of another suspect, Sumit Kumar, surfaced, who was in continuous contact with Pakistani intelligence agencies. Sent confidential information to Pakistani handlers Investigations revealed that the accused, Sumit Kumar (36), son of Beni Madhav, is a resident of Lahurpar in Prayagraj district (Uttar Pradesh). He is currently posted as an MTS (Multi Tasking Staff) at Chabua Air Force Station in Dibrugarh, Assam. Misusing his position, he collected confidential information related to the Air Force station and passed it to Pakistani handlers through social media. Was in contact with Pakistani intelligence agency since 2023 The Rajasthan Intelligence team, in coordination with Air Force Intelligence in New Delhi, detained Sumit Kumar from Chabua. He was then brought to the Central Interrogation Centre in Jaipur, where multiple intelligence agencies questioned him. During interrogation, it was revealed that the accused had been in contact with a Pakistani intelligence agency since 2023 and was sharing sensitive information in exchange for money. The probe found that apart from Chabua Air Force Station, he had also shared crucial information related to Nal Air Force Station in Bikaner and other military bases. This included locations of fighter aircraft, missile systems and confidential details related to officers and staff. Additionally, the accused used mobile numbers issued in his name to create social media accounts for Pakistani handlers.

stories.title: 4 die, including woman and child, in Sambhal road accident:Car hits tempo while overtaking, vehicle crushed to half size
stories.summary: On Sunday evening, a speeding car and a tempo collided. In the accident, 4 people, including a woman, died, while 9 people were injured. Among them, 5 are in critical condition in Sambhal. The accident occurred near Udharanpur village in the Dhanari area on the Agra-Moradabad National Highway. The collision was so severe that both the tempo and the car were badly damaged. The tempo's body was crushed to half its size. Upon receiving information about the accident, the police and the 108 ambulance reached the spot. The injured were immediately taken to Community Health Center (CHC) Bahjoi. 12 people, including women and children, were sitting in the tempo According to police, the Ertiga car was moving at high speed. It was going from the district headquarters, Bahajoi, towards Barwala, while the tempo was coming towards Bahajoi. During this time, the car driver tried to overtake another vehicle, due to which it lost control and collided with the tempo. The tempo had 12 people on board, including children and women. There were two people in the car, including the driver. In the accident, Rajesh, son of Kallu (20) from Pathakpur ki Madaiya of Bahajoi police station, Rajni (14), daughter of Ompal from Raipur Kala, and Kishori (40 years), son of Jhandu Singh from Manakpur of Dhanari police station, died. One woman's identity has not yet been established. Rajni's father, Ompal (35), mother, Pravesh (32), sister, Saloni (7), and brother, Kuldeep (2) are undergoing treatment. Shaukin (32), son of Rafi from Akbarpur Bahjai, Rajnish (20), son of Kallu from Pathakpur ki Madhaiya, who were in the tempo, and car passengers Priyanchu (14), son of Ramgopal, and Kripal (35), son of Puran Singh from Lahra Nagla Shyam village of Junawai police station, are admitted to the hospital. Rajni's mother, Pravesh, said that she lives in Delhi with her husband Ompal and supports the family by selling golgappas and vegetables from a street cart. She said that they were returning home from Delhi and were about to reach the village by tempo. Just 10 minutes away from home, a vehicle crashed hard into their tempo, causing this accident. Meanwhile, Rajesh's father, Kallu, said that his son had left home alone to take a bath in the Rajghat Ganga, but he boarded the tempo with other passengers. He said that Rajesh was to be married in a month. Kallu said, "He was my only son," and broke down while saying this. CCTV investigation will reveal cause of accident CO Bahajoi Dr. Pradeep Kumar said, CCTV cameras installed in the surrounding area are being examined to determine the causes of the accident. 10 seriously injured people have been referred to the district hospital for better treatment. 4 people including a woman and a young girl have died in this accident. All bodies have been sent for post-mortem.

According to Iran’s consulate in Mumbai, the aircraft had entered Iranian airspace near the country’s southern coast, after which it was intercepted and targeted with a surface-to-air missile. 2. CM Yogi distributes nursing appointment letters to 1,100 women: Dy CM Pathak targets opponents, says era of job loot is over Yogi Adityanath distributes joining letters to 1,097 female and 131 male nursing officers in Lucknow on Sunday, saying at a program held at Lok Bhawan that receiving appointment letters during Navratri reflects the growing strength of women. 3. New claims in Farsa Baba death case: Disciples allege truck ran him over intentionally; questions raised over police hiding the container Whether the death of Farsa Wale Baba aka Chandrashekhar Singh (45) in Mathura is an accident or murder... this mystery is getting more complicated. Baba's supporters are calling it murder, while police are saying it was an accident. According to the theory stated by the police, the Baba was checking a container with Nagaland number plate when a truck bearing Rajasthan number plate hit the container from behind. Baba died after being caught in the collision. 4. PM Modi becomes longest-serving head of government Prime Minister Narendra Modi has become the longest-serving head of government in India. By completing 8,931 days as head of government, both as Chief Minister of Gujarat and as Prime Minister 5. Shringar Gauri temple opens after a year: 2 km queues as women raise ‘Free Gyanvapi’ slogans, Australian devotee joins chants A large number of devotees gathered on Sunday for darshan at the Maa Shringar Gauri temple inside Varanasi’s Gyanvapi complex, with queues stretching nearly 2 km. The temple opens for devotees only once a year on the fourth day of Chaitra Navratri, and will now reopen next year. 6. Accused held in Varanasi BSc student killing: Police carry accused to court after chase; students clash with ADM The accused in the murder of a student at UP College in Varanasi was produced in court under tight security on Saturday evening. Police feared that lawyers and students might assault the accused. Therefore, the police tried to make him run, but he stumbled because his leg was fractured. Following this, police personnel carried him into the courtroom. 7. LPG from US, crude from Russia reach India A cargo ship carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from Texas, US, arrived at Mangalore Port on Sunday. Meanwhile, a ship from Russia carrying crude oil also reached India. 8. Fake IAS has married not once but 25 times: Victim's father alleges serial marriage fraud; vows to get justice for his daughter The paralysed father from Gorakhpur alleges the fake IAS accused married 25 times, extorting money, and ruined his daughter’s life. Speaking anonymously to Dainik Bhaskar, he said he is determined to ensure strict punishment and explained how the family fell into the trap, how the marriage was arranged, and how the truth later surfaced. 9. Film ‘Dhurandhar’ sparks row over Atiq Ahmed portrayal: Chargesheet in Umesh Pal Murder mentions Pakistan link A brief 7–8-minute appearance by a character named Atif Ahmed in the film Dhurandhar: The Revenge has sparked a political and factual debate. The reel character closely resembles the real-life mafia don Atiq Ahmed from Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The film recreates his murder in a manner strikingly similar to the killing of Atiq and his brother Ashraf in April 2023, while attributing the sequence of events to a conspiracy involving National Security Advisor Ajay Sanyal. 10. Air travel prices may go up soon, Civil Aviation Ministry lifts airfare cap Airline companies will be able to increase domestic flight fares according to seat demand as the Civil Aviation Ministry has removed the cap on airfares.

stories.title: BJP core committee meets at Deputy CM’s residence:First such instance in 9 years; Yogi yet to return from Noida
stories.summary: A BJP core committee meeting has begun at the Lucknow residence of UP Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was on a visit to Noida today and has not yet returned to Lucknow. The meeting is being held in his absence, and members may later move to the Chief Minister’s residence after his arrival. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary, and organisation general secretary Dharampal Singh are present at the meeting. This is the first time in nine years of the Yogi government that a core committee meeting is being held at a Deputy CM’s residence. Earlier, such meetings were always held at the CM’s official residence at 5 Kalidas Marg or at the BJP state headquarters. No core committee meeting has ever been held at Keshav Prasad Maurya’s residence. However, before the 2022 Assembly elections, CM Yogi Adityanath, RSS leader Dattatreya Hosabale, Krishna Gopal, and others had visited his residence for a meal after a coordination meeting at the CM’s house. Roadmap to be prepared at Brajesh Pathak’s residence In the core committee meeting, a roadmap will be drawn to implement decisions taken in the coordination meeting between the RSS, government, and BJP. The BJP has assured the RSS that district executive bodies in all districts will be formed by March 30. The party’s state team will be constituted by April 15. Political appointments in all corporations, commissions, and boards will be completed by May 15. According to sources, discussions will also focus on forming the OBC Commission for panchayat elections, political appointments and the state team structure.

stories.title: Power struggle stalls BJP district president appointments in UP:Disputes between top leaders over candidates delay naming district chiefs in 5 areas
stories.summary: The politics of Purvanchal is considered incomplete without caste and pressure politics. This time BJP appears to be caught in this political maze. The party's stalwarts have linked their prestige to the appointment of 5 district presidents in Purvanchal. In Chandauli, there is an open tussle between Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and former state president Mahendranath Pandey. In Deoria, the egos of 2 former state presidents (Surya Pratap Shahi and Ramapati Ram Tripathi) clashed. While in Gorakhpur-Varanasi, CM Yogi and PM Modi's likes and dislikes have completely stalled the matter. This is also affecting the party's functioning. What is the reason for this tug of war? With less than a year left for assembly elections, when will the 5 district presidents be announced? Read in our special report... First District - Chandauli District President appointment stuck between Brahmin vs Thakur Chandauli is the home district of former Union Minister Dr. Mahendranath Pandey and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Party sources say Pandey wants to remove the current district president, Kashi Singh. He wishes to appoint a Brahmin face as president. Their camp believes that Kashi Singh did not work properly in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Even after being the Kshatriya district president, the Thakurs voted for SP. This led to the defeat of two-time MP Dr. Mahendranath Pandey. Kashi Singh belongs to the Defence Minister's camp. Now the announcement of the district president is stuck in the tug of war between Rajnath Singh and Dr. Mahendranath's camps. The special thing is that the party had made Pandey the in-charge of state organisational elections. Under his supervision, 93 district presidents have been declared in the organisational elections. However, the appointment of the district president is stuck in his home district itself. Second District - Deoria Ramapati says, ‘Whoever I advocate for will become president’ In Deoria, Pintu Jaiswal, a close associate of former state president Ramapati Ram Tripathi and Sadar block chief, was almost certain to become the district president. Tripathi had also approved Jaiswal's name to state president Pankaj Chaudhary. However, Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi, MP Shashank Mani Tripathi and 2 local MLAs opposed Pintu's appointment. However, in the case Ramapati Ram Tripathi says, ‘I did not ask anyone to make Pintu Jaiswal the district president’. Ask whoever is saying this and why they are saying so. As far as advocacy is concerned, if I advocated for someone, they would definitely become president. The argument against Pintu was that he joined the BJP in 2021 before the panchayat elections. The party made him block chief. Now, if I were made district president, it would send the wrong message to workers. This matter went from Lucknow to Delhi, and Pintu could not become the district president. Now the party is looking for a name that everyone agrees on. Third District - Ambedkarnagar State President looking for a Kurmi-Brahmin face BJP wanted to promote district vice president Rana Randhir Singh to make him president here. However, state president Pankaj Chaudhary's argument was that Faizabad division is a Kurmi and Brahmin-dominated area. SP has Kurmi and Brahmin leaders here. The party has only appointed a Kurmi district president in Barabanki of Faizabad division. Not a single Brahmin has been made district president. In such a situation, Chaudhary suggested making a Kurmi or Brahmin face the district president instead of Rana, which would help in securing the vote bank. This is the reason why the announcement of the district president's name could not be made in Ambedkar Nagar as well. Fourth District - Varanasi District President will be appointed based on PM's preference Hansraj Vishwakarma is the district president in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency, Varanasi. The party has also made him a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC). Active in politics for 34 years, Hansraj is an important face of the backward classes in the area. Therefore, a search is on for a strong alternative to replace him. According to sources, the decision of the district president in Varanasi will only be made after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's green signal. It is by the Prime Minister's wish that Hansraj has remained district president for three terms. Fifth District - Gorakhpur Metropolitan President passed away last June In March 2025, Devesh Srivastava was declared Metropolitan President in Gorakhpur. However, he passed away from a heart attack in June 2025. Now the position of Metropolitan President is vacant here. There is no political manoeuvring happening here. The Metropolitan President will be appointed only with CM Yogi's preference. Therefore, everyone is waiting for his signal. 93 names approved so far BJP has divided UP into 98 organisational districts. The party released the first list of 70 district presidents on March 16, 2025. Devesh Srivastava, the district president of Gorakhpur, included in this list, passed away in June 2025. Meanwhile, Gonda district president Amar Kishore Kashyap was removed after a video of him with a female worker went viral in the party office. This left 68 district presidents. After this, 14 more names came forward on November 26 and 11 district presidents on February 26 this year. In this, Iqbal Bahadur Tiwari was made president in Gonda. However, the appointment of district presidents in Chandauli, Deoria, Varanasi, Ambedkar Nagar and Gorakhpur has not been made yet.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'women will get ₹40,000 if party forms govt':SP chief hits out at ‘Dhurandhar’, claiming BJP funding films
stories.summary: “These people have decided on a cabinet expansion during Navratri. It is just an attempt to pacify those who are upset. Now that the budget has been fully spent, they are making ministers. Funds are being released quickly to several departments. One department has even approved tenders worth ₹1,000 crore, but it is unclear what has actually been delivered,” said SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday, taking a swipe at the Yogi government’s likely cabinet expansion. Akhilesh was speaking at the Murti Devi–Malti Devi Women Honour Ceremony in Lucknow, where several women were felicitated. His wife and Mainpuri MP Dimple Yadav were also present. He reiterated that if voted to power, his party would give ₹40,000 annually to women and revive the Samajwadi pension scheme. Amid the controversy over the film ‘Dhurandhar’, he alleged that the BJP is now funding films to defame opposition parties. The film ‘Dhurandhar: The Revenge’, released on March 19, features a character named Atif Ahmed, resembling real-life mafia Atiq Ahmed. Leaders from Congress and SP have termed the film propaganda. Dimple Yadav said that in the “new India”, women feel unsafe and fearful. Referring to the Ankita Bhandari case in Uttarakhand, she said such incidents leave deep wounds and raise concerns about the country’s progress. Key points from Akhilesh’s speech: 1. ‘Not a green corridor, but a wasted corridor’ in Lucknow Akhilesh said the Defence Minister wants to do good work for Lucknow, but CM Yogi has built a “wasted corridor” instead of a green corridor. He claimed it lacks space for pedestrians and does not meet proper standards, despite costing ₹7,000 crore. 2. ‘Election setting has already begun in UP’ He alleged that preparations and “settings” for elections have already started in UP, including the posting of officials. He also claimed irregularities in previous elections. 3. ‘LPG cylinder depends on luck now’ Mocking the situation, he said getting an LPG cylinder depends on luck, otherwise people must stand in queues. He also accused BJP leaders of irregularities in cylinder distribution. 4. ‘Law and order have collapsed in UP’ Akhilesh blamed the administration and police for deteriorating law and order, citing incidents in Gorakhpur, Varanasi and Mathura. He alleged political misuse of the police and rising corruption. 5. ‘PDA strength troubling BJP’ He claimed that the strength of PDA (backward, Dalit, minority alliance) is worrying the BJP, and alleged plans of large-scale deployments and election manipulation. 6. ‘If Shankaracharya not spared, anyone can be insulted’ He criticised police actions, saying if even religious leaders like Shankaracharya are not spared, anyone can be insulted. He also questioned the process of appointing the DGP.

stories.title: Shringar Gauri temple opens after a year:2 km queues as women raise ‘Free Gyanvapi’ slogans, Australian devotee joins chants
stories.summary: A large number of devotees gathered on Sunday for darshan at the Maa Shringar Gauri temple inside Varanasi’s Gyanvapi complex, with queues stretching nearly 2 km. The temple opens for devotees only once a year on the fourth day of Chaitra Navratri, and will now reopen next year. The four women plaintiffs in the Gyanvapi case also arrived to offer prayers, raising slogans of “Free Gyanvapi”. They have moved court seeking recognition of the site as a temple. Tight security arrangements were in place due to the heavy footfall, with devotees allowed entry under strict supervision. During the 25-minute worship, vermillion and sandalwood paste were applied to the ancient, damaged stones of the shrine, while mantras were chanted. The premises echoed with chants of “Har Har Mahadev”, accompanied by damru beats. Among the devotees was Maria from Australia, who joined in chanting praises of the Goddess. See 3 photos... Regular worship banned after 1992 Regular darshan and worship of Maa Shringar Gauri continued until 1992. Following the Babri demolition in Ayodhya, access was restricted due to security concerns. Since then, the temple has been opened for darshan only once a year, on the fourth day of Chaitra Navratri. On August 18, 2021, five women filed a petition in a Varanasi court seeking permission for regular worship at the site. Acting on court orders, a survey was later conducted within the premises. After the survey, the Hindu side claimed that a Shivling was found in the basement, while the Muslim side maintained that it was a fountain. The petition is led by Delhi-based Rakhi Singh. The other petitioners—Sita Sahu, Manju Vyas, Laxmi Devi and Rekha Pathak—are residents of Varanasi.

stories.title: CM Yogi distributes nursing appointment letters to 1,100 women:Dy CM Pathak targets opponents, says era of job loot is over
stories.summary: Yogi Adityanath distributes joining letters to 1,097 female and 131 male nursing officers in Lucknow on Sunday, saying at a program held at Lok Bhawan that receiving appointment letters during Navratri reflects the growing strength of women. He said, The days are gone when it was believed that nothing would come of opening medical colleges or nursing colleges. Earlier, a parallel government of mafias used to run in medical colleges. Every department had a mafia. The department ran as he wished. Now, instead of mafias, 'One District, One Medical College' has been established. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak said, Nurses are made for service. So you should not get angry, you have to serve the patients. You people never worry. If there is any problem, tell us. You are like our family's daughters and brothers. Some have been posted far away. If you don't find a place to live, tell us too. Pathak also said- Earlier, people from the same community used to get jobs. Connections (jugaad) worked in every job, but now jobs are obtained through intellect and skill. Mafia who looted jobs are now fleeing to save their lives. Those who watched dances in Saifai. They are also troubled. In commerce, it is said - bad money drives good money out of circulation, so we have to go among the public and explain the difference. Now, 5 major points from Yogi's address 1. ‘Earlier hospitals ran on God’s mercy’ He said Indian nursing staff are in high demand globally (Japan, Germany, Korea, Europe). From 1947–2017, UP had only 17 medical colleges; now there are 81 (government + private). Earlier, the nursing and paramedical sectors were neglected, and hospital facilities depended largely on fate. 2. Story of Gorakhpur nursing school He recalled a nursing school in Gorakhpur that had only one faculty member. When the principal feared closure affecting 100 trainees, he arranged an honorarium to continue operations. He said 35 ANM/JNM institutes closed during the SP government are being revived, and construction of 31 nursing colleges has restarted. Nursing is the backbone of healthcare. 3. Major rise in medical seats He said healthcare improved under the double-engine government: maternal mortality now matches the national average; 3.5 crore people linked to Universal Health Coverage; 14 crore ABHA IDs created. Nursing seats increased by 7,000, paramedical by 2,000, MBBS seats from 5,390 to 12,700, and PG seats from 1,221 to 5,056. PPP-mode medical colleges are also running. 4. UP to supply nurses nationwide During Navratri, distributing appointment letters to many women reflects empowerment. With a population of 25 crore, UP aims to provide nursing manpower for the entire country. He suggested offering nursing education in multiple Indian languages like Tamil, Marathi, and Kannada. 5. ‘No discrimination in jobs or schemes’ He said reservation rules for SC, ST, and OBC are fully followed. In the last 9 years, 9 lakh government jobs have been provided without recommendation or transactions. Recruitment is done transparently through commissions under monitoring. Deputy CM highlights role of nurses Deployment in 14 districts including Kanpur The nursing officers who have received joining letters will be deployed in medical colleges of Agra, Kanpur, Prayagraj, Meerut, Jhansi, Gorakhpur, Ambedkarnagar, Kannauj, Azamgarh, Jalaun, Saharanpur, Banda and Badaun, along with JK Cancer Institute and Cardiology Institute, Kanpur.

stories.title: Fake IAS has married not once but 25 times:Victim's father alleges serial marriage fraud; vows to get justice for his daughter
stories.summary: He has married not once, but 25 times. He extorted money by posing as a fake IAS officer and also ruined my daughter's life. He left us with nothing. Every day a new story about him comes to light. This is what the father-in-law of the fake IAS officer, who lives in Gorakhpur, has to say. Half of his body is paralysed, and he remains confined to bed. Only a few years after suffering paralysis, another calamity struck, leaving the entire family shattered. On condition of anonymity, he told Dainik Bhaskar that he will not rest until the man who ruined his daughter’s life is punished. He also explained how the family fell into the fake IAS officer’s trap, how the relationship was arranged, and how the truth eventually came to light. The father-in-law of the fake IAS said, I have 3 daughters and one son. I have married off 2 daughters. Meanwhile, I became paralyzed. Half of my body doesn't work, so I started looking for a match for my youngest daughter. My youngest daughter has graduated. IAS profile shared in community group He said his elder daughter, who lives in Delhi, told him about a community group where someone shared the profile of an IAS officer named Pritam Kumar Nishad from Ludhiyat Mohalla in Etawah. The profile stated he was 32 years old and posted as an SDM in Manikpur, and that his family did not want dowry, only a beautiful bride. Hearing this, he felt the match was suitable and asked his daughter to proceed with the talks. Family visits Etawah to verify groom After his elder daughter spoke to Pritam Kumar Nishad about marriage, she arranged a phone conversation with him as well. He later visited Gorakhpur in December 2025, where the family met him, and he liked the girl upon seeing her. As talks progressed, family members went to Etawah to verify details. They found a 2BHK house in Ludhiyat Mohalla, where Pritam said he lived with his sister and that the house was in her name. He told them his financial condition had been poor earlier, but he was planning to sell the house and buy a new one. Dowry demand made before wedding When Pritam Kumar Nishad was asked about his village, he said it was 35 km away across a river and claimed it was very backward, adding he was the first boy from there to become an IAS officer. This helped him gain the family’s trust, and they were satisfied with the match. The wedding was fixed for March 11, 2026. Although he initially refused dowry, after the date was finalised, he demanded money, citing wedding and reception expenses, saying important guests would attend. At his insistence, ₹15 lakh was given to him one month before the wedding. 'Government of India' written on car Relatives expose groom’s fake identity Pritam showed videos in his defense The girl's father said that in his defense, Pritam provided a video. That video contained Pritam's interview. A YouTuber had interviewed him after he became an SDM, which had been running on his channel for four years. After this, Pritam said that his relatives are jealous and they don't want him to get married. After being convinced, the farewell ceremony was completed on March 12, 2026. Villagers called and revealed the truth The girl's father said that shortly after, several more calls came from Pritam's village. They also provided proof of Pritam's fraud. They said that Pritam had run away from the village. He has defrauded many people. He has married 25 times by lying. Reached groom’s house after farewell The girl’s father said they were frightened after the farewell and asked their daughter to keep sharing her location. Three hours later, his son, nephew, and elder daughter left Gorakhpur by car. Pritam Kumar Nishad reached his house in Ludhiyat Mohalla, Etawah, around 9 PM, while the girl’s family arrived at 11 PM. They found people at his house intoxicated, and Pritam himself returned with red eyes. Truth revealed after interrogation SSP Dr. Kaustubh said, A case has been registered. After investigating the family's allegations, action will be taken against the accused.

stories.title: New claims in Farsa Baba death case:Disciples allege truck ran him over intentionally; questions raised over police hiding the container
stories.summary: Whether the death of Farsa Wale Baba aka Chandrashekhar Singh (45) in Mathura is an accident or murder... this mystery is getting more complicated. Baba's supporters are calling it murder, while police are saying it was an accident. According to the theory stated by police the Baba was checking a container with Nagaland number plate when a truck bearing Rajasthan number plate hit the container from behind. Baba died after being caught in the collision. Baba received information that cattle was being transported by truck Supporters stated that Baba had received information regarding cattle being transported by truck. He chased the truck on a bike with his two companions. They overtook and stood in front of it. They started checking the container. That's when a truck coming from behind deliberately crushed Baba. Baba's companions were also targeted but they narrowly escaped. However, the DIG stated, There were no cattle in the trucks. The Nagaland number truck contained soap-shampoo and the Rajasthan number truck had oil. The Rajasthan number truck was damaged in the accident. The driver died during treatment, while regarding the container and its location This has not been traced yet". In this situation, Baba's supporters have raised questions that if the container really had soap-shampoo, why did the police keep it in an unknown location? They said that CCTV footage from the highway will reveal the truth. Read what the disciples who accompanied Baba said. Hariom said – the collision was deliberate, the container had cows Hariom, a disciple who lives at Baba’s cowshed, said, “Around 3 am on Saturday someone called Farsa Wale Baba and informed him that cattle were being transported from the National Highway near Kosi. After receiving the information, Baba took me and Kanha on his motorcycle and reached the spot”. He added, “As soon as Baba arrived, a container with a Nagaland registration number started speeding towards Delhi. Baba chased it and stopped it near the Navipur area”. He further stated, “Baba got down from the bike and was checking the container when a truck with a Rajasthan number coming from behind rammed into him at high speed. It wanted to crush all of us, but Baba pushed us away and came under the truck himself”. He also said, “If there was nothing illegal in the container, why did the people inside try to flee?” He claimed that the container was carrying cows. That is why the truck moving behind deliberately hit Baba. Another companion said - There was adequate light at the accident spot Kanha, another companion who was with Baba, said, “You can go and see how much light there is at the place where the incident occurred. The truck running in the middle directly hit Maharaj Ji after seeing him. Maharaj Ji didn't get a chance. After the collision, the container people ran away. They were Muslims, that's why the police let them go. Otherwise, the public would have killed them”. He added, “Maharaj Ji used to go on patrol every day. This is just a conspiracy. At this same point, three years ago, Sonu Sarpanch, who was involved in cow protection, was also killed. Kanha claims that if the administration checks CCTV footage, it will show that there were cows in that vehicle. Why hasn't the police shown the recovery of the container yet”. Now find out what the police and administration are saying Who is Farsa Wale Baba? Chandrashekhar Baba's home is in Ajnaukh village in the Chhata area on Barsana Road in Mathura. He has been serving cows for many years. Local people say, “Farsa Wale Baba was always dedicated to cows. Initially, whenever there was any problem regarding cows in the Barsana area, people would tell Baba. He gradually became famous in the area by helping cows”. Farsa Wale Baba, who dedicated his life to cow service, was so feared among smugglers that as soon as they learned of his presence, they would abandon the illegally transported cattle and run away. Baba's elder brother Keshav Singh said, “Younger brother was 45 years old. Originally from Sirsaganj Langra of Firozabad. He had become a Baba at the age of 10. In the family, we were the only two brothers. I have 4 sons, 4 daughters-in-law, 7 grandsons and 6 granddaughters. Baba never married”. He further stated, “We live in Ayodhya. Earlier, Baba also used to live with us in Ayodhya. Later he came to Mathura”. He has also demanded death penalty for the culprits. Understand the complete matter... Farsa Wale Baba died after being crushed by a truck in Kosikalan's Kotvan police station area on Saturday. A video has emerged after the accident. In this, Baba is lying on the ground. A sword with its sheath is lying near him. The front part of the Rajasthan number truck appears damaged. Its driver Khurshid, a resident of Alwar, also died during treatment in Agra. News of the incident spread like wildfire in the area. Thousands of people came out on the highway in Mathura's Chhata town. Angry people placed Baba's body and blocked the Delhi-Kolkata highway. They started demanding encounter of the accused. The police who arrived to take possession of the body and clear the traffic jam were chased away by people. They also pelted stones, in which some policemen were injured. People vandalized 5 to 6 police vehicles. Windows were broken. Seeing the situation getting out of control, police resorted to lathi charge. Tear gas shells were fired. CM Yogi took cognizance of the matter Meanwhile, people took Baba's body to the gaushala located in Ajnaukh village. They put forward 6 demands including building a memorial for Baba before the administration. The DM assured that a memorial site will be built at the place of Baba's cremation. After this, Baba's last rites were performed. CM Yogi also took cognizance of the matter. While directing officials to take strict action, he said, “The accused will not be spared”. Meanwhile, late Saturday night, 16 rioters including Hindu Raksha Dal worker Daksh Chaudhary have been arrested for causing disturbance regarding Farsa Baba's death.

stories.title: Accused held in Varanasi BSc student killing:Police carry accused to court after chase; students clash with ADM
stories.summary: The accused in the murder of a student at UP College in Varanasi was produced in court under tight security on Saturday evening. Police feared that lawyers and students might assault the accused. Therefore, the police tried to make him run, but he stumbled because his leg was fractured. Following this, police personnel carried him into the courtroom. The Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) sent Manjeet to jail for 14 days. Police had arrested Manjeet on Friday for the murder of student Surya Pratap Singh. However, his associate Anuj Singh, who allegedly helped him, is still absconding. See Manjeet's court appearance in 2 pictures... Manjeet said - Student used to do ragging Police interrogated the accused named Manjeet Chauhan before presenting him in court. During this, he revealed that Surya Pratap Singh along with his friends used to rag him. Manjeet said, “Surya Pratap Singh and his associates often troubled me and my friends in the name of ragging. They would physically assault us. On the day of the incident, March 20, we also had an argument on the college campus. There were threats and intimidation”. He added, “In anger and revenge, along with my companion Anuj Singh, I fired 4-5 rounds at Surya Pratap near the administrative building. This resulted in his death”. Sharp argument between protesting students and ADM Meanwhile, on Saturday (March 21), ADM Alok Verma reached to persuade the students who were protesting against Surya Pratap's murder at UP College. During the talks, there was a sharp argument between ADM and the students. After this, the students put forward 5 demands. The officials assured to take the charter of demands from the students and send it to the government. These 5 demands were put forward by students to ADM Now know the complete matter... Student had returned to college on Friday after 20 days The deceased father Rishi Dev Singh is a driver at Atulanand School. His mother Kiran Singh is an assistant at Atulanand School. Surya has two sisters, one is married while the other sister is still studying. Surya Pratap had chickenpox 20 days ago. Due to this, he was not coming to college. After recovering, he came to college on March 20 only. That's when he was murdered. Crime Scene and Subsequent Events… It was 11 o'clock in the morning. Students were studying in their respective classes. Suddenly, BSc student Surya Pratap Singh was shot and killed on the college campus. BA second-year student Manjeet Singh Chauhan shot him in filmy style in front of the principal and students. A student recorded a video of the live incident. After the murder, the accused fled after throwing the pistol in a garbage heap. After this, everyone had just one question in their mind that why did Manjeet kill Surya? It was reported that Surya used to call senior students to the hostel. He would rag junior students. Manjeet had complained about this to the principal. The principal had summoned both of them. On Friday, after meeting with the principal, there was a dispute between Manjeet and Surya. In which Manjeet rolled up his shirt sleeves, then Surya grabbed Manjeet's collar while hurling abuses. At that time, friends intervened and stopped them. Manjeet went to his home. From there, he came to college with a pistol along with a friend. He parked his Pulsar bike near the gate outside the college. Then, as soon as he saw Surya in the arts faculty corridor, he opened fire on him. He fell down, yet he continued shooting at him with the pistol. Manjeet's leg broke after jumping from 12 feet height After the murder, Manjeet felt that he would be caught if he escaped through the gate, so he jumped from the roof to avoid this. His leg broke when he jumped from a height of about 12 feet. His bike was parked at the gate, but seeing himself surrounded, he ran towards Airport Road even with his broken leg. He took a lift in an e-rickshaw to reach Gilt Bazar intersection and then turned off his phone. After this, he tried to get treatment after reaching a deserted place. After breaking his leg, he could not flee outside the city. Meanwhile, police pressured the family members for his arrest. Angry students created ruckus in college premises After the incident, angry students created a ruckus on the college campus. They broke chairs inside the campus. After about 4 hours, the police got the college gate opened. Students and teachers were evacuated from the college by forming a cordon. Three professors were injured in stone pelting by students. Police chased away the protesting students with lathi charge. Meanwhile, parents fainted upon seeing the body of their only son. Now know about Surya Pratap Singh... 21-year-old Surya Pratap Singh was from Ghazipur district. He completed his education till 8th standard from Ghazipur. He came to UP College to study from 9th standard. Since then, he had been studying here. He was very talented in studies. He passed his 12th examination in PCM from UP College itself with first division. Then he cleared the entrance exam and got admission in BSc Mathematics here. Fellow students said that he was very friendly. He kept himself busy with studies. After BSc, he wanted to do research in MSc Mathematics from here. His dream was to go into academics. Case registered against accused Manjeet Chauhan The accused student Manjeet Chauhan is a BA second year student. Manjeet is from Chandmari area of Varanasi itself. He already had a case under section 323 registered at Shivpur police station, while his associate Anuj also has several cases registered against him. The accused, who gets into fights over small matters, is of an aggressive nature. He has a bad boy image on social media. He calls himself a mafia on Instagram. He is also well-known in local police stations like Bhojubir, Shivpur and Bada Lalpur. He runs an 1818 gang on social media. He had written in his Instagram bio “Your respect remains only as long as it doesn't hurt my self-respect. Jai Maa Bhawani”.

stories.title: Film ‘Dhurandhar’ sparks row over Atiq Ahmed portrayal:Chargesheet in Umesh Pal Murder mentions Pakistan link
stories.summary: A brief 7–8-minute appearance by a character named Atif Ahmed in the film Dhurandhar: The Revenge has sparked a political and factual debate. The reel character closely resembles the real-life mafia don Atiq Ahmed from Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The film recreates his murder in a manner strikingly similar to the killing of Atiq and his brother Ashraf in April 2023, while attributing the sequence of events to a conspiracy involving National Security Advisor Ajay Sanyal. In contrast, in Uttar Pradesh, it is widely believed that the decline of mafia dominance, including that of Atiq, resulted from CM Yogi Adityanath’s stringent crackdown. The film also portrays Atif Ahmed as having links with Pakistan’s intelligence agency ISI, depicting him as a major arms supplier, counterfeit currency operator, and political influencer. These claims have led leaders from the Congress and Samajwadi Party to label the film as propaganda. Former SP MP Dr. S.T. Hasan stated that no Indian investigative agency has confirmed such allegations, calling it an attempt to generate controversy for publicity. Amidst these claims, here is a breakdown of what the film shows versus documented realities. Fact 1: Alleged ISI links and arms supply Film portrayal: The film depicts Atif Ahmed procuring AK-47 rifles through Pakistan’s ISI, facilitated by Baloch mafia networks. Reality: Atiq Ahmed was murdered on 15 April 2023. Fifteen days earlier, Prayagraj Police filed a chargesheet in the Umesh Pal murder case, naming Atiq and his brother Ashraf in arms trafficking. According to the document, Atiq claimed he had ample access to weapons and acknowledged links with ISI and Lashkar-e-Taiba operatives. The chargesheet states that weapons were airdropped via drones in Punjab and then routed through local agents to Atiq’s network. The same consignments allegedly reached militants in Jammu and Kashmir. Atiq also indicated possible recovery points for weapons. Based on these statements, police registered an FIR mentioning ISI-supplied arms, including AK-47 rifles, a .45 bore pistol, a sten gun, and even RDX. A .45 pistol was reportedly used in the Umesh Pal murder, while 58 Pakistan-made 9mm cartridges were recovered. Fact 2: Criminal network operated from jail Film portrayal: Atif Ahmed is shown managing his operations from inside prison, coordinating with ISI officials and directing smuggling activities, including drugs via Nepal. Reality: This aspect aligns closely with documented incidents. Following the 2007 Raju Pal murder, Atiq spent most of his time in various prisons, including Naini (Prayagraj), Deoria, Banda, and Chitrakoot. In April 2013, while lodged in Deoria Jail, Atiq’s associates abducted Lucknow-based businessman Mohit Jaiswal and brought him into the prison. There, Jaiswal was brutally assaulted, suffering fractures in his fingers, and coerced into transferring ownership of his companies, MJ Infra, to associates Farooq and Zaki. The case gained national attention, leading to Atiq’s transfer to Bareilly Jail in December 2018 and subsequently to Sabarmati Jail in Gujarat in 2019. Fact 3: Counterfeit currency via Nepal route Film portrayal: The narrative links Atif Ahmed to a massive counterfeit currency operation orchestrated by Dawood Ibrahim, prompting the Indian government’s demonetisation move in November 2016. Reality: No formal case was registered against Atiq Ahmed for circulating fake Pakistani currency through Nepal into Uttar Pradesh. However, multiple cases involving hawala transactions were filed. Investigations revealed that Atiq was involved in extortion, routing funds through shell companies, transferring them abroad, and reintroducing them into India via alternative channels. Fact 4: Political influence in UP Film portrayal: The film suggests that Atif Ahmed played a role in influencing government formation in Uttar Pradesh. Reality: Atiq Ahmed did wield significant political influence. He was first elected MLA from Allahabad West in 1989 and retained the seat in 1991, 1993, 1996, and 2002. In 2004, he became an MP from Phulpur on a Samajwadi Party ticket. Even after imprisonment in the Raju Pal murder case, he remained politically active. However, there is no evidence supporting two key cinematic claims: that his political rise was funded by counterfeit currency operations, or that he directly influenced the formation of state governments. Why is the film being called propaganda ? Former IPS officer Lalji Shukla, who investigated multiple cases involving Atiq during his tenure in Prayagraj, offered a nuanced perspective. He acknowledged that counterfeit currency does enter India from Pakistan, often through Bangladesh and Nepal routes, and noted that such consignments were intercepted during his posting in Bahraich. However, he clarified that Atiq’s name never directly surfaced in these cases. On weapons, Shukla stated that Atiq had a known fascination with firearms and that multiple weapons were seized from him over time, including a .30 pistol licensed in another individual’s name. He added that while the film draws inspiration from reality, it cannot be treated as factual. Individuals involved in violent crime may also engage in smuggling or financial crimes, but such links must be proven. Senior journalist and writer Manoj Rajan Tripathi also emphasised the film’s disclaimer stating that any resemblance to real individuals is coincidental. He pointed out that despite over 175 cases registered against Atiq, none conclusively established arms smuggling from Pakistan during his lifetime. Tripathi further noted that the film focuses on selective elements while omitting major incidents, including the Raju Pal and Umesh Pal murder cases and other serious allegations. As such, he argues, Dhurandhar: The Revenge should be viewed as a dramatised narrative rather than a factual account.

stories.title: Man poses as IAS for marriage, plans to sell bride:Organised grand wedding in Gorakhpur, flees when exposed
stories.summary: A shocking case has emerged from Gorakhpur, where a man from Etawah allegedly posed as an IAS officer to marry a woman and later planned to sell her in Goa. The accused, identified as Pritam Nishad, managed to deceive the bride’s family with fake credentials before his identity was exposed. Grand wedding, heavy expenses The marriage was solemnized with great pomp at a marriage lawn in the Nandanagar area. The bride’s family reportedly spent around ₹30 lakh on the wedding, including ₹15 lakh in cash given as dowry. After the wedding, the bride’s father filed a complaint at the Cantt police station in Gorakhpur against the accused and his family. Fraudulent claims and fake proof The victim’s family, residents of Mohaddipur, came into contact with Pritam through a matrimonial group. He claimed to be an IAS officer posted in Manikpur. To gain trust, he shared alleged news channel interviews, photos of an office setup, and images with political leaders. Demanded money before marriage Although Pritam initially claimed he would marry without dowry, he later demanded ₹15 lakh before the engagement under the pretext of expenses. The family paid ₹10 lakh during the engagement and the remaining ₹5 lakh on the wedding day. Truth revealed after wedding On March 11, 2026, the wedding took place at Durga Marriage Lawn in Nandanagar. The next day, after the groom’s party departed, someone informed the bride’s family that he was not an IAS officer. When the family reached the address given by the accused, they found their daughter in a small room. The accused and his sister fled upon seeing them. Allegation of trafficking plan After returning home, the bride revealed that the accused was allegedly planning to take her to Goa and sell her. The family has accused him of being a habitual fraudster who uses fake identities and documents to deceive people. There are also suspicions of his involvement in human trafficking. Police investigation underway According to Senior Superintendent of Police Dr. Kaustubh, a case has been registered and an investigation is underway. Authorities have assured that strict action will be taken after verifying all allegations.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Cow vigilante's death triggers 10 km jam in Mathura; PM Modi stresses to keep sea routes open
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Modi dials Iranian President, stresses to keep sea routes open The US-Israel-Iran war has entered its 22nd day. On Saturday, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with the Iranian President over the phone and extended greetings on Eid and Nowruz. During the conversation, he condemned attacks on critical infrastructure in the region, noting that they harm regional stability and disrupt global supply chains. 2. Cow vigilante's death triggers 10 km highway blockade in Mathura, cops injured in stone-pelting Cow vigilante Chandrashekhar Baba, popularly known as 'Farsa Wale Baba', died after being run over by a truck in Mathura. One of his associates claimed that early Saturday morning, Baba was chasing a truck along with two companions after suspecting it was transporting cattle. 3. RSS urges UP ministers, MLAs to avoid controversial statements The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) has asked ministers and MLAs of the Uttar Pradesh Government to improve their working style and avoid making controversial statements against the government. 4. BJP releases new candidate list for Kerala, Assam and Puducherry Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday released fresh lists of candidates for upcoming assembly elections in Kerala, Assam and Puducherry. The party announced nine candidates for the Puducherry Assembly elections. It also released the third list of 11 candidates for the Kerala Assembly polls. Additionally, the BJP issued a list of two candidates for the Assam Assembly elections. 5. Akhilesh Yadav joins massive Eid gathering in Lucknow Eid is being celebrated in UP today. Amid high alert, Eid prayers will be offered at different times at Eidgahs in Lucknow. More than 50 thousand people are offering prayers at Aishbagh Eidgah. Meanwhile, former CM Akhilesh Yadav, former Deputy CM Dinesh Sharma, and Congress state president Ajay Rai have arrived. 6. BSc student's cremated in midnight in Varanasi The last rites of BSc student Surya Pratap Singh (21) from UP College in Varanasi were performed at 12:30 am. His father had insisted that the accused be killed in an encounter before the cremation. Police officials somehow convinced him. 7. Airlines warn of airfare hike, blames it on Centre Indigo, Air India, and SpiceJet have opposed the government's decision not to charge extra for 60% of flight seats. Airlines say that this move will force them to increase airfares to compensate for their lost revenue. 8. Sanjay Nishad targets 160 seats in UP election: Focus on Kevat-Mallah community votes Nishad Party is going to launch its election rally from Gorakhpur. After this, there will be 3 more mega rallies. The party wants to focus on 160 Kevat-Mallah dominated seats in UP. 9. Train coach restaurant shuts down in Lucknow A unique restaurant operating out of a rail coach near Charbagh Railway Station in Lucknow has been forced to halt most of its operations due to a shortage of commercial gas cylinders. 10. Asim Munir threatens Shia clerics at iftar, says ‘go to Iran if you love it’ Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, told Shia clerics that those who “love Iran so much should go there,” a statement Shia leaders described as insulting and provocative.

stories.title: ग्राइंडर ऐप पर हुई दोस्ती, होटल बुलाकर जमकर की युवक की पिटाई, फिर बनाई अश्लील वीडियो
stories.summary: Lucknow News: लखनऊ में एक युवक के साथ एक हादसा हो गया। उसे ग्राइंडर नाम के डेटिंग ऐप पर दोस्ती के बहाने होटल बुलाया गया। वहां जाकर उसके अश्लील वीडियो बना लिए गए। जब उसने मना किया तो उसे जमकर पीटा गया और 35 हजार रुपये लूट लिए गए। पुलिस ने इस मामले में केस दर्ज किया है और जांच शुरू कर दी है। पीड़ित युवक बीकेटी इलाके का रहने वाला है। उसकी मुलाकात ग्राइंडर ऐप पर अलीगंज के रहने वाले अभिषेक वर्मा से हुई थी। दोनों ने ऐप पर बातचीत शुरू की और धीरे-धीरे दोस्ती हो गई। अभिषेक ने युवक को होटल में मिलने के लिए बुलाया। युवक को लगा कि यह सिर्फ मिलने-जुलने की बात है, इसलिए वह गुरुवार को होटल गैलेक्सी पहुंच गया। यह होटल जीसीआरजी कॉलेज के पास बीकेटी इलाके में स्थित है। अभिषेक इसी होटल में काम करता है।

stories.title: Train coach restaurant shuts down in Lucknow:Manager says, 'No gas supply since March 3, causing daily losses of ₹20,000'
stories.summary: A unique restaurant operating out of a rail coach near Charbagh Railway Station in Lucknow has been forced to halt most of its operations due to a shortage of commercial gas cylinders. Since March 3, the restaurant has not received any gas supply, leaving most of its kitchen stoves non-functional. Only coal-fired furnaces and tandoors are currently in use, severely limiting food preparation. Limited menu, reduced workforce With only coal-based cooking available, the restaurant is now serving a restricted menu. As a result, half of its staff has been asked to take leave. Out of 14 employees, only 7 are currently working. Head chef Vijay Kashyap said that operations have been severely impacted over the past 10 days, making it difficult to prepare meals efficiently. Daily losses of ₹20,000 Restaurant manager Vimlesh stated that the lack of gas supply has led to significant financial losses, estimated at around ₹20,000 per day. “If we don’t receive gas cylinders soon, we may have no option but to shut down the restaurant completely,” he said, adding that all gas stoves remain idle. Customers turning away disappointed Once a bustling spot, especially during nighttime with heavy footfall from passengers and locals, the restaurant is now witnessing a sharp decline in customers. Most menu items are unavailable, leading to disappointed customers returning without dining. The limited food options from tandoor and coal furnaces have also affected the restaurant’s reputation and customer trust. Livelihoods at risk The crisis has extended beyond business losses, impacting the livelihoods of employees and their families. Chef Vijay Kashyap highlighted that many workers depended solely on this job for their income. With reduced operations and staff cuts, their financial stability is now at risk. Customers are returning disappointed Earlier, the restaurant was always crowded with customers. Especially at night, it was a gathering place for travelers and locals. Now the situation has changed. Most of the menu items are not available, causing customers to return disappointed. Due to limited food being prepared in the tandoor-oven, both the identity and trust of the restaurant are being affected. Uncertain future The management fears that if gas supply is not restored soon, the rail coach restaurant may have to shut down temporarily. With expenses continuing despite declining revenue, the key question remains: how long can the business sustain these losses?
