stories.title: ‘How is Atiq shown linked to ISI in Dhurandhar’:Former UP MP angry, Imran Masood calls it a rubbish film
stories.summary: Controversy has erupted in UP over actor Ranveer Singh's film 'Dhurandhar: The Revenge', depicting Atiq Ahmed's character and demonetization as a masterstroke. Congress MP Imran Masood from Saharanpur called the film nonsense. He said, "Who will watch this film and who will believe it? Former SP MP ST Hasan said, "Intelligence agencies and the police have not yet revealed whether Atiq had any connection with the Pakistani intelligence agency ISI. In such a situation, what is shown in the film has no basis." Meanwhile, AIMIM leader Waris Pathan said that just like 'Kerala Story-1 and 2', Muslims have also been targeted in Dhurandhar. Films that spread hatred in society should be immediately banned. Now read, who said what- Imran Masood said - Demonetisation was not a masterstroke Imran Masood said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had broken the back of the country's economy by demonetisation, whereas in the film it has been shown as a masterstroke. Demonetisation was not a masterstroke, but a decision that harmed the country. He said that the decisions Rahul Gandhi had criticized are proving to be correct today. If glorification is to be done in films, then former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi should be shown and it should be told how she responded to US President Richard Nixon. Imran Masood stated that the government has run out of development issues, which is why politics of spreading hatred in society is being pursued. He questioned how long people would continue to be divided in the name of Hindu-Muslim. He alleged that Prime Minister Modi stands with folded hands before former US President Donald Trump to protect industrialists. ST Hasan said - Now films are being made for politics ST Hasan said that talks of Don Dawood Ibrahim's connection with ISI have been heard, but in the case of Atiq Ahmed, no Indian investigation agency has made any such revelation so far. An attempt is being made to run the film by creating controversy. He said - Today films are being made for politics. No positive message is being given to society. I think filmmakers take money from parties to spread hatred. Such films are being made to break the Hindu-Muslim fabric. Rajeev Rai said - Such films come only during elections SP MP from Ghosi, Rajeev Rai said - When it happened, he was not in our party, first thing. Secondly, the Bharatiya Janata Party has a propaganda machine, there is an advisor who keeps making movies about himself. He keeps making movies about his imaginary world. He can say anything to anyone, he can add any link. I would request him to make a movie where a brave person is shown apologizing, begging, taking a pension. Where the real character is shown informing. Where it is shown how in 1942 you were writing letters for the British with the Muslim League. This is the real truth, which is factually recorded in history. MP Rajeev Rai said - He has not seen the film, but whenever elections come, such films are deliberately released to influence the atmosphere. He alleged that the government indirectly supports such films. He also gave examples of films like 'Kashmir Files'. Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi said - The aim is to earn money by inciting controversy Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi Bareilvi, president of All India Muslim Jamaat, expressed displeasure over the film 'Dhurandhar 2'. He said - People in the film industry choose such subjects to earn money, which create controversy in society. That's why they add a Hindu-Muslim angle. Maulana Razvi said that their only aim now is to earn money, whereas earlier films were made to give a message to society, bring change and reform. Earlier, a film was made on 'Sambhal', and similarly, films like 'Udaipur Files', 'Kerala Story' and 'Pandit Ghuskhore' were also made in the same way. Why did the controversy arise? Actually, the film depicts the demonetization that took place in 2016. It also features a character 'Atif Ahmed' based on mafia don Atiq Ahmed. This character is played by Salim Siddiqui. Atif Ahmed's look, physique, mustache, and style are shown to be exactly similar to Atiq Ahmed. In the film, the character Atif Ahmed's connection with Pakistan's intelligence agency ISI is shown. He is depicted operating his entire criminal network even while being in jail. There is a dialogue in the film, "As long as Atif Ahmed is there, whether in jail or out... he will manage everything." According to the film, before the 2017 UP assembly elections, a large consignment of fake notes was to be brought to India from Pakistan through hawala. This character was given the responsibility of distributing money in the state, but the government gets wind of it. After this, demonetization is announced, and the entire plan is foiled. The film also features a scene of a mafia assassination. Additionally, a character based on former DGP Prashant Kumar has also been included. It shows the character, who has become the NSA, showing him Atiq's criminal profile.

stories.summary: UP New Permanent DGP: उत्तर प्रदेश को चार साल बाद स्थायी पुलिस महानिदेशक (DGP) मिलने वाला है। अभी तक राज्य में केवल कार्यवाहक DGP ही रहते आए हैं। अब योगी सरकार ने इस दिशा में कदम बढ़ा दिया है। राज्य सरकार ने केंद्र को जो प्रस्ताव भेजा है, उसमें IPS अधिकारी राजीव कृष्ण का नाम दूसरे स्थान पर है। संकेत मिल रहे हैं कि 1 अप्रैल से पहले ही उनका स्थायी DGP बनने का आदेश जारी हो सकता है। राजीव कृष्ण को 31 मई 2025 को कार्यवाहक DGP बनाया गया था। उन्होंने पूर्व DGP प्रशांत कुमार की जगह ली थी। वे उत्तर प्रदेश के लगातार पांचवें कार्यवाहक DGP हैं। इतने लंबे समय तक कोई स्थायी DGP न होने से कई सवाल उठते रहे हैं। अब राजीव कृष्ण को ही इस कुर्सी पर स्थायी रूप से बैठाया जा रहा है।

stories.title: Weather worsens in UP, hail hits Lucknow-Ayodhya:Heavy rain in 25 districts, storm in Kashi; 5 killed by lightning
stories.summary: The weather in UP has deteriorated. In Lucknow, sudden darkness enveloped at 10 AM on Friday. It rained with strong winds. Hail also fell in some areas. Ayodhya, Barabanki, Sitapur, and Siddharthnagar also experienced heavy rain with hail. Earlier, heavy rain occurred in Prayagraj and Mathura. A dust storm blew. Roads were waterlogged in many places. School children and people heading to offices were seen with raincoats and umbrellas. Intermittent rain occurred in more than 25 districts including Kanpur, Noida, Agra, Aligarh, and Meerut. In Kashi, there was a drizzle with a storm. People who set up shops on the ghats packed their belongings and returned. Meanwhile, 5 people, including 3 farmers, died due to lightning strikes in Prayagraj, Balrampur, Bahraich, and Mirzapur. Standing wheat crops fell in many places. Farmers say that unseasonal rain poses a threat of damage to mustard and potato crops as well. The Meteorological Department says that due to the activation of the Western Disturbance, the weather has changed across the entire state. The weather will remain bad for the next 2 days. Winds will blow at a speed of 40 km/h. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Singh said- Due to the Western Disturbance, there is a possibility of rain across the entire state. Its effect will start to decrease after 2 days. In the last 24 hours, winds blew at the fastest speed of 87 km/h in Mathura. The wind speed was recorded at 59 km/h in Noida, and 57 km/h in Agra and Bulandshahr. The highest rainfall was recorded in Baghpat and Bulandshahr, about 6 mm. Weather Pictures-

stories.title: Female patient raped at Saifai medical college:Staff member arrested, department head removed
stories.summary: A 40-year-old female patient was allegedly raped at Saifai Medical College in Etawah. She is mentally ill and had been admitted for nine months. The incident came to light during a routine medical examination, when she was found to be five months pregnant. The case caused a stir within the medical college. Prof. AK Mishra, Head of the Psychiatry Department, filed an FIR at Saifai police station on 18 March. Following preliminary investigation, police arrested cleaner Ravindra Kumar on 19 March. Administrative action taken by college The college management removed AK Mishra from his post. All staff of the psychiatry department were transferred to other departments. A three-member inquiry committee has been formed, and the administration has sought a report within 48 hours. A separate medical team has also been set up to monitor the condition of the victim. Police statement on the case Saifai CO Ramgopal Sharma said the victim has no family member present and had been admitted to the medical college on 24 June 2025, where she remained since. He said- ‘A sanitation worker sexually assaulted her. The accused has been arrested. CCTV footage has been sought from the medical college. Other ward staff and doctors are being questioned Accused employed through outsourcing University spokesperson Shivam Jha said Dr Arun Kumar Mishra informed the management about the matter through a letter on 18 March 2026. The allegation was against a sanitation worker employed through outsourcing. The matter was immediately handed over to the police. The management also took action against Dr Mishra, citing departmental negligence, and assigned additional charge to the Dean of Medicine. Inquiry committee and medical team formed Shivam Jha stated that a three-member inquiry committee was constituted on 19 March to ensure justice for the victim. The panel will investigate the role of department staff, security arrangements and any negligence. At the same time, considering the patient’s condition, the Chief Medical Superintendent formed a special medical team under the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology. The team will oversee all necessary tests and treatment related to the woman’s pregnancy and overall health. Report sought from authorities Information about the case was sent to the District Magistrate of Etawah on 19 March. A report has also been sought from the Internal Complaints Committee. The matter is being treated seriously at the administrative level and is under continuous monitoring. Police raise key questions Police are examining the possible involvement of other staff and officials and are seeking answers to several questions-

stories.title: Ganga Iftar row—Why SP and Congress are in support ?:Experts cite Muslim vote bank; Maulana says, 'throwing bones is wrong'
stories.summary: Fourteen young men in Varanasi organised a Roza Iftar party on a boat in the Ganga river, filmed a reel and shared it on social media. The video showed them eating biryani. Following a complaint by the BJP Yuva Morcha, police arrested all 14 and sent them to jail. The incident has since triggered a political controversy. Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress leader Imran Pratapgarhi supported the youths, questioning police action. Meanwhile, Muslim clerics from Bareilly, Varanasi and Saharanpur criticised the act, calling it inappropriate and against Islamic principles. Religious leaders criticise the act Maulana: Throwing bones into Ganga is wrong Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi Bareilvi, President of the All India Muslim Jamaat, said Islam promotes simplicity and discourages showmanship. He stated that charity and good deeds should be done discreetly. 'These boys lack understanding of Deen (religion),' he said. 'They held Iftar on the Ganga and allegedly threw bones into the river after eating biryani. This is completely wrong and unacceptable.' He added that such actions harm the sanctity of the Ganga and criticised political leaders supporting the act, saying they should seek guidance from religious scholars. Varanasi cleric: No place for such acts in Islam SM Yasin, Joint Secretary of Anjuman Intezamia Masajid in Varanasi, said Iftar is a purely religious act, not a picnic or outing. He stressed that Maghrib prayers are obligatory after Iftar. 'What have their families taught them?' he asked. ‘Such actions only bring disrepute to Islam.’ Alternate view: Police acted under pressure Maulana Sufiyan Nizami, spokesperson for Firangi Mahal, offered a contrasting view. He argued that the police acted under public pressure. 'In Varanasi, people consume alcohol on cruises, yet no action is taken because there is no protest,' he said. 'I am not in favour of filing an FIR. The police acted under pressure, which is not appropriate under the law.' He also referred to a previous controversy in Sambhal, alleging misuse of authority. Hindu religious leader reacts Ram Ratan Giri, secretary of Panchayati Akhara Shri Niranjani, condemned the incident, emphasising the sacred status of the Ganga. ‘We consider the Ganga as a mother. Is it now a place for Iftar parties? Should bones be thrown into it?’ he said. He also questioned why SP and Congress were supporting the youths, stating that political backing of such actions sends the wrong message. Political reactions intensify debate Akhilesh Yadav questions police action SP chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that the arrests were made to appease the government and create divisions. He pointed out that luxury cruise ships operating in Varanasi serve alcohol and discharge waste into the Ganga, asking what action had been taken against them. Imran Pratapgarhi slams police Congress Rajya Sabha MP Imran Pratapgarhi said the arrests were triggered by the objections of a 'small-time leader'. 'A group of youths was having Iftar on a boat when someone’s sentiments were hurt, leading to arrests,' he said. He accused Uttar Pradesh Police of being quick to act against Muslims while ignoring similar issues involving others. Expert views: Vote bank politics at play Call for collective criticism Senior journalist Samiratmaj Mishra said the facts, such as whether bones were actually thrown, should be established through investigation. However, he noted that holding an Iftar party on the Ganga would not be widely considered appropriate. 'Ganga is a symbol of religious faith. Political parties should have collectively criticised the act,' he said, adding that comparisons with sewage discharge or cruises are misplaced. ‘Appeasement Politics’ alleged Veteran journalist Alok Pathak described the political support as an example of 'Muslim appeasement'. He argued that when religious leaders themselves oppose the act, political backing becomes difficult to justify. He also maintained that pollution from sewage and deliberate disposal of food waste cannot be equated. Vote Bank considerations Senior journalist Harshvardhan said the reactions reflect electoral calculations. He argued that political parties aim to retain Muslim support, fearing voter shifts. According to him, both SP and Congress seek to consolidate Muslim votes, with leaders like Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav viewing the community as a crucial electoral base. He added that while environmental concerns about the Ganga are widely acknowledged, actions perceived as disrespectful to religious sentiments draw sharper reactions. How the incident unfolded ? The incident took place in the Tadtalla area of Madanpura in Varanasi. Fourteen youths from the Babu Bidi family planned an Iftar party on the Ganga on 16 March. They boarded a boat at Assi Ghat, which travelled to Namo Ghat. During the gathering, they recorded a reel showing themselves eating chicken biryani and posted it on Instagram. The video sparked controversy. BJP Yuva Morcha metropolitan president Rajat Jaiswal filed a police complaint, alleging that the youths threw chicken bones into the river after eating. A case was registered at Kotwali police station, and all 14 were arrested. Court proceedings and jail The accused were presented in court at around 8 pm on 19 March. Kashi Police told the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) court that the youths had effectively hijacked the boat and coerced the boatman to conduct the Iftar on the river. They also cited the making and sharing of videos as evidence of deliberate conduct. The families filed bail applications, but the court rejected all pleas. The youths have been remanded to 14 days in judicial custody, with the next bail hearing scheduled for 1 April. During the hearing, five of the accused reportedly broke down in court. With their custody extending through the festive period, they are set to spend Eid in jail.

stories.title: BSc student shot dead in Varanasi:4 shots fired; accused threw pistol in garbage and fled
stories.summary: A BSc student was shot dead in broad daylight inside the campus of Uday Pratap College in Varanasi. The attacker fired four rounds at the student outside a classroom, causing him to collapse in a pool of blood. A friend of the victim said they rushed to the spot after hearing the gunshots. The accused allegedly pointed a pistol at them as well before fleeing. He is said to have discarded the weapon in a heap of rubbish while escaping. Victim taken to hospital, declared dead Following the incident, chaos gripped the college. Teachers and students gathered at the scene as the injured student was rushed to the BHU Trauma Centre. Doctors there declared him dead on arrival. The shooting took place on Friday afternoon outside the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences. Violence and vandalism on campus After the killing, students staged protests that quickly turned violent. Acts of vandalism were reported within the campus, and shops outside the college were also targeted. Police responded by shutting the college gates and ordering the closure of more than 150 shops in the surrounding area. A heavy police deployment, including personnel from seven police stations, has been stationed inside the campus to maintain order. Victim and accused identified The deceased has been identified as 23-year-old Surya Pratap Singh, a resident of Ghazipur. The accused, Manjeet, is a second-year BA student reportedly from the Chandmari area of Varanasi. The reason behind the attack remains unknown, and police investigations are ongoing. See 4 pictures-

stories.title: Bangkok return man's nude body found on terrace in Gorakhpur:Clothes found hanging 25 metres away on tree; mother alleges murder, demands probe
stories.summary: A 28-year-old man’s nude body was discovered on the roof of a toilet in Gorakhpur. His jeans and T-shirt were found hanging from a tree 25 metres away. His mother alleges murder and demands that those responsible be hanged. According to police, Rishabh Yadav worked in Bangkok, the capital of Thailand. He had returned home on 19 February for his sister’s wedding. His body was found on Thursday morning. A condom was in his hand, and there were scratch marks on his stomach. No other injury marks were found. The incident occurred within the Gagaha police station area. SSP Dr Kaustubh said- The post-mortem will be conducted today. Further action will follow based on the report. No written complaint has been filed by the family so far.’ Family’s reaction and discovery of body Rishabh’s father, Rajendra Yadav, runs a flour mill 20 metres from the Gorakhpur–Varanasi highway. On Thursday morning, he reached the mill and saw a body on the roof of the toilet behind it. He informed the police, who arrived with a forensic team. The body was sent to BRD Medical College. On receiving the news, the mother and wife rushed to the scene. The mother fainted while crying. His wife said tearfully, 'My husband was murdered and his body was dumped. Strict action must be taken against those responsible.' Family background Rishabh was from Rawatpar and worked in Bangkok with his father, Uday Chand Yadav. He married Chandni seven years ago and had two sons, aged six years and two-and-a-half years. He had two brothers and two sisters. His mother, Guddi Devi, said he had come from Bangkok for his younger sister’s wedding on 19 February. Ten days after the wedding, his father returned to Bangkok, but Rishabh remained in Gorakhpur.

stories.title: President Murmu meets Premanand Maharaj in Mathura:Arrives with family at ashram, holds 25-min spiritual discussion
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu met Premanand Maharaj in Mathura, where they held a spiritual discussion for 25 minutes. The President arrived at Premanandji’s ashram with her family at 7 am on Friday amid rain and greeted him with folded hands. Premanandji responded with ‘Radhe-Radhe’. The President was welcomed by ashram volunteers with garlands and a ceremonial scarf. She also wished him on his birthday, which was on Thursday. 3-day Uttar Pradesh visit The President is on a three-day visit to Uttar Pradesh. On the second day, she is scheduled to visit the ashram of Neem Karoli Baba and offer prayers to Hanuman ji. She will then visit the Ramakrishna Mission Hospital to inaugurate Western Uttar Pradesh’s most modern cancer unit. This is her second visit to Mathura; she had previously visited on 25 September last year. See 3 pictures- Warm reception at Ashram The President was received by the ashram’s attendants with garlands and stoles. Chairs were arranged for her and her family at Kelikunj Ashram. She was accompanied by her daughter Itishree Murmu, son-in-law Ganesh Hembram, and granddaughters Adyashree and Nityashree. Emotional spiritual interaction During the spiritual discussion with Premanand Maharaj, the President reportedly became emotional. The interaction took place privately inside a hut, attended only by the President, her family, and Premanand’s close disciples. Visit to Ayodhya and Ram Temple On the first day of her visit, the President offered prayers to Ramlala in Ayodhya. She installed the Ram Yantra in the Ram Darbar on the second floor and toured the temple complex. Yogi Adityanath briefed her on the ongoing construction work related to the temple. The President said that Lord Shri Ram was born in Ayodhya and described it as a matter of great fortune to set foot on the sacred land. ISKCON and Prem Mandir visits In the evening, she travelled from Ayodhya to Mathura and visited the ISKCON temple, where she offered prayers to Radha-Shyam Sundar. She praised the temple’s decoration and interacted with children, distributing chocolates. After spending about half an hour at ISKCON, she proceeded to Prem Mandir to offer prayers.

stories.title: CMO office manager held in bribery trap in UP:Vigilance raid catches official taking ₹2 lakh in Mahoba; breaks down during arrest
stories.summary: In Mahoba, a vigilance team dragged away the Health Department’s Family Planning Logistic Manager. He had demanded a bribe of ₹3.5 lakh from a contractual employee. Yesterday he had called the employee to a hotel to take the first instalment of ₹2 lakh, where he was caught red-handed. He broke down in tears and kept shaking his hands and legs in an attempt to free himself. The man apologised to the vigilance officers and pleaded, “Sir, I fold my hands, please let me go.” The officers detained him forcefully and said, “Take him away. Put him in the vehicle.” The manager tried with all his strength to escape from the team’s grip. One team member held his belt while another dragged him towards the Bolero vehicle. See 3 pictures... Now read the complete sequence of events... Allegation - CMO had asked to meet the manager Meraj Mohammad from Hamirpur is an account manager at Panwadi Community Health Center in Mahoba. He said, “I had asked the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) for transfer or adjustment to Kabrai Community Health Center. The CMO said, go meet Jitesh. Jitesh is the Family Planning Logistics Manager. He is also a contract employee and has a clerk-like position”. He added, “When I met Jitesh, he said, give ₹3.5 lakh, your work will be done. I complained about this to the Jhansi Vigilance officers. Vigilance planned to catch accused Jitesh red-handed”. Manager called employee to hotel basement He added, “On Thursday, I called Jitesh and said the money has been arranged. Where should I give it? To this, Jitesh called me to a hotel basement about 5 km away from the CMO office”. After reaching the hotel, as soon as he gave ₹2 lakh to the manager, the team deployed in plain clothes caught him on the spot. When the accused's hands were washed, they turned pink due to the effect of the chemical, confirming the acceptance of the bribe. After arrest, the accused was brought to the city police station. Where he is being intensively interrogated in a closed room. In this case, CMO Asaram has given clarification. He said, “Meraj's allegations are baseless. Meraj was pressuring me to forcefully transfer him”. He added, “I have not had any conversation with Meraj for the past one and a half years. He had come to my residence and misbehaved. Since then I have not talked to him. He was transferred only due to irregularities found in his work. The person from whom Meraj is alleging to have demanded a bribe, his work is related to logistics.” Vigilance team in-charge said - Preparing to send accused to jail Meanwhile, Vigilance team in-charge Piyush Pandey said, “A case has been registered against the accused under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Preparations are being made to send him to jail. Investigation is also being done about who else could be involved in this case”.

stories.title: UP permanent DGP proposal returned by UPSC:3 months to resubmit; Rajeev Krishna topped in earlier list
stories.summary: The proposal for appointing a permanent DGP in Uttar Pradesh has been stalled for now. The UPSC has raised objections and returned the proposal to the Chief Secretary. The Commission said a fresh proposal should be prepared in line with the 2025 guidelines and Supreme Court rulings, and resubmitted. A three-month window has been given for this. In the earlier proposal, Rajeev Krishna was widely expected to be appointed as the permanent DGP. He was made acting DGP of Uttar Pradesh on 31 May 2025, replacing Prashant Kumar. He is the fifth consecutive acting DGP in the state. Renuka Mishra removed from the race Senior IPS officer Renuka Mishra, once a strong contender, has been excluded from the DGP race. The Uttar Pradesh government held her responsible for lapses linked to the 2024 police recruitment paper leak. Mishra served as Chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board from 14 February 2023 to 5 March 2024. During her tenure, the constable recruitment examination paper was leaked on 24 February, leading to the cancellation of the test. Investigations revealed that a blacklisted firm had been entrusted with printing the question papers. Following this, Mishra was removed from her position and placed on a waiting list. In its communication to the UPSC, the state government stated that the irregularities rendered her unsuitable for appointment as DGP. Why was Alok Sharma not considered ? The state government also excluded Alok Sharma, currently serving in the Special Protection Group on central deputation. Sources indicate that 5 February 2026 was treated as the official vacancy date for the DGP post, following a directive from the Supreme Court to appoint a permanent DGP. As per UPSC norms, only officers with at least six months of remaining service are eligible. Sharma’s remaining tenure falls short of this requirement, leading to his exclusion. Likely panel for DGP appointment With Mishra and Sharma out of contention, the panel expected to be considered by the UPSC includes- Additionally, the state has forwarded a broader list of officers up to the 1994 batch. These include Ashutosh Pandey and Anand Swaroop (1992 batch); Sanjay Singhal, SB Shiradkar, Zaki Ahmed, KS Pratap Kumar, Rajiv Sabharwal and Vitul Kumar (1993 batch); and BK Singh, Akhil Kumar, Raja Srivastava, DK Thakur, Sujit Pandey, Prakash D and Jai Narayan Singh (1994 batch). Proposal returned by UPSC A proposal for appointing the permanent DGP, sent by Chief Secretary SP Goyal, was returned by the UPSC due to technical discrepancies. The primary issue was that the proposal had been submitted in an outdated format rather than the revised one mandated by the आयोग. 4 years without a permanent DGP Uttar Pradesh has not had a full-time DGP since Mukul Goel was removed on 11 May 2022. Since then, a series of acting DGPs have held the position- Krishna, a 1991 batch IPS officer, is currently set to serve until June 2029. A Technocrat image and policing innovations Rajiv Krishna is regarded as a technocrat within the police force. As Additional Director General (ADG), he developed the ‘Operation Pehchan’ application, aimed at tracking criminals. He also integrated digital monitoring systems for the Women Beat programme and Anti-Romeo Squads. His initiatives include the introduction of e-Malkhana (digital evidence storage), digitisation of case records and focused campaigns against cybercrime. During his tenure as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) in Agra, he led effective operations against kidnapping gangs operating in ravine areas. Career trajectory and postings After joining the IPS in 1991, Krishna began his career as a trainee in Allahabad (now Prayagraj). He later served as Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) in Bareilly, Kanpur and Aligarh. On 10 March 1997, he became Superintendent of Police (SP) of Firozabad. He subsequently served as SSP in multiple districts, including Etawah, Mathura, Fatehgarh, Bulandshahr, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Agra, Lucknow and Bareilly. During administrative restructuring under Mayawati’s government, he was appointed DIG of Lucknow. He later served as IG of Meerut Range and went on central deputation in 2012, returning in 2017. Strong family background in public service Krishna comes from a family with a long-standing presence in civil services and politics. His wife, Meenakshi Singh, serves as Deputy Secretary in the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) in Noida. His brother-in-law, Rajeshwar Singh, is currently an MLA from Sarojini Nagar in Lucknow and a former IPS officer who later joined the Enforcement Directorate. Rajeshwar’s wife, Lakshmi Singh, is the Police Commissioner of Gautam Buddh Nagar. Krishna’s father-in-law also served as a Deputy Inspector General of Police. With the administrative process nearing completion, Uttar Pradesh appears set to end its prolonged reliance on acting DGPs, marking a significant shift in its policing leadership structure.

stories.title: Kaila devi pilgrimage turns fatal for a family in UP:Five devotees including father and son die in road accident; 3 injured
stories.summary: A pilgrimage tour turned fatal for a family as a Bolero full of devotees crashed into a tree in Agra killing 5 people. The deceased include husband, son, daughter-in-law grand daughter. Meanwhile three people were injured in this incident. After the accident, villagers broke the car windows and pulled everyone out. The family from Etawah had gone to Rajasthan's Kaila Devi temple for darshan on the first day of Navratri. The accident occurred in Chitrahaat police station area while they were returning late at night. See 2 pictures of the accident…. Villagers broke the car windows to rescue people Eight people from the same family had gone to Rajasthan on Wednesday to have darshan of Kaila Devi in a Bolero car. While returning, around 11 PM on Thursday night, the speeding Bolero car crashed into a tree on the roadside near Pai village area. Hearing the sound of a loud explosion and cries of the injured, nearby villagers came running. The villagers broke the car windows to rescue people trapped inside. Meanwhile, the locals also informed the police about the incident. Police and villagers sent the injured to the local CHC. There, the doctor declared 70-year-old Kanta Prasad, his son Devendra (35), his 3-year-old granddaughter Aradhya, his daughter-in-law Seema (30), and 20-year-old driver Rishi dead. Driver dozed off resulting in the accident In the accident, three people sustained injuries. After first aid, they were referred to the hospital at Saifai Medical College. According to the villagers the collision was so severe that the car doors got stuck and they had no options but to break the windows. Inspector Chittrahat Seema said, “Prima facie the accident occurred due to the driver dozing off. Upon receiving information, the deceased's family members reached the hospital. There were cries and screams upon seeing the bodies. Everyone was in a terrible state, crying continuously. Police have sent the bodies to Bah CHC for post-mortem”.

This discovery pushes back the timeline of human history in the Arabian Peninsula, demonstrating a thriving desert society with long-term occupation and extensive trade networks, challenging previous notions of the region's marginal role in early human development.

'Unconstitutional': SC rules adoptive mothers can't be denied maternity leave if child is older than 3 months
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has struck down a provision in the Social Security Code 2020 that limited maternity leave for adoptive mothers. The court declared the provision irrational, stating adoptive children are no different from biological ones. Consequently, adoptive mothers are now entitled to 12 weeks of maternity leave, irrespective of the child's age at adoption.

stories.title: Trump Shocked By Iran Strikes: intel had warned of Gulf retaliation; markets fear wider conflict
stories.summary: US President Trump expressed shock at Iran's expanded strikes across the Middle East, despite US intelligence anticipating such retaliation. The conflict, now in its third week, has seen Iranian attacks on US positions and allied infrastructure, disrupting vital shipping lanes like the Strait of Hormuz. Concerns are mounting over the war's justification and its escalating regional impact.

India’s mental health helpline flooded: 34 lakh calls signal rising anxiety crisis
stories.summary: India's national mental health helpline, Tele-MANAS, has received over 34.34 lakh calls since its October 2022 launch, indicating a significant rise in demand for psychological support. Uttar Pradesh leads in call volume, with other states like Tamil Nadu and Karnataka also showing high engagement.

stories.title: Trump Slams Reluctant Allies: key partners reject Hormuz naval push; rifts widen as war escalates
stories.summary: US President Trump expressed disappointment as key allies like Germany and Italy refused to send warships to the Strait of Hormuz. Citing legal limits and lack of mandates, these nations declined. Trump, however, asserted US strength, suggesting the request was partly a test of allied commitment amid escalating regional conflict and Iran's closure of the vital waterway.

stories.title: Iran war impact: Sri Lanka shifts to 4-day week to conserve fuel
stories.summary: Sri Lanka has declared Wednesdays a public holiday to conserve fuel amid escalating Middle East tensions impacting global oil supplies. This move, alongside similar measures in other Asian nations like Thailand and Myanmar, aims to mitigate potential shortages. Motorists in Sri Lanka now face fuel rationing, a stark reminder of past economic struggles.

Where is Iran’s new supreme leader? How Mojtaba Khamenei escaped the ‘Blue Sparrow’ strike that killed his father
stories.summary: Iran's new supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, narrowly survived a deadly airstrike that targeted his family and top officials. Audio reveals Mojtaba was outside his father's compound when Israeli missiles struck, killing his wife and son. The attack also claimed the lives of Ayatollah Khamenei and other senior leaders.

NMC fines 7 medical colleges Rs 1 crore each for not disclosing intern stipends
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has fined seven medical colleges ₹1 crore each for failing to disclose stipend details for interns and residents. This action follows repeated directives and court orders mandating transparency in payments. The NMC warned of further disciplinary measures for continued non-compliance.

stories.title: FSSAI asks milk vendors to register, launches drive to curb adulteration
stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has mandated registration or licenses for all independent milk producers and vendors nationwide. This directive aims to bring unregistered sellers into the food safety regulatory system, addressing concerns over milk adulteration and ensuring better traceability and safety for consumers.

stories.title: 'Principles of Dravidian ideology and Islam are fundamentally the same': Udhayanidhi Stalin
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu deputy chief minister Udhayanidhi Stalin, who aslo happens to be the son of chief minister MK Stalin, said no "conspiracies" can break the relationship between the urling DMK and the Muslim coummunity. "As long as brotherhood and unity exist, no matter how many attempts or conspiracies take place, no one will be able to break the relationship between the DMK and the Muslim community," said Stalin, who is DMK's heir apparent.

stories.title: Pakistan airstrike on Afghanistan: 400 killed after Kabul drug rehab centre hit; Pak says military infra targeted — 10 things to know
stories.summary: Pakistan airstrikes have struck a drug rehabilitation hospital in Kabul, Afghanistan. Hundreds have died and many more are injured. Afghan officials accuse Pakistan of deliberately targeting civilians. Pakistan denies this, stating strikes hit militant infrastructure. Cross-border clashes continue, raising regional security concerns. Both nations present conflicting casualty figures.

Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish highlighted atrocities in India's western neighborhood, criticizing fabricated Islamophobia claims and brutal repression of minorities. He asserted that Muslims in India have elected representatives and enjoy peaceful coexistence.

This observance blends deep religious devotion with unique cultural traditions, showcasing the monarchy's role in preserving faith and heritage. Dignitaries attended, underscoring Morocco's ties with Muslim nations.

stories.summary: Muslims in the UAE and Saudi Arabia are observing Laylat ul-Qadr, the holiest night in Islam. Thousands are gathering in mosques for special prayers and reflection. This sacred night occurs during the final ten days of Ramadan. Believers seek forgiveness of God and blessings. Preparations for Eid al-Fitr are also underway as Ramadan concludes.

stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has called upon Muslims to sight the Shawwal crescent moon on Wednesday evening, March 18, 2026, to determine the start of Eid Al Fitr. This sighting dictates the end of Ramadan and the beginning of the festival. Many global Muslim communities await Saudi Arabia's announcement, though South Asian nations may observe a day later based on local moon sightings.

stories.title: Pakistan launches strikes on Afghanistan; Taliban says civilians killed in hospital attack
stories.summary: Afghanistan accused Pakistan of killing civilians in fresh airstrikes on Kabul, alleging a hospital treating drug addicts was hit. Pakistan denied targeting civilians, stating precision strikes hit military and "terrorist" targets used against Pakistan. Tensions escalate amid ongoing border clashes and accusations of sheltering militants.

stories.title: Dubai, Doha travel alert: Oman Air cancels flights to 9 cities until March 31 amid airspace disruptions due to Iran vs US-Israel war
stories.summary: Oman Air has extended flight suspensions to nine international destinations until March 31 due to ongoing Middle East airspace restrictions. The airline cited evolving security situations and flight safety as reasons for the cancellations, impacting major hubs like Dubai and Doha. Passengers are advised to check bookings as disruptions continue to affect regional and global travel networks.

The airline is gradually restoring its schedule after safety checks, highlighting its operational resilience and Dubai's crucial role as a global aviation hub.

Other Indian carriers also face potential schedule changes as the region's vital air corridors remain under strain, causing passenger confusion and delays.

stories.summary: YouTuber Brandon Buckingham recounted a harrowing experience where he was attacked and robbed, resorting to shooting his assailant multiple times in self-defense. Despite ongoing health issues from a previous illness, Buckingham shared the incident to update followers on a dangerous real-life encounter outside his usual travel filming. He showed a handgun and a bandage, confirming he was injured but okay.

stories.title: RaKai finally addresses Twitch 30 day ban as LaMelo Ball connection raises questions about possible permanent suspension
stories.summary: Streamer RaKai said Twitch suspended his channel for 30 days after he showed private messages from Charlotte Hornets guard LaMelo Ball during a livestream. The messages included a phone number, which Twitch classified as sharing personal information. RaKai revealed the platform warned him that another similar violation would lead to a permanent ban.

While the UAE has strong air defences, this rare event highlights the unpredictable reach of regional hostilities into civilian areas. Authorities are investigating and urging public caution.
